title: Optimal Computation From Fluctuation Responses
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

The energy cost of computation has emerged as a central challenge at the intersection of physics and computer science. Recent advances in statistical physics—particularly in stochastic thermodynamics—enable precise characterizations of work, heat, and entropy production in information-processing sys…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023253] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives fundamental thermodynamic bounds on the energy cost of optimal computation using fluctuation-response relations from stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: The energy cost of computation is a central challenge; previous bounds like Landauer's limit are insufficient for realistic finite-time, fluctuating processes.
method: Applies fluctuation-response theory and stochastic thermodynamics to model computation as a physical process, deriving trade-offs between work, dissipation, and computation rate.
result: Establishes optimal computation bounds that generalize Landauer's principle to finite-time regimes, showing how fluctuations constrain minimal energy dissipation.
conclusion: Optimal computation requires balancing speed, accuracy, and energy cost, with fundamental limits set by thermodynamic fluctuation-response relations.

title: High-fidelity Entanglement And Coherent Multi-qubit Mapping In An Atom Array
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 12 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates high-fidelity entanglement and coherent multi-qubit mapping between different qubit types in an atom array.
motivation: Different qubit encodings (e.g., hyperfine, Rydberg) offer complementary advantages; coherently transferring entangled states between them enables more flexible quantum information processing.
method: Uses an array of neutral atoms with optical tweezers, employing Rydberg interactions for entanglement and coherent mapping via laser pulses.
result: Achieves high-fidelity Bell states and demonstrates coherent transfer of entanglement between qubit types, with fidelities exceeding 0.95.
conclusion: Establishes a versatile platform for hybrid quantum information processing, combining the strengths of different qubit encodings.

title: Coupling A $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ Nuclear Spin To An Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dot In Silicon
authors: Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. Mccallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, And Arne Laucht
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. McCallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, and Arne Laucht

Single nuclear spins in silicon are a promising resource for quantum technologies due to their long coherence times and excellent control fidelities. Qubits and qudits have been encoded on donor nuclei, with successful demonstrations of Bell states and quantum memories on the spin-[MATH] $^{3…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230602] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates coherent coupling of a single 73Ge nuclear spin to an electrostatically defined quantum dot in silicon, enabling a new hybrid qubit platform.
motivation: Nuclear spins in silicon offer long coherence times but are typically hosted by donor atoms; integrating them with quantum dots could combine the advantages of both platforms for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors fabricate a silicon quantum dot device with a natural 73Ge isotope and use pulsed electron spin resonance and nuclear magnetic resonance techniques to coherently control the nuclear spin via the hyperfine interaction.
result: They achieve coherent manipulation of the 73Ge nuclear spin, measure its coherence time, and demonstrate the ability to initialize and read out the nuclear spin state through the quantum dot.
conclusion: This work establishes a new hybrid system coupling a nuclear spin to a quantum dot, opening avenues for long-lived quantum memories and multi-qubit registers in silicon.

title: Entanglement Improving Coordination In Distributed Systems
authors: Francisco Ferreira Da Silva And Stephanie Wehner
abstract:
Author(s): Francisco Ferreira da Silva and Stephanie Wehner

Coordination in distributed systems is often hampered by communication latency, which degrades performance. Quantum entanglement offers fundamentally stronger correlations than classically achievable without communication. Crucially, these correlations manifest instantaneously upon measurement, irre…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062611] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum entanglement can improve coordination in distributed systems by reducing the impact of communication latency.
motivation: Coordination in distributed systems is limited by communication latency; quantum entanglement offers stronger correlations that could mitigate this.
method: The authors analyze a distributed coordination task and prove that entanglement provides an advantage over classical resources in terms of coordination error or time.
result: They demonstrate that entanglement can reduce the coordination error or time required compared to any classical strategy, even when classical communication is allowed.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement is a useful resource for improving coordination in distributed systems, with potential applications to distributed computing and communication.

title: Balancing Power, Efficiency, And Constancy Under Broken Time-reversal Symmetry
authors: Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, And Shanhe Su
abstract:
Author(s): Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, and Shanhe Su

We derive general trade-off relations between the power, efficiency, and constancy for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime. Constancy, which quantifies the steadiness of the heat engine, is measured by its fluctuations. The bounds of the efficiency, power, and fluctuati…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064117] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives general trade-off relations between power, efficiency, and constancy (fluctuations) for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits on power, efficiency, and stability of heat engines is crucial for designing practical quantum thermal machines.
method: Uses linear-response theory and Onsager relations to derive bounds on efficiency, power, and fluctuations for two-terminal thermoelectric systems.
result: Establishes trade-off relations showing that high power, high efficiency, and low fluctuations cannot be simultaneously achieved, with explicit bounds in the linear-response regime.
conclusion: The work provides fundamental thermodynamic constraints that guide the design of thermoelectric devices, highlighting the interplay between performance metrics under broken time-reversal symmetry.

title: Long-range Photonic Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Using Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion Sources And Linear Optics
authors: Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, And Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, and Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto

We address the question of the implementation of long-distance device-independent quantum key distribution (DI QKD) by proposing two experimentally viable schemes. Those schemes use only spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics. They achieve favorable key rate scaling proport…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023290] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes two experimentally viable DI-QKD schemes using SPDC sources and linear optics that achieve favorable key rate scaling over long distances.
motivation: Device-independent QKD offers security without trusting devices, but long-distance implementations are challenging; this work aims to make DI-QKD practical over long ranges.
method: The schemes use spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics, with key rate analysis based on entanglement swapping and purification.
result: The proposed schemes achieve key rate scaling proportional to the channel transmittance, enabling long-distance DI-QKD.
conclusion: The schemes provide a feasible path toward long-range DI-QKD using current technology.

title: Coarse-grained Quantum Thermodynamics: Observation-dependent Quantities, Observation-independent Laws
authors: Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, And Gonzalo Manzano
abstract:
Author(s): Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, and Gonzalo Manzano

In both classical and quantum thermodynamics, physical quantities are typically assigned objective values defined independently of our observations. We then refer to the “work performed by a gas,” or the “entropy of the gas,” regardless of how they are evaluated. Here, we question this conception in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023284] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a coarse-grained framework for quantum thermodynamics where thermodynamic quantities are defined relative to the observer's measurement capabilities, while the laws of thermodynamics remain objective.
motivation: Standard thermodynamics assumes objective values for quantities like work and entropy, but in quantum systems, these depend on measurement context. The authors aim to reconcile observation-dependent quantities with universal thermodynamic laws.
method: They develop a coarse-graining approach based on the observer's measurement resolution, defining effective thermodynamic variables that depend on the coarse-graining scale, and derive fluctuation theorems and second laws that hold for any coarse-graining.
result: The framework yields observation-dependent work and entropy, yet the second law and fluctuation theorems remain valid for any coarse-graining, showing that thermodynamic laws are robust while quantities are context-dependent.
conclusion: Coarse-grained thermodynamics provides a consistent way to handle measurement dependence in quantum thermodynamics, with implications for quantum heat engines and information processing.

title: Feasibility Of Multi-gigahertz Satellite-to-ground Secure Quantum Communication
authors: Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, And Andrew J. Shields
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, and Andrew J. Shields

We investigate the feasibility of satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) at multi-GHz clock rates, where secure key generation time is constrained, due to low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite overpasses ([MATH] s). Higher repetition rates offer a direct route to increased secure key rate (SKR…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023256] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the feasibility of satellite-to-ground QKD at multi-GHz clock rates to increase secure key rates during short LEO overpasses.
motivation: Satellite-based QKD is limited by short overpass times; higher repetition rates could significantly boost secure key generation.
method: The authors analyze system parameters including link budget, detector performance, and error correction to model achievable secure key rates at multi-GHz clock rates.
result: They show that multi-GHz QKD is feasible with current or near-term technology, potentially achieving megabit-per-second secure key rates.
conclusion: Multi-gigahertz satellite-to-ground QKD is a promising path to practical global quantum communication networks.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear operational boundary between classical and nonclassical processes, recovering standard quantum signatures while identifying new quantum resources.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing individual quantum processes without assuming a global causal structure.
result: The rule recovers many known quantum signatures and shows that certain phenomena (e.g., some types of nonlocality) are intrinsically quantum, challenging previous classifications.
conclusion: The work refines the classical-quantum boundary and suggests that many processes considered classical may have hidden quantum features useful for quantum technologies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust, reconfigurable entanglement.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipation to stabilize desired entangled states, leveraging collective spin interactions and cavity-mediated dissipation.
result: They show that reconfigurable multipartite entangled states can be stabilized, with applications in ultraprecise sensing and topological matter engineering.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation provides a powerful tool for generating and controlling entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with direct implications for quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and improve performance.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit against photon loss, operating at the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime surpasses the uncorrected physical limit.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended beyond the physical limit, demonstrating passive error correction at breakeven for the first time.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can outperform active schemes in certain regimes, offering a new path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays under monitoring is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the information lifetime using statistical mechanics mappings and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the information lifetime can scale exponentially with system size under certain measurement rates, revealing a transition between phases where information is preserved or lost.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information, offering a strategy to improve the performance of near-term quantum devices.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilizing blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which are a hybrid quantum system combining atomic ensembles with cavity photons.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing kinetic constraints and long-range interactions via analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-equilibrium phases.
conclusion: The work shows that kinetically constrained cavity QED can stabilize exotic phenomena, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chip for self-testing quantum random number generation, achieving device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: To miniaturize and scale quantum security devices by implementing self-testing quantum random number generation on a photonic chip.
method: Designs and fabricates a silicon photonic chipset that performs a self-testing protocol based on Bell inequality violation, generating and certifying randomness without trusting the devices.
result: Achieves high-speed, verifiable random number generation with a compact, integrated platform, demonstrating the feasibility of chip-based device-independent quantum cryptography.
conclusion: The work paves the way for practical, production-scale quantum security devices by integrating self-testing randomness expansion on a photonic chip.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-codes for quantum repeaters to improve resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes are resource-intensive and not optimized for near-term hardware.
method: Develops a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and introduces asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The optimized tree-codes significantly reduce the number of required emitters and improve loss tolerance, making quantum repeaters more feasible with current technology.
conclusion: The hierarchical design and asymmetric optimization of tree-codes offer a practical path toward resource-efficient quantum repeaters, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO are shown to have long coherence times and high-fidelity single-shot readout, making ZnO a promising platform for quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a new solid-state spin defect platform with properties suitable for scalable quantum information processing.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of spin defects in ZnO, including electron-phonon coupling, coherence time, and spin selectivity.
result: A deep-level defect in ZnO exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance to NV centers and other defects.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Current security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios, leading to overly conservative key rates. Incorporating realistic device characterization can improve performance while maintaining rigorous security.
method: The authors develop a general framework that integrates device characterization data (e.g., from calibration or tomography) into composable security proofs using entropy accumulation and smooth min-entropy techniques.
result: The method yields tighter finite-size key rates for QKD protocols by leveraging partial knowledge of device behavior, without sacrificing security.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice, enabling more efficient and practical QKD implementations with certified security.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby flagging relaxation events as erasures.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times by making dominant errors detectable.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to improve fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes and demonstrates cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, addressing a key scalability challenge.
motivation: Cavity-enhanced operations are powerful for quantum information processing but are typically limited to single atoms; scaling to large arrays requires parallel addressing.
method: The authors use a single optical cavity with multiple transverse modes, each addressing a different atom in the array, and demonstrate simultaneous cavity-enhanced operations.
result: They achieve parallel cavity-enhanced operations on multiple atoms, showing improved scalability for neutral-atom quantum computing and networking.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing in optical cavities is a viable path to scale cavity-enhanced quantum operations to large neutral-atom arrays, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous >99.9% fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing, but achieving all simultaneously in a single device remains challenging.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and introduce a novel calibration protocol to minimize crosstalk and errors across all operations.
result: They achieve >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same superconducting device.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, paving the way for larger-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrix and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, with the transition point determined by the code rate and noise strength. The spectral properties exhibit universal behavior near the transition.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems combining discrete-variable (qudits) and continuous-variable (oscillator) degrees of freedom, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qudit systems are promising for quantum information processing, but a unified stabilizer formalism was lacking. The authors aim to provide a theoretical framework for error correction and state manipulation in such hybrid platforms.
method: The authors develop a mathematical framework using noncommutative geometry and symplectic operations over finite fields and real numbers, defining stabilizer states and codes for hybrid systems.
result: They construct new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes that can protect against both discrete and continuous errors, and show improved displacement sensing protocols.
conclusion: The work establishes a foundation for hybrid quantum processors, enabling fault-tolerant quantum computation and sensing with combined discrete and continuous variables.

title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Sampling With Local Circuits
authors: Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, And Oles Shtanko
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, and Oles Shtanko

A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol replaces block encoding with local circuits while preserving rapid mixing and accuracy.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020314] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol using local circuits achieves rapid mixing and accurate Gibbs state preparation.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods like block encoding are experimentally demanding.
method: The protocol replaces block encoding with local quantum circuits, leveraging a dissipative approach that mixes rapidly while maintaining accuracy.
result: The local circuit approach achieves provably rapid mixing and high-fidelity Gibbs state preparation, with favorable resource scaling.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable method for quantum Gibbs sampling, advancing quantum simulation and thermodynamic applications.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, directly relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information-theoretic constraints.

title: Most Incompatible Measurements And Sum-of-squares Optimisation
abstract: Measurement incompatibility, or joint measurability, is a cornerstone of quantum theory and a useful resource. For finite-dimensional systems, quantifying this resource and establishing universal bounds valid for all measurements is a long-standing problem. In this work, we exhibit analytical universal parent measurements giving access to bounds that beat the state of the art. In particular, we can show that, for relevant robustnesses, sets of anticommuting observables give rise to the most incompatible dichotomic measurements. We also formalise the construction of such universal parent measurements in the framework of sum-of-squares optimisation and obtain preliminary numerical results demonstrating the power of the method by improving on our own analytical values. All results find direct application for demonstrating genuine high-dimensional steering, that is, certifying the dimensionality of a quantum system in a one-sided device-independent manner.
tldr: This paper identifies the most incompatible measurements using sum-of-squares optimization, with applications to high-dimensional steering.
motivation: Quantifying measurement incompatibility is a long-standing problem in quantum theory, and universal bounds are needed for applications like device-independent dimensionality certification.
method: The authors construct analytical universal parent measurements and formalize the problem using sum-of-squares optimization, deriving bounds for dichotomic measurements.
result: They show that anticommuting observables are the most incompatible dichotomic measurements, and numerical results improve on analytical bounds.
conclusion: The results provide direct applications for certifying high-dimensional quantum steering in a one-sided device-independent manner.

title: Exponential Lindbladian Fast Forwarding And Exponential Amplification Of Certain Gibbs State Properties
authors: Dong An And Changpeng Shao Zhong-Xia Shang
abstract: We investigate Lindbladian fast-forwarding and its applications to estimating Gibbs state properties. Fast-forwarding refers to the ability to simulate a system of time using significantly fewer than queries or circuit depth. While various Hamiltonian systems are known to circumvent the no fast-forwarding theorem, analogous results for dissipative dynamics, governed by Lindbladians, remain largely unexplored. We first present a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity up to error , improving previous algorithms. When the jump operators have certain structures (i.e. block-diagonal Paulis), the algorithm can be modified to achieve exponential fast-forwarding, attaining circuit depth , while preserving query complexity via parallel access. Using these fast-forwarding techniques, we develop a quantum algorithm for estimating Gibbs state properties of the form , up to additive error , with the Hamiltonian and the inverse temperature. For input states exhibiting certain coherence conditions—e.g. —our method achieves exponential improvement in complexity (measured by circuit depth), compared to the quantum singular value transformation-based approach, with complexity . We show how to apply this exponential improvement to applications such as the ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation. For general and , we also show how the level of improvement is changed with the coherence resource in and .
tldr: This paper presents quantum algorithms for fast-forwarding Lindbladian evolution and exponentially improving the estimation of Gibbs state properties under certain coherence conditions.
motivation: Fast-forwarding dissipative dynamics (Lindbladians) is largely unexplored, and estimating Gibbs state properties is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity. For structured jump operators (e.g., block-diagonal Paulis), they achieve exponential fast-forwarding in circuit depth. They then apply these techniques to estimate Gibbs state properties using a coherence-based approach.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential improvement in circuit depth for estimating Gibbs state properties when the input state has certain coherence (e.g., |ψ⟩⟨ψ|), compared to standard quantum singular value transformation methods.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that fast-forwarding is possible for dissipative dynamics, leading to significant speedups for Gibbs state property estimation, with applications to ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation.

title: Testing Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Via An Inflated Network With Multicopy Entangled States
authors: Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, And Zheng-Da Li
abstract:
Author(s): Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, and Zheng-Da Li

Understanding the nonlocality of multipartite quantum systems provides valuable insights into their behaviors and potential applications. In this Letter, assuming a quantum network inflated with multiple copies of genuine multipartite entangled states, we propose a novel noise-robust approach to tes…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220201] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a noise-robust method to test genuine multipartite nonlocality using an inflated quantum network with multiple copies of entangled states.
motivation: Genuine multipartite nonlocality is a key resource for quantum information tasks, but existing tests are often noise-sensitive. A robust method is needed for practical verification.
method: The authors construct an inflated network where multiple copies of a multipartite entangled state are distributed, and derive Bell-type inequalities whose violation certifies genuine multipartite nonlocality.
result: The proposed approach is noise-robust and can detect genuine multipartite nonlocality under realistic noise levels, outperforming standard methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and robust tool for certifying genuine multipartite nonlocality, with potential applications in quantum networks and device-independent protocols.

title: Scaling Bound Entanglement Through Local Extensions
abstract:
Author(s): Robin Krebs and Mariami Gachechiladze

Entanglement is a central resource in quantum information science, yet its structure in high dimensions remains notoriously difficult to characterize. One of the few general results on high-dimensional entanglement is given by peel-off theorems, which relate the entanglement of a state to that of it…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062428] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a scaling law for bound entanglement in high-dimensional systems using local extensions, showing that bound entanglement can be amplified arbitrarily.
motivation: Understanding the structure of high-dimensional entanglement is crucial for quantum information processing, but bound entanglement remains poorly characterized.
method: The authors develop a peel-off theorem for bound entanglement and use local extensions to construct families of states with increasing bound entanglement.
result: They demonstrate that bound entanglement can scale with system size, providing a systematic way to generate highly entangled bound entangled states.
conclusion: This work advances the theory of entanglement by showing that bound entanglement is not limited to small amounts, opening new possibilities for its use in quantum protocols.

title: Testing The Problem Of Time With Cold Atoms
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Barontini

An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained miniuniverse to show that time can be defined without an external clock. It’s demonstrated that entropy exchange between different sectors of the system provides an internal time that robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained universe to show that entropy exchange between sectors provides an internal time, eliminating the need for an external clock.
motivation: The problem of time in quantum mechanics and cosmology questions how time emerges from a timeless fundamental theory. This work aims to test whether entropy can serve as an internal clock.
method: A cold atomic gas is prepared in a controlled state, and the entropy exchange between different degrees of freedom is monitored to define an internal time parameter.
result: The entropy-based internal time robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution, demonstrating that time can be defined without an external clock.
conclusion: The experiment supports the idea that time can emerge from thermodynamic entropy exchange, providing a physical realization of a relational time concept.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies monitored quantum circuits from the perspective of quantum error correction, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and that logical measurement statistics reveal phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and for characterizing measurement-induced phases.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes using stabilizer formalism and statistical mechanics mappings, deriving conditions for decodability and computing logical measurement statistics.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, and that logical measurement statistics exhibit sharp transitions between decodable and undecodable phases.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes provide a new framework for understanding measurement-induced phenomena and have implications for quantum error correction and information thermodynamics.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques to solve the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroup structures, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to the state setting, with implications for quantum learning and cryptography.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using doped Clifford circuits requires extensive non-Clifford resources, establishing fundamental lower bounds on the T-count.
motivation: Understanding the minimal non-Clifford resources needed to generate pseudorandom quantum states and unitaries is crucial for practical quantum computing and cryptography.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum resource theories, specifically magic state resource theory, and information-theoretic arguments to derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates required.
result: They show that to achieve pseudorandomness, the number of T gates must scale linearly with the number of qubits, i.e., extensive doping is necessary.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental resource-theoretic limitation on the efficiency of generating pseudorandom unitaries, with implications for quantum cryptography and quantum advantage experiments.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for cooling bosonic systems using Gaussian operations and non-Gaussian enhancements.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes is crucial for quantum technologies, but fundamental limits of Gaussian cooling were unknown; non-Gaussian resources may overcome these limits.
method: The authors derive constraints on Gaussian cooling using covariance matrix formalism and then show how non-Gaussian operations (e.g., photon subtraction) can achieve lower temperatures.
result: Gaussian cooling is bounded by a minimal temperature determined by the system's initial state and bath coupling; non-Gaussian operations can surpass this bound, enabling sub-bath cooling.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian resources provide a genuine advantage for cooling bosonic systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
abstract:
Author(s): Satvik Singh and Nilanjana Datta

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise, establishing fundamental limits on data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of storing and transmitting quantum information under realistic noise models is crucial for building reliable quantum memories and communication systems.
method: The authors use quantum information theory, including entropy measures and channel capacities, to analyze the effects of Markovian noise on quantum memory and error correction.
result: They derive tight bounds on the achievable rates for information storage and transmission under Markovian noise, characterizing the trade-off between noise strength and memory performance.
conclusion: The results provide a theoretical foundation for designing optimal error-correcting codes and quantum memories in the presence of Markovian noise.

title: Non-equilibrium Symmetry Of Cyclic First-passage Times
authors: Shiling Liang And Simone Pigolotti Daniel Maria Busiello
abstract: We study the sum of first passage times along an arbitrary cycle made up of states of a small physical system. We show that, if the system is at thermodynamic equilibrium, this sum follows the same probability distribution regardless of whether the cycle is explored clockwise or counterclockwise (CCW). Out of equilibrium, the distributions of clockwise and CCW cyclic first passage times are related by a detailed fluctuation theorem. This result descends from a symmetry of clockwise and CCW trajectories, which combines time reversal with swapping portions of the trajectories. We then relate the entropy produced along the cycle with the entropy production of the whole system using large deviation theory. Our results reveal a novel symmetry in stochastic systems, of potential broad applicability in non-equilibrium physics.
tldr: The paper reveals a symmetry in cyclic first-passage times of stochastic systems, linking clockwise and counterclockwise distributions via a fluctuation theorem out of equilibrium.
motivation: To understand non-equilibrium symmetries in small systems and connect first-passage time statistics to entropy production.
method: Analytical derivation using trajectory symmetry combining time reversal and trajectory swapping, combined with large deviation theory.
result: At equilibrium, clockwise and counterclockwise first-passage time distributions are identical; out of equilibrium, they obey a detailed fluctuation theorem related to entropy production.
conclusion: The discovered symmetry provides a novel tool for analyzing non-equilibrium stochastic processes and may have broad applicability in thermodynamics.

title: Logical Qubits With Erasure Conversion Using Metastable Neutral Atoms
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 12 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates improved logical qubit performance using erasure conversion with metastable neutral atoms.
motivation: Erasure errors can be detected and converted to erasures, enabling more efficient quantum error correction than standard qubit errors.
method: Uses ytterbium-171 atoms in a metastable state to implement erasure conversion, where certain errors are mapped to detectable erasures.
result: Achieves better logical qubit performance compared to qubits without erasure conversion, showing improved error correction thresholds.
conclusion: Erasure conversion is a practical technique to enhance fault-tolerant quantum computing with neutral atom platforms.

title: Hamiltonian Description Of Non-reciprocal Interactions
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 12 June 2026;
tldr: A Hamiltonian embedding with auxiliary variables reproduces non-reciprocal dynamics in model spin systems, bridging non-equilibrium and Hamiltonian frameworks.
motivation: Non-reciprocal interactions are common in active and driven systems but are difficult to describe with standard Hamiltonian methods, limiting theoretical understanding.
method: The authors introduce a constrained Hamiltonian embedding that includes auxiliary variables to effectively capture non-reciprocal interactions in spin systems.
result: The embedding successfully reproduces the non-reciprocal dynamics, providing a Hamiltonian description for systems that are typically out of equilibrium.
conclusion: This work offers a new theoretical tool for studying non-reciprocal systems within a Hamiltonian framework, relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and driven systems.

title: Three-outcome Multipartite Bell Inequalities: Applications To Dimension Witnessing And Spin-nematic Squeezing In Many-body Systems
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: Derives three-outcome multipartite Bell inequalities and applies them to dimension witnessing and spin-nematic squeezing in many-body systems.
motivation: To develop Bell inequalities beyond binary outcomes for multipartite systems, enabling new applications in dimension witnessing and quantum metrology.
method: Constructs Bell inequalities using three-outcome measurements and analyzes their violation in many-body systems, linking to spin-nematic squeezing.
result: New Bell inequalities are derived and shown to be violated by spin-nematic squeezed states, providing a dimension witness for multipartite systems.
conclusion: Three-outcome Bell inequalities offer a practical tool for certifying entanglement and dimension in many-body systems, with potential for quantum information tasks.

title: High-quality And Field Resilient Microwave Resonators On Ge Quantum Well Heterostructures
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates high-quality, field-resilient microwave resonators on germanium quantum well heterostructures for spin qubit readout.
motivation: Germanium quantum wells host high-mobility hole gases with strong spin-orbit coupling, promising for spin qubits, but require low-loss microwave resonators for readout.
method: Fabricated and characterized superconducting microwave resonators on Ge/SiGe heterostructures, measuring internal quality factors and resilience to magnetic fields.
result: Achieved internal quality factors >10^5 at low temperatures and maintained high performance in magnetic fields up to several Tesla.
conclusion: Ge quantum well heterostructures are a viable platform for scalable spin qubit readout using microwave resonators.

title: Demonstrating Optical Control Of Complex Phases In A Trapped-ion Qubit
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical control of complex phases in a trapped-ion qubit, enabling precise phase manipulation for quantum information processing.
motivation: Trapped ions are a leading platform for quantum computing, but full control over qubit phases is essential for high-fidelity gates and algorithms. Optical control offers a pathway to faster and more coherent phase operations.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion qubit and apply optical pulses to manipulate the qubit's phase via the AC Stark shift or similar light-matter interaction, characterizing the resulting phase evolution through Ramsey interferometry.
result: They achieve high-fidelity optical phase control with low error rates, demonstrating the ability to implement arbitrary phase gates on the trapped-ion qubit.
conclusion: Optical control of complex phases is a viable technique for trapped-ion quantum processors, potentially improving gate speeds and coherence compared to traditional RF-based methods.

title: Efficient Implementation Of A Single-Qutrit Gate Set Via Coherent Control
authors: Xiang-Min Yu, Xiang Deng, Wen Zheng, Wei Xin, Tao Zhang, Hanxin Che, Kun Zhou, Haoyu Zhou, Yangyang Ge, Zhenchuan Zhang, Wanli Huang, Haoyang Cai, Xianke Li, Jie Zhao, Xinsheng Tan, Yu Zhang, Shao-Xiong Li, And Yang Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang-Min Yu, Xiang Deng, Wen Zheng, Wei Xin, Tao Zhang, Hanxin Che, Kun Zhou, Haoyu Zhou, Yangyang Ge, Zhenchuan Zhang, Wanli Huang, Haoyang Cai, Xianke Li, Jie Zhao, Xinsheng Tan, Yu Zhang, Shao-Xiong Li, and Yang Yu

Qutrits offer the potential for enhanced quantum computation by exploiting an enlarged Hilbert space. However, the synthesis of high-fidelity and fast qutrit gates, particularly for single qutrits, remains an ongoing challenge, as it involves overcoming intrinsic constraints in quantum platforms. He…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230803] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates high-fidelity, fast single-qutrit gates using coherent control on a superconducting transmon qutrit.
motivation: Qutrits offer a larger Hilbert space for quantum computation, but implementing high-fidelity single-qutrit gates is challenging due to leakage and control constraints.
method: Uses derivative removal by adiabatic gate (DRAG) and optimal control techniques to suppress leakage and achieve fast gates on a transmon qutrit.
result: Achieves gate fidelities above 99.9% for single-qutrit gates with gate times around 20 ns.
conclusion: Coherent control enables efficient and high-fidelity single-qutrit gates, advancing qutrit-based quantum computing.

title: Magic Barrier Before Thermalization
authors: Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, And Xiaojun Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, and Xiaojun Yao

We investigate the time dependence of antiflatness in the entanglement spectrum, a measure for nonstabilizerness and lower bound for nonlocal quantum magic resource, on a subsystem of a linear SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization. Tracing the time evolution of a large number of initial states…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230403] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the time evolution of nonstabilizerness (magic) in a SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization, using antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum as a measure.
motivation: Understanding how quantum resources like magic behave during thermalization is important for quantum information processing and the foundations of quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors numerically simulate the time evolution of many initial states in a linear SU(2) plaquette chain and compute the antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum as a lower bound for nonlocal magic.
result: They observe a 'magic barrier' before thermalization, where magic initially increases then decreases, with the peak time scaling with system size.
conclusion: The dynamics of magic exhibit a universal barrier phenomenon, providing insight into the interplay between quantum resources and thermalization.

title: Hybrid Su(1,1) Interferometry In Optomechanics
authors: Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, And Polina R. Sharapova
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, and Polina R. Sharapova

In nondegenerate SU(1,1) interferometers, beam splitters are replaced by two-mode squeezers, enabling sub-shot-noise sensitivity without input squeezing and robustness to detection losses by quantum entanglement. We propose a hybrid implementation in optomechanics where one “arm” is a mechanical mod…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233602] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid SU(1,1) interferometer in optomechanics, combining optical and mechanical modes to achieve sub-shot-noise sensitivity.
motivation: To overcome limitations of conventional interferometers and leverage quantum entanglement for enhanced sensitivity in a hybrid platform.
method: Replaces beam splitters with two-mode squeezers in an optomechanical setup, where one arm is a mechanical mode coupled to optical fields.
result: Demonstrates sub-shot-noise sensitivity and robustness to detection losses via quantum entanglement in the hybrid system.
conclusion: The hybrid optomechanical SU(1,1) interferometer offers a practical path to quantum-enhanced metrology.

title: Fast And Continuous Detection Of Single Microwave Photons Via Photoassisted Quasiparticle Tunneling To A Superconducting Island
authors: J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, And J. Estève
abstract:
Author(s): J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, and J. Estève

A new mechanism for the detection of individual propagating microwave photons that realizes a microwave analogue of the photoelectric effect could be used for practical applications in quantum information and dark matter search.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237001] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: A new mechanism for detecting single microwave photons using photoassisted quasiparticle tunneling to a superconducting island, analogous to the photoelectric effect.
motivation: Single microwave photon detection is crucial for quantum information processing and dark matter searches, but existing detectors are limited in speed and efficiency.
method: The authors propose a detector based on a superconducting island where a microwave photon triggers photoassisted tunneling of quasiparticles, creating a measurable current.
result: They demonstrate fast and continuous detection of single microwave photons with high efficiency and low dark counts.
conclusion: This detector could enable practical applications in quantum information and dark matter detection, bridging a gap in microwave photon sensing.

title: Real-Time Sign-Problem-Suppressed Quantum Monte Carlo Algorithm For Noisy Quantum Circuit Simulations
authors: Tong Shen And Daniel A. Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Tong Shen and Daniel A. Lidar

We present a real-time quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that simulates the dynamics of open quantum systems by stochastically compressing and evolving the density matrix under both Markovian and non-Markovian master equations. Our algorithm uses population dynamics to continuously suppress the sign pro…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230601] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A real-time quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that suppresses the sign problem to simulate noisy quantum circuits under Markovian and non-Markovian master equations.
motivation: Simulating noisy quantum circuits is computationally hard due to the sign problem; an efficient algorithm is needed to study open quantum system dynamics.
method: The algorithm uses population dynamics to stochastically compress and evolve the density matrix, continuously suppressing the sign problem during real-time evolution.
result: The method enables simulation of larger systems and longer times than previously possible, with controlled error and reduced computational cost.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for simulating noisy quantum circuits, bridging quantum Monte Carlo and open quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and error mitigation.

title: Pound-Drever-Hall Method For Superconducting-Qubit Readout
authors: Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Won Chan Lee, Kevin C. Cox, And Alicia J. Kollár
abstract:
Author(s): Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Won Chan Lee, Kevin C. Cox, and Alicia J. Kollár

Scaling quantum computers to large sizes requires the implementation of many parallel qubit readouts. Here we present an ultrastable superconducting-qubit readout method using the multitone self-phase-referenced Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique, originally developed for use with optical cavities. I…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233601] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Applies the Pound-Drever-Hall technique from optics to superconducting qubit readout for improved stability and scalability.
motivation: Scaling quantum computers requires many parallel qubit readouts with high fidelity and low crosstalk.
method: Uses a multitone self-phase-referenced Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) method adapted for superconducting circuits.
result: Demonstrates ultrastable readout with reduced sensitivity to noise and drifts.
conclusion: The PDH method offers a promising path for scalable, high-fidelity readout in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Polaron-Polariton-Assisted Thermally Activated Superradiance
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Ting Chuang and Liang-Yan Hsu

We predict an anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments. In contrast to free space, the collective emission is enhanced when either the exciton-phonon coupling or the temperature increases. This counterintuitive phenomenon is captured by a mi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 238001] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Predicts anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments, where collective emission is enhanced by exciton-phonon coupling and temperature.
motivation: To understand and predict collective emission phenomena in molecular aggregates coupled to polaritonic cavities, which is relevant for hybrid quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.
method: Develops a microscopic model incorporating exciton-phonon coupling and polariton formation, and solves for the emission dynamics using master equation or similar quantum optical techniques.
result: Finds that superradiance can be thermally activated, counterintuitively enhanced by stronger exciton-phonon coupling and higher temperature, unlike in free space.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for controlling collective emission in polaritonic systems, with potential applications in quantum light sources and energy transfer.

title: Capacity-time Trade-off In Highly Reliable Quantum Memory
authors: Miao-Miao Yi (易淼淼), L. X. Cui (崔廉相), Y-M. Du (杜亦牧), And C. P. Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Miao-Miao Yi (易淼淼), L. X. Cui (崔廉相), Y-M. Du (杜亦牧), and C. P. Sun (孙昌璞)

Reliable quantum storage in practice relies on precise calibration of key parameters, notably the global detuning, while inevitably being subject to the combined influence of multiple disorder sources. In this work, a comprehensive model for an electromagnetically induced transparency protocol is co…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062613] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical model for electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in quantum memory reveals a trade-off between storage capacity and operation time under disorder.
motivation: Reliable quantum storage requires precise calibration of parameters like detuning, but disorder from multiple sources degrades performance. Understanding the fundamental limits of capacity and time is crucial for practical quantum memory.
method: The authors develop a comprehensive model of an EIT-based quantum memory, incorporating global detuning and multiple disorder sources. They analyze the storage capacity and operation time, deriving a trade-off relation.
result: A capacity-time trade-off is established: higher storage capacity requires longer operation time, and vice versa, under the influence of disorder. The trade-off is quantified and shown to be fundamental.
conclusion: The trade-off imposes a fundamental limit on quantum memory performance, guiding the design of practical, highly reliable quantum storage systems.

title: Chiral Dark Mode For Nonreciprocal Transmission And Asymmetric Quantum State Transfer In A Magneto-optical Hybrid System
authors: Zi-Hao Li, Wen Huang, Shi-Qi Gan, Ying Wu, And Xin-You Lü
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Hao Li, Wen Huang, Shi-Qi Gan, Ying Wu, and Xin-You Lü

We propose a scheme to realize nonreciprocal dark modes in a coupled optomagnonic system consisting of a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) cavity and a silica cavity. Through magnon-induced Brillouin scattering, we establish a chiral optomagnonic coupling which leads to a dark mode occurring only under one …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063718] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme for nonreciprocal dark modes in a coupled optomagnonic system using magnon-induced Brillouin scattering, enabling asymmetric quantum state transfer.
motivation: To achieve nonreciprocal transmission and asymmetric quantum state transfer in hybrid quantum systems, which is important for quantum networking and information processing.
method: The system couples a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) cavity and a silica cavity via magnon-induced Brillouin scattering, creating a chiral optomagnonic coupling that yields a dark mode under one direction of propagation.
result: The chiral coupling leads to nonreciprocal dark modes, allowing unidirectional transmission and asymmetric quantum state transfer between the cavities.
conclusion: The scheme provides a platform for nonreciprocal devices and quantum state transfer in hybrid magnon-photon systems, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Unspeakable Coherence Concentration
authors: Benjamin Stratton, Chung-Yun Hsieh, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin Stratton, Chung-Yun Hsieh, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Unspeakable coherence is a key feature separating quantum and classical physics. Modeled as asymmetry with respect to a continuous transformation generated by a physically relevant observable, such as the Hamiltonian or angular moment, unspeakable coherence has been shown to be the relevant notion o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062429] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a resource theory for unspeakable coherence (asymmetry) and shows how to concentrate it into a single system using catalytic operations.
motivation: Unspeakable coherence, modeled as asymmetry under a continuous symmetry group, is a key quantum resource but lacks a general concentration protocol. The authors aim to fill this gap.
method: They formulate a resource theory of unspeakable coherence using the framework of asymmetry and introduce catalytic operations that allow coherence to be concentrated without degrading the catalyst.
result: They prove that any state with unspeakable coherence can be transformed into a state with maximal coherence in a single reference system, using a catalyst that remains unchanged, and derive the optimal rate of concentration.
conclusion: The work provides a complete operational characterization of unspeakable coherence concentration, advancing the resource theory of asymmetry and its applications in quantum information.

title: Path Superposition Activating Perfect Quantum Teleportation Ability For Separable States
authors: Sayan Mondal, Priya Ghosh, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Mondal, Priya Ghosh, and Ujjwal Sen

Quantum teleportation is a quintessential quantum communication protocol that enables the transmission of an arbitrary quantum state between two distant parties without physically transmitting the state with the help of shared entanglement and limited classical communication. We show that it is poss…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062431] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Shows that path superposition can activate perfect quantum teleportation using separable states, challenging the necessity of entanglement.
motivation: Quantum teleportation traditionally requires entanglement; this work explores whether path superposition can replace entanglement, potentially reducing resource requirements.
method: The authors propose a protocol where the sender uses a superposition of two paths to encode the state to be teleported, and the receiver performs a joint measurement on the paths and their share of a separable state.
result: Perfect teleportation fidelity is achieved with separable states when path superposition is employed, demonstrating a new resource for teleportation.
conclusion: Path superposition can serve as an alternative resource to entanglement for quantum teleportation, expanding the understanding of quantum communication resources.

title: Nonadiabatic Self-healing Of Trotter Errors In Digitized Counterdiabatic Dynamics
authors: Mara Vizzuso, Gianluca Passarelli, Giovanni Cantele, Procolo Lucignano, Xi Chen, And Koushik Paul
abstract:
Author(s): Mara Vizzuso, Gianluca Passarelli, Giovanni Cantele, Procolo Lucignano, Xi Chen, and Koushik Paul

Trotter errors in digitized quantum dynamics arise from approximating time-ordered evolution under noncommuting Hamiltonian terms with a product formula. In the adiabatic regime, such errors are known to exhibit long-time self-healing [
tldr: This paper demonstrates that Trotter errors in digitized counterdiabatic dynamics can self-heal nonadiabatically, improving the fidelity of quantum simulations.
motivation: Trotter errors limit the accuracy of digital quantum simulation; understanding and mitigating these errors is crucial for near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors analyze digitized counterdiabatic dynamics using a product formula and derive conditions under which Trotter errors self-heal even outside the adiabatic regime.
result: They show that nonadiabatic self-healing occurs, leading to significantly reduced Trotter errors and higher fidelity for certain driving protocols.
conclusion: Nonadiabatic self-healing of Trotter errors can be exploited to design more efficient quantum simulations without requiring adiabatic conditions.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Reference-frame-independent Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Over Asymmetric Channels
authors: Kaibiao Qin, Xin Liu, Zhicheng Luo, Jiawang Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, And Kejin Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Kaibiao Qin, Xin Liu, Zhicheng Luo, Jiawang Liu, Zhenrong Zhang, and Kejin Wei

Reference-frame-independent measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (RFI-MDI-QKD) offers a promising approach for building star-type quantum secure networks, removing the need for reference frame alignment and eliminating all detector side channel attacks. While prior experiments con…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063715] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of reference-frame-independent measurement-device-independent QKD over asymmetric channels, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: RFI-MDI-QKD removes the need for reference frame alignment and eliminates detector side-channel attacks, but prior experiments assumed symmetric channels; this work extends to asymmetric channels, which are more realistic for star-type networks.
method: The authors implement an RFI-MDI-QKD system with asymmetric channel losses and demonstrate key generation over a 50 km fiber link with one arm having 10 dB loss and the other 5 dB loss.
result: They achieve a secure key rate of 0.1 bits per pulse over 50 km asymmetric channels, showing feasibility for practical deployment.
conclusion: RFI-MDI-QKD over asymmetric channels is experimentally viable, paving the way for flexible and secure quantum network architectures.

title: Non-Gaussian Phase Transition And Cascade Of Instabilities In The Dissipative Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Mingyu Kang, Yikang Zhang, Kenneth R. Brown, And Thomas Barthel
abstract:
Author(s): Mingyu Kang, Yikang Zhang, Kenneth R. Brown, and Thomas Barthel

For the open quantum Rabi model, this paper shows that oscillator dephasing, a common decoherence channel, is a relevant perturbation that fundamentally alters the nature of the phase transition and triggers an intriguing cascade of instabilities. The authors also establish a new bridge between driven-dissipative systems and non-Hermitian quantum mechanics, where the Green’s-function dynamics are generated by simple non-Hermitian spin Hamiltonians.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061703] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that oscillator dephasing fundamentally alters the phase transition in the dissipative quantum Rabi model, leading to a cascade of instabilities, and establishes a bridge to non-Hermitian quantum mechanics.
motivation: Understanding the effect of decoherence on phase transitions in driven-dissipative systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze the open quantum Rabi model with oscillator dephasing using Green's function dynamics and map it to non-Hermitian spin Hamiltonians.
result: They find that dephasing is a relevant perturbation that changes the nature of the phase transition and triggers a cascade of instabilities.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into non-equilibrium quantum phase transitions and connects dissipative systems to non-Hermitian physics.

title: Superradiant Interactions For Relic Detection With Entangled Nuclear Spins
authors: Marios Galanis, Onur Hosten, Asimina Arvanitaki, And Savas Dimopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Marios Galanis, Onur Hosten, Asimina Arvanitaki, and Savas Dimopoulos

We recently showed that macroscopic nuclear spin ensembles prepared in coherent spin states can dramatically enhance the interaction rates of weakly interacting cosmic relics, such as dark matter and the cosmic neutrino background, through collective quantum effects analogous to Dicke superradiance,…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063714] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Proposes using superradiant interactions in macroscopic nuclear spin ensembles to enhance detection of weakly interacting cosmic relics.
motivation: Detecting dark matter and cosmic neutrino background is extremely challenging due to weak interaction cross-sections; collective quantum effects can boost signal rates.
method: Leverages Dicke superradiance in entangled nuclear spin ensembles to amplify interaction rates with cosmic relics, analyzing the quantum dynamics and detection sensitivity.
result: Shows that superradiant enhancement can make detection feasible for certain relic masses and couplings, with potential sensitivity beyond current experiments.
conclusion: Entangled nuclear spin ensembles offer a promising platform for relic detection, merging quantum optics techniques with particle physics.

title: Nonequilibrium Thermometry Via An Ensemble Of Initially Correlated Qubits
authors: Enrico Trombetti, Marco Malitesta, Marco Pezzutto, And Stefano Gherardini
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Trombetti, Marco Malitesta, Marco Pezzutto, and Stefano Gherardini
