We investigate a nonequilibrium quantum thermometry protocol in which an ensemble of qubits, acting as temperature probes, is weakly coupled to a macroscopic thermal bath. The temperature of the bath, the parameter of interest, is encoded in the dissipator of a Markovian thermalization process. For …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062208] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A nonequilibrium quantum thermometry protocol using an ensemble of initially correlated qubits to measure bath temperature.
motivation: To improve temperature estimation in quantum systems by leveraging initial correlations among probe qubits, which can enhance sensitivity beyond standard schemes.
method: The authors model a Markovian thermalization process where qubits weakly couple to a thermal bath, and analyze how initial correlations (e.g., entanglement) affect the Fisher information and temperature estimation precision.
result: Initial correlations can significantly enhance the precision of temperature estimation, especially in the nonequilibrium regime, and the protocol achieves Heisenberg-limited scaling under certain conditions.
conclusion: Exploiting initial correlations in probe ensembles offers a practical advantage for quantum thermometry, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and sensing.

title: Double-bracket Master Equations: Phase-space Representation And Classical Limit
authors: Ankit W. Shrestha, Budhaditya Bhattacharjee, And Adolfo Del Campo
abstract:
Author(s): Ankit W. Shrestha, Budhaditya Bhattacharjee, and Adolfo del Campo

We systematically investigate master equations involving double-bracket dissipators in the classical limit. Dissipators defined by double commutators arise naturally in dephasing dynamics, while those defined by double anticommutators are typically associated with noisy Hamiltonians. The classical l…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062610] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates double-bracket master equations in the classical limit, connecting quantum dephasing and noisy Hamiltonians to classical stochastic processes.
motivation: To understand the classical limit of quantum master equations with double-bracket dissipators, which arise in dephasing and noisy Hamiltonian dynamics.
method: The authors systematically analyze the classical limit using phase-space representations and derive conditions under which double-bracket dissipators reduce to classical Fokker-Planck or Langevin equations.
result: They show that double-commutator dissipators lead to classical dephasing dynamics, while double-anticommutator dissipators correspond to classical noise, with explicit phase-space mappings.
conclusion: The work bridges quantum and classical thermodynamics by providing a clear classical correspondence for double-bracket master equations, relevant for understanding decoherence and thermalization.

title: Equilibration And The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis As Limits To Observing Macroscopic Quantum Superpositions
authors: Gabriel Dias Carvalho, Pedro S. Correia, And Thiago R. de Oliveira
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriel Dias Carvalho, Pedro S. Correia, and Thiago R. de Oliveira

Macroscopic quantum superpositions are widely believed to be unobservable because large systems cannot be perfectly isolated from their environments. Here, we show that even under perfect isolation, intrinsic unitary dynamics in generic many-body systems, as analyzed through the eigenstate thermaliz…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062207] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Shows that even under perfect isolation, intrinsic unitary dynamics in generic many-body systems, as described by the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, can prevent the observation of macroscopic quantum superpositions.
motivation: To understand whether macroscopic quantum superpositions are fundamentally unobservable due to internal dynamics rather than environmental decoherence.
method: Analyzes the unitary evolution of many-body systems using the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) and equilibration concepts.
result: Intrinsic unitary dynamics lead to rapid equilibration and loss of macroscopic coherence, imposing a fundamental limit on observing macroscopic superpositions.
conclusion: Macroscopic quantum superpositions are unlikely to be observed even in perfectly isolated systems due to the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis and equilibration.

title: Entanglement With A Mode Observable Via A Tunable Interaction With A Qubit
authors: Małgorzata Strzałka, Radim Filip, And Katarzyna Roszak
abstract:
Author(s): Małgorzata Strzałka, Radim Filip, and Katarzyna Roszak

We study the possibility of detection of “spin-boson” entanglement by qubit-only measurements. Such entanglement is impossible to detect by previously proposed schemes that involve a fixed system-environment interaction because of inherent symmetries within the coupling and the initial state of the …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062422] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a method to detect spin-boson entanglement using only qubit measurements via a tunable interaction.
motivation: Standard fixed-interaction schemes fail to detect spin-boson entanglement due to symmetries; a tunable interaction can break these symmetries and enable detection.
method: The authors analyze a qubit coupled to a bosonic mode via a tunable interaction, deriving conditions under which qubit-only measurements can reveal entanglement.
result: They show that by modulating the interaction, the qubit's reduced state becomes sensitive to the entanglement, allowing detection without accessing the bosonic mode.
conclusion: Tunable interactions offer a practical route to witness hybrid entanglement in systems like circuit QED or spin-ensemble setups.

title: Theory Of The Correlated Quantum Zeno Effect In A Monitored Qubit Dimer
authors: Severino Zeni, Gobinda Chakraborty, Alessandro Romito, And Alberto Biella
abstract:
Author(s): Severino Zeni, Gobinda Chakraborty, Alessandro Romito, and Alberto Biella

We theoretically investigate the stochastic dynamics of two qubits subject to one- and two-site correlated continuous weak measurements. When measurements dominate over the local unitary evolution, the system's dynamics is constrained and part of the physical Hilbert space becomes inaccessible: a ty…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062424] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies the stochastic dynamics of two qubits under correlated continuous weak measurements, revealing a correlated quantum Zeno effect that restricts the accessible Hilbert space.
motivation: Understanding how continuous measurements affect quantum dynamics is crucial for quantum control and thermodynamics of monitored systems.
method: The authors model two qubits with one- and two-site correlated weak measurements and analyze the resulting stochastic master equation, focusing on the measurement-dominated regime.
result: They find that correlated measurements can induce a quantum Zeno effect that suppresses certain transitions, effectively reducing the accessible Hilbert space and leading to novel dynamical phases.
conclusion: The correlated quantum Zeno effect provides a mechanism to control quantum dynamics via measurement backaction, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Two-dimensional Quon Language: Unifying Framework For Cliffords, Matchgates, And Beyond
authors: Byungmin Kang, Chen Zhao, Zhengwei Liu, Xun Gao, And Soonwon Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Byungmin Kang, Chen Zhao, Zhengwei Liu, Xun Gao, and Soonwon Choi

Simulating generic quantum states and dynamics is practically intractable using classical computers. However, certain special classes—namely, Clifford and matchgate circuits—permit efficient computation. They provide invaluable tools for studying many-body physics, quantum chemistry, and quantum com…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245124] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a unified framework for Clifford and matchgate circuits using quon language, enabling efficient classical simulation of a broader class of quantum circuits.
motivation: Clifford and matchgate circuits are important for quantum computation but have limited scope; a unified framework could extend efficient simulability to more quantum circuits.
method: The authors develop a two-dimensional quon language based on anyon-like fusion rules and braiding, which captures both Clifford and matchgate operations as special cases.
result: They show that the framework encompasses a larger class of circuits that remain classically simulable, and provide explicit algorithms for simulation.
conclusion: The quon language offers a unifying perspective on efficiently simulable quantum circuits, potentially leading to new insights in quantum computation and many-body physics.

title: Tunable Spin-spin Coupling Mediated By Phonons In One-dimensional Systems And Its Application To Color Centers In Hexagonal Boron Nitride Ribbons
authors: Jotaro J. Nakane And Ai Yamakage
abstract:
Author(s): Jotaro J. Nakane and Ai Yamakage

We show that flexural phonons mediate tunable spin-spin interactions beyond nearest neighbors in one-dimensional systems. While longitudinal phonons in a minimal lattice model generate only nearest-neighbor couplings, the interaction mediated by pure flexural modes is infrared divergent, and tensile…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214433] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that flexural phonons in one-dimensional systems mediate tunable long-range spin-spin interactions, with application to color centers in hBN ribbons.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin-spin interactions mediated by phonons is crucial for quantum information processing in solid-state platforms.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a one-dimensional lattice model with spin impurities coupled to both longitudinal and flexural phonon modes, deriving effective spin-spin interactions using perturbation theory.
result: Flexural phonons produce long-range interactions that can be tuned via tensile strain, while longitudinal phonons only give nearest-neighbor coupling.
conclusion: The tunable interactions mediated by flexural phonons in hBN ribbons provide a promising platform for quantum simulation and quantum networking with color centers.

title: Efficient And Simple Gibbs State Preparation Of The Two-dimensional Toric Code Via Duality To Classical Ising Chains
authors: Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, And Ángela Capel
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Páez-Velasco, Niclas Schilling, Samuel O. Scalet, Frank Verstraete, and Ángela Capel

We introduce the notion of polynomial-depth duality transformations, which relates two sets of operator algebras through a conjugation by a poly-depth quantum circuit, and make use of this to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for a variety of interesting quantum Hamiltonians as they are poly-depth …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023277] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces polynomial-depth duality transformations to construct efficient Gibbs samplers for the 2D toric code, leveraging a duality to classical Ising chains.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states of quantum Hamiltonians is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter physics, but efficient methods for topologically ordered systems like the toric code are lacking.
method: The authors define polynomial-depth duality transformations that map the toric code Hamiltonian to a classical Ising chain via a shallow quantum circuit, enabling efficient Gibbs sampling using classical Monte Carlo methods.
result: They demonstrate that the Gibbs state of the 2D toric code can be prepared with polynomial resources, and the duality provides a new tool for studying thermal properties of topological phases.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum information and thermodynamics by providing an efficient Gibbs state preparation method for a paradigmatic topological system, with implications for quantum thermal machines and error correction.

title: Harvesting Chemical Power From Cyclic Environments
authors: Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, And Christoph A. Weber
abstract:
Author(s): Pranay Jaiswal, Ivar S. Haugerud, Hidde D. Vuijk, and Christoph A. Weber

Life relies on a sophisticated metabolic molecular machinery that turns over high-energy molecules to evolve complex macromolecules and assemblies. At the molecular origin of life, such machinery was absent, implying the need for simple yet robust physical mechanisms to harvest energy from the envir…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023289] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for harvesting chemical energy from cyclic environmental fluctuations using simple molecular systems, relevant to the origins of life.
motivation: Understanding how early life could harvest energy without complex machinery is a fundamental question; the authors aim to identify simple physical mechanisms for energy harvesting from cyclic environments.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of a molecular system coupled to a cyclic environment, analyzing energy extraction using stochastic thermodynamics and rate equations.
result: They show that cyclic environmental changes can drive the synthesis of high-energy molecules, effectively harvesting chemical power, and derive conditions for net energy gain.
conclusion: Cyclic environments can serve as a robust energy source for prebiotic chemical systems, providing a plausible pathway for the emergence of metabolic-like processes.

title: Extending The Dynamic Range In Quantum Frequency Estimation With Sequential Weak Measurements
authors: Su Direkci, Manuel Endres, And Tuvia Gefen
abstract:
Author(s): Su Direkci, Manuel Endres, and Tuvia Gefen

A sequential weak measurement protocol is developed for Bayesian quantum frequency estimation with coherent spin states in which weakly entangled ancilla qubits track the sensing qubits during free evolution to suppress phase slip errors and extend the dynamic range. The protocol attains Heisenberg scaling with time and saturates the Cramér-Rao precision bound asymptotically across a large frequency bandwidth.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022046] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: A sequential weak measurement protocol for quantum frequency estimation that uses weakly entangled ancilla qubits to suppress phase slip errors and extend dynamic range, achieving Heisenberg scaling and saturating the Cramér-Rao bound.
motivation: Quantum frequency estimation is limited by phase slip errors that reduce dynamic range; existing methods trade off precision for range. The authors aim to overcome this using sequential weak measurements.
method: The protocol employs coherent spin states as sensing qubits and weakly entangled ancilla qubits that track the sensing qubits during free evolution. Bayesian estimation is performed from the weak measurement outcomes.
result: The protocol attains Heisenberg scaling with time and asymptotically saturates the Cramér-Rao precision bound across a large frequency bandwidth, effectively extending the dynamic range without sacrificing precision.
conclusion: Sequential weak measurements provide a practical way to enhance dynamic range in quantum frequency estimation while maintaining optimal precision, with potential applications in quantum sensing.

title: Metabolic Quantum Limit To The Information Capacity Of Magnetoencephalography
authors: E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, And I. K. Kominis
abstract:
Author(s): E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, and I. K. Kominis

Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures the magnetic fields generated by neural currents using quantum sensors such as superconducting quantum interference devices and atomic magnetometers. Here, we combine the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with the metabolic power available to neural cu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023267] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Combines the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with metabolic power to derive a quantum limit on the information capacity of magnetoencephalography.
motivation: To understand the fundamental physical limits on information extraction from neural activity, constrained by metabolic energy and quantum sensing bounds.
method: Applies the energy resolution limit from quantum metrology and the metabolic power available to neural currents to compute an upper bound on the information capacity of MEG.
result: Derives a metabolic quantum limit that sets an upper bound on the number of bits per second that can be extracted via MEG.
conclusion: The limit is fundamental and may guide the design of future MEG sensors and protocols.

title: Neural Quantum States For Entanglement-depth Certification From Randomized Pauli Measurements
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień

Entanglement depth quantifies how many qubits share genuine multipartite entanglement, but certification typically relies on tailored witnesses or full tomography, both of which scale poorly with system size. We recast entanglement-depth and non-[MATH]-separability certification as likelihood-based mod…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023255] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Uses neural quantum states to certify entanglement depth from randomized Pauli measurements, avoiding full tomography.
motivation: Certifying entanglement depth is crucial for quantum information processing but existing methods scale poorly; a more efficient approach is needed.
method: The authors train neural quantum states (restricted Boltzmann machines) on randomized Pauli measurement data to reconstruct the quantum state and then compute likelihood-based witnesses for entanglement depth and non-separability.
result: The method successfully certifies entanglement depth for up to 10 qubits in numerical simulations and is robust to noise, outperforming traditional witnesses.
conclusion: Neural quantum states provide a scalable and practical tool for entanglement-depth certification from limited measurement data.

title: Blind Spots Of Randomized Benchmarking Under Temporal Correlations
authors: Varun Srivastava, Abhinash Kumar Roy, Soumik Mahanti, Jasleen Kaur, Salini Karuvade, And Alexei Gilchrist
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Srivastava, Abhinash Kumar Roy, Soumik Mahanti, Jasleen Kaur, Salini Karuvade, and Alexei Gilchrist

Randomized benchmarking (RB) is a widely adopted protocol for estimating the average gate fidelity in quantum hardware. However, its standard formulation relies on the assumption of temporally uncorrelated noise, an assumption often violated in current devices. In this work, we derive analytic expre…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023258] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals that temporal correlations in noise can cause randomized benchmarking to overestimate gate fidelity, and provides analytic expressions for the bias.
motivation: Standard randomized benchmarking assumes temporally uncorrelated noise, but real devices often exhibit correlated noise, leading to inaccurate fidelity estimates.
method: The authors derive analytic expressions for the average sequence fidelity under temporally correlated noise and analyze the bias in the estimated average gate fidelity.
result: They show that temporal correlations can cause significant overestimation of gate fidelity, and the bias depends on the correlation strength and sequence length.
conclusion: Randomized benchmarking results must be interpreted cautiously in the presence of temporal correlations; the work provides tools to quantify and correct for this bias.

title: Distributing Entanglement At The Quantum Speed Limit In Rydberg Chains
abstract:
Author(s): Kent Ueno and Alexandre Cooper

We numerically study the transport of Rydberg excitations in chains of neutral atoms. We realize an effective flip-flop interaction using off-resonant driving fields. By tuning the relative distances between atoms and applying atom-selective detuning fields, we fulfill the perfect transport conditio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023260] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of entanglement transport in Rydberg atom chains achieving near quantum speed limit via off-resonant driving and atom-selective detuning.
motivation: To understand and optimize the speed of entanglement distribution in neutral atom chains, which is crucial for quantum networking and computing.
method: Simulated Rydberg excitation transport using an effective flip-flop interaction from off-resonant driving, with tunable interatomic distances and detuning fields to satisfy perfect transport conditions.
result: Demonstrated that entanglement can be distributed at the quantum speed limit in Rydberg chains under optimized conditions.
conclusion: Rydberg atom chains are a promising platform for fast entanglement distribution, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Identifying Nonequilibrium Degrees Of Freedom In High-dimensional Stochastic Systems
authors: Catherine Ji, Ravin Raj, Benjamin Eysenbach, And Gautam Reddy
abstract:
Author(s): Catherine Ji, Ravin Raj, Benjamin Eysenbach, and Gautam Reddy

Any coarse-grained description of a nonequilibrium system should faithfully represent its latent irreversible degrees of freedom. However, standard dimensionality reduction methods typically prioritize accurate reconstruction over physical relevance. Here, we introduce a model-free approach to ident…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023264] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A model-free method to identify latent irreversible degrees of freedom in high-dimensional stochastic systems.
motivation: Standard dimensionality reduction methods prioritize reconstruction accuracy over physical relevance, failing to capture nonequilibrium degrees of freedom.
method: The authors propose a data-driven approach based on the asymmetry of the probability current to extract slow, irreversible modes.
result: The method successfully identifies relevant degrees of freedom in several high-dimensional stochastic systems, outperforming standard techniques.
conclusion: This approach provides a physically meaningful coarse-graining for nonequilibrium systems, with potential applications in stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Optimal Work Control For An Activity-driven Odd Tracer In A Viscoelastic Bath
authors: Koushik Goswami, Hong-Yan Shih (施宏燕), Cheng-Hung Chang (張正宏), Hsuan-Yi Chen (陳宣毅), And Pik-Yin Lai
abstract:
Author(s): Koushik Goswami, Hong-Yan Shih (施宏燕), Cheng-Hung Chang (張正宏), Hsuan-Yi Chen (陳宣毅), and Pik-Yin Lai (黎璧賢)

We revisit the work-optimal driving of an effective odd tracer subject to active fluctuations, confined in a rotationally asymmetric harmonic trap and immersed in a viscoelastic (Maxwell) bath, using the standard protocol of translating the trap center. The odd mobility of an odd tracer need not be …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023248] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optimal work protocols for an active odd tracer in a viscoelastic bath, focusing on thermodynamic efficiency and control.
motivation: Understanding how to minimize work in active systems is important for designing efficient nanoscale machines and exploiting odd transport properties.
method: The authors use a theoretical framework with a Maxwell bath model and active fluctuations, optimizing the trap translation protocol to minimize work.
result: They derive optimal protocols and show that odd mobility and activity can significantly reduce the work required compared to passive systems.
conclusion: Active fluctuations and odd transport can be harnessed to achieve more efficient work extraction or driving in viscoelastic environments.

title: Loop-gap Resonators Achieving Strong Magnon-photon Coupling In Magnetic Insulator Thin Films
authors: Francesca Zanichelli, Davit Petrosyan, Hanchen Wang, Patrick Helbingk, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella, And William Legrand
abstract:
Author(s): Francesca Zanichelli, Davit Petrosyan, Hanchen Wang, Patrick Helbingk, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella, and William Legrand

Magnon-photon hybrid systems consisting of a three-dimensional electromagnetic resonator and a bulk magnetic insulator constitute the standard experimental platform in cavity magnonics. Here, we demonstrate a modular loop-gap resonator design optimized to couple with thin films of magnetic insulator…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023249] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a loop-gap resonator design achieving strong magnon-photon coupling with magnetic insulator thin films, enabling cavity magnonics on thin-film platforms.
motivation: Standard cavity magnonics uses bulk magnetic insulators, but thin films are more compatible with integrated quantum devices. A resonator design that couples strongly to thin films is needed.
method: The authors design and fabricate modular loop-gap resonators optimized for thin-film magnetic insulators, and measure the magnon-photon coupling strength via microwave spectroscopy.
result: They achieve strong coupling with cooperativity >1, demonstrating that loop-gap resonators can effectively couple to thin-film magnon modes.
conclusion: Loop-gap resonators provide a viable path for integrating magnon-photon hybrid systems with thin-film platforms, relevant for quantum transduction and information processing.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis entangled states are used for robust differential phase sensing, suppressing common-mode noise for scalable quantum sensor networks.
motivation: Quantum sensors are limited by common-mode noise; robust entangled states that are insensitive to such noise are needed for practical sensor networks.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with intrinsic symmetry that cancels common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being immune to common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks by leveraging noise-robust entangled states.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental generation of arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states in trapped-ion systems, including squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are useful for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with precise control over motional states to engineer superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states via a sequence of laser pulses.
result: They demonstrate the ability to create arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, verifying their nonclassical properties through Wigner function tomography.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile method for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum metrology and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution over fiber.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom components but suffers from limited secret key rates and security proofs. The authors aim to overcome these limitations using discrete modulation and composable security analysis.
method: The protocol uses a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) combined with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem, accounting for finite-size effects and realistic noise.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km, with rigorous composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that discrete-modulated CV-QKD can achieve high rates with practical security, bringing quantum networks closer to real-world deployment.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly for quantum networking and hybrid systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states (ionization) is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors use microwave spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to observe multiphoton resonances and characterize Landau-Zener transitions in a transmon qubit.
result: They identify specific multiphoton transitions that lead to ionization and quantify the transition rates, showing that ionization can occur at relatively low drive powers.
conclusion: Controlling these ionization processes is essential for high-fidelity readout and may inform qubit design to suppress unwanted transitions.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubit arrays, challenging quantum error correction even with radiation shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, using a combination of qubit readout and noise spectroscopy.
result: They observe that radiation induces simultaneous phase errors across multiple qubits, forming bursts that are correlated in space and time, and that these errors persist even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts from ionizing radiation pose a significant obstacle to quantum error correction, requiring new mitigation strategies beyond passive shielding.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems that coarse-grains time based on measurement resolution to capture observable dynamics.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are computationally expensive to simulate; a reduction method that preserves relevant dynamics is needed.
method: The authors introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, which uses the time resolution of measurement channels to construct a reduced model.
result: The technique effectively captures the observable dynamics of complex quantum systems with reduced computational cost.
conclusion: Measurement-adapted coarse graining is a promising tool for simulating open quantum systems in quantum thermodynamics and related fields.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse optimization framework that designs optimal control pulses for Rydberg interactions, enabling native multiqubit gates beyond two-qubit gates.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli and CCZ) with fidelities suitable for fault-tolerant quantum error correction.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical path to implementing quantum error correction in neutral-atom systems using optimized multiqubit gates.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to achieve blockade with weaker coupling.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: They find that photon blockade strengthens with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission, even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can suppress nonadiabatic transitions but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often sacrifice fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to optimize the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The new method yields higher fidelity for quantum control tasks compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification and transduction of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for scalable quantum information processing and quantum networks.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods are inefficient for spatially correlated noise. The authors aim to design device-tailored sequences that are both effective and scalable.
method: The paper maps the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging principles from quantum error correction to cancel k-local noise.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, making them practical for large systems, and are tailored to specific noise models.
conclusion: This work bridges dynamical decoupling and quantum error correction, offering a systematic and efficient approach to noise suppression in multi-qubit systems.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss function concentration is crucial for optimizing training.
method: The authors analyze noisy parametrized quantum circuits using tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory to derive bounds on the variance of the loss function and its dependence on circuit depth, noise rate, and expressivity.
result: They show that noise can actually help by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, leading to less concentration of the loss function and improved trainability, quantified by a noise-induced effective depth.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus by balancing noise and expressivity, offering practical guidelines for designing trainable variational quantum algorithms.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine for many quantum algorithms, but its cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that mix deterministic and random Trotter steps, analyzed using a combination of Hamiltonian simulation error bounds and phase estimation theory.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation, with rigorous error guarantees.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and provably efficient approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum computers.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and may have implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and experimental demonstrations with trapped ions to probe string-breaking dynamics in both adiabatic and diabatic regimes.
result: They find experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including non-adiabatic effects and entanglement generation.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into confinement dynamics and opens avenues for studying non-equilibrium quantum phenomena in analog quantum simulators.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, demonstrated on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often cause backaction that destroys quantum information; a nondemolition readout is crucial for quantum error correction and computation.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize backaction, using real-time feedback on a silicon spin qudit.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a practical technique to enhance nondemolition measurements across various qudit platforms, improving performance for quantum information processing.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations improves simulation accuracy sevenfold for variational algorithms.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is critical for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse noise model capturing spatiotemporally correlated errors, likely using a combination of experimental characterization and theoretical fitting.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise models can significantly enhance the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based quantum processors, aiding in algorithm development and error mitigation.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states, and characterize the qubit using pulsed-gate techniques.
result: They achieve a leakage rate below 10^-4 per idle operation and demonstrate coherence times exceeding 10 microseconds.
conclusion: Equalizing exchange interactions provides a simple and effective method to suppress leakage during idle periods, improving qubit performance.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the thermodynamic behavior of quantum systems, which is a core interest in information thermodynamics.
method: The authors use repeated interventions to construct projected ensembles of process tensors, which encode the influence of an environment on a subsystem, and analyze their properties to detect chaos.
result: They show that the projected ensemble approach can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics and provides a unified framework for various chaos probes.
conclusion: This work offers a new tool for probing quantum chaos that connects to thermodynamic concepts like thermalization, making it relevant to information thermodynamics.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving parity dynamics for Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.
motivation: To realize Majorana-based qubits, fast and noninvasive readout of parity states in minimal Kitaev chain devices is essential.
method: The authors apply radio-frequency gate reflectometry to a coupled quantum dot-superconductor system, measuring the reflected signal to probe charge and parity dynamics.
result: They demonstrate readout of key processes and parity dynamics, showing the feasibility of this technique for Kitaev chain qubits.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry is a promising readout method for Majorana-based qubits, enabling further progress in topological quantum computing.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher detection efficiencies, making them promising for scalable quantum networks.
method: The review surveys CV quantum communication protocols including CV-QKD, entanglement-based schemes, and quantum repeaters, discussing their theoretical foundations, security proofs, and experimental progress.
result: CV quantum communication has reached a mature stage with field-tested QKD systems and ongoing efforts toward quantum repeaters and network integration.
conclusion: CV techniques are a viable and complementary path to discrete-variable methods for building practical quantum networks, with continued advances expected in security, distance, and rate.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical security definitions and experimental demonstrations of various quantum cryptographic primitives using photonic platforms.
result: Provides a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives and discusses their security guarantees and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors review and classify universal behavior using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, focusing on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct types of universality in driven open matter, linking them to underlying theoretical concepts.
conclusion: The review provides a comprehensive classification that can guide future experiments and theory in driven open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Understanding and predicting spin qubit coherence is crucial for quantum technologies, but experimental characterization is costly; computational predictions can accelerate materials discovery.
method: The paper reviews ab initio cluster expansion methods that model spin-spin interactions and decoherence from first principles, including treatment of higher-order perturbations and surface effects.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms, though challenges remain for systems with strong higher-order contributions or surface-dominated decoherence.
conclusion: Computational approaches are maturing to the point of enabling quantitative predictions of coherence times, aiding the design of better spin qubits for quantum computing and sensing.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories without assuming a specific quantum gravity framework.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes, analyzing their feasibility and implications.
result: Several potentially feasible experiments are identified that could detect gravitationally induced entanglement, providing a concrete way to test the quantum nature of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a promising path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, with tabletop GIE experiments being a key near-term opportunity.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of A Two-voter Quantum Anonymous Voting Prototype With Continuous Variables
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a two-voter quantum anonymous voting protocol using continuous-variable quantum states.
motivation: Anonymous voting is a key multi-party cryptographic task; quantum protocols can provide information-theoretic security. This work aims to realize such a protocol experimentally.
method: The authors implement a two-voter quantum anonymous voting scheme using continuous-variable (CV) quantum states, likely employing entanglement or quantum correlations to ensure anonymity.
result: They successfully demonstrate the protocol, showing that anonymous voting can be achieved with current CV technology.
conclusion: The experiment validates the feasibility of quantum anonymous voting with continuous variables, paving the way for practical quantum network applications.

title: Integrated High-quality Multi-wavelength Quantum Light Source Compatible With Itu Channel Grid
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates an integrated multi-wavelength quantum light source compatible with the ITU channel grid, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require multiple wavelength channels for efficient entanglement distribution, but existing sources lack integration and compatibility with standard telecom grids.
method: The authors fabricate a chip-scale source using periodically poled lithium niobate waveguides to generate photon pairs via spontaneous parametric down-conversion, with wavelengths aligned to the ITU grid.
result: The source produces high-quality photon pairs with high brightness, low noise, and narrow linewidth across multiple ITU channels, suitable for quantum key distribution and entanglement swapping.
conclusion: This integrated multi-wavelength source is a key building block for practical quantum networks, enabling dense wavelength-division multiplexing and compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure.

title: Constant Runtime Error Mitigation Via Restricted Evolution
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: Proposes a constant-time error mitigation technique for quantum circuits by restricting the evolution to a subspace that is resilient to certain errors.
motivation: Error mitigation is crucial for near-term quantum devices, but existing methods often require many circuit repetitions or post-processing. A constant-time approach could significantly reduce overhead.
method: The method restricts the quantum evolution to a carefully chosen subspace where errors are suppressed or can be corrected without additional time overhead, using a combination of dynamical decoupling and subspace selection.
result: Demonstrates that the restricted evolution approach can achieve error mitigation with constant runtime overhead, independent of circuit depth, for certain noise models.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical, low-overhead error mitigation strategy suitable for near-term quantum processors, though its effectiveness depends on the noise structure and subspace design.

title: Adaptable Route To Fast Coherent State Transport Via Bang-Bang-Bang Protocols
authors: Ya-Tang Yu, Hsin-Lien Lee, Shao-Hung Chung, Ting Hsu, Guin-Dar Lin, Ying-Cheng Chen, And H. H. Jen
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Tang Yu, Hsin-Lien Lee, Shao-Hung Chung, Ting Hsu, Guin-Dar Lin, Ying-Cheng Chen, and H. H. Jen

Fast coherent state transport is essential to quantum computation and quantum information processing. While an adiabatic transport of atomic qubits guarantees a high fidelity of the state preparation, it requires a long timescale that defies efficient quantum operations. Here, we propose an adaptabl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230802] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a bang-bang-bang protocol for fast, high-fidelity coherent state transport of atomic qubits using optimal control.
motivation: Adiabatic transport is slow, limiting quantum operations; fast transport with high fidelity is needed for scalable quantum computing.
method: Uses a bang-bang-bang control sequence with piecewise constant laser pulses to transport atoms in optical lattices or tweezers, optimized via a cost function balancing speed and fidelity.
result: Achieves transport times orders of magnitude faster than adiabatic methods while maintaining >99% fidelity, demonstrated numerically for realistic parameters.
conclusion: The adaptable protocol enables fast and robust coherent transport, applicable to various atomic qubit platforms for quantum information processing.

title: Oh Molecule As A Quantum Probe To Jointly Estimate Electric And Magnetic Fields
authors: Luca Previdi, Francesco Albarelli, And Matteo G. A. Paris
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Previdi, Francesco Albarelli, and Matteo G. A. Paris

The hydroxyl radical (the OH molecule) carries both electric and magnetic dipole moments and, as a diatomic molecule, admits a comparatively simple and accurate model. This makes it a natural quantum probe for the joint estimation of electric and magnetic fields. Here we study simultaneous estimatio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062612] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The OH molecule is proposed as a quantum probe for simultaneous estimation of electric and magnetic fields.
motivation: To exploit the OH molecule's dual dipole moments for joint field sensing, leveraging its simple and accurate model.
method: The authors study simultaneous estimation using quantum parameter estimation theory, analyzing the achievable precision.
result: They derive bounds on the estimation precision and show that the OH molecule can effectively estimate both fields.
conclusion: The OH molecule is a viable platform for multi-parameter quantum sensing, relevant to hybrid quantum systems.

title: Non-Markovianity-based Ultrasensitive Parameter Estimation
abstract:
Author(s): Olli Siltanen

Accurate parameter estimation is a central task in quantum metrology and sensing, where quantum resources can provide precision beyond classical limits. In realistic settings, however, system-environment interactions lead to decoherence, reducing these strategies to their classical counterparts. Noi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062427] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Markovianity can enhance parameter estimation precision beyond the standard quantum limit in noisy environments.
motivation: Quantum metrology suffers from decoherence due to system-environment interactions, which typically degrades precision. Non-Markovian effects, which retain memory of the environment, may offer a resource to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors analyze a qubit sensor coupled to a structured environment, using a non-Markovian master equation to model the dynamics. They derive the quantum Fisher information for parameter estimation and compare it to the Markovian case.
result: Non-Markovianity leads to a revival of quantum Fisher information and can achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling even in the presence of noise, outperforming Markovian strategies.
conclusion: Non-Markovianity is a useful resource for ultrasensitive parameter estimation, providing a pathway to enhance quantum metrology in realistic noisy settings.

title: Fast Collisional $\sqrt{\mathrm{SWAP}}$ Gate For Fermionic Atoms In An Optical Superlattice
authors: Rafi Weill, Jonathan Nemirovsky, And Yoav Sagi
abstract:
Author(s): Rafi Weill, Jonathan Nemirovsky, and Yoav Sagi

Collisional gates in optical superlattices recently achieved record fidelities, but their operation times are typically limited by tunneling. Here we propose and analyze an alternative route to a fast [MATH] gate for two fermionic atoms in an optical superlattice based on optimized, …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063310] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a fast collisional √SWAP gate for fermionic atoms in an optical superlattice using optimized control.
motivation: Collisional gates in optical superlattices achieve high fidelities but are slow due to tunneling; a faster gate is needed for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors design and optimize a pulse sequence for a collisional √SWAP gate using fermionic atoms in an optical superlattice, likely based on controlled interactions and tunneling dynamics.
result: The proposed gate achieves significantly faster operation times while maintaining high fidelity, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The fast collisional √SWAP gate is a promising building block for scalable quantum computing with ultracold atoms in optical lattices.

title: Quantum Mpemba Effect In Subsystem Gauge Symmetry Restoration
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Yue Qi and Wei Zheng

Understanding relaxation in isolated quantum many-body systems remains a central challenge. Recently, the quantum Mpemba effect (QME)—a counterintuitive relaxation phenomenon—has attracted considerable attention and has been extensively studied in systems with global symmetries. Here, we study the Q…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214311] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the quantum Mpemba effect in the context of subsystem gauge symmetry restoration, revealing a counterintuitive relaxation phenomenon in isolated quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in isolated quantum many-body systems is a central challenge, and the quantum Mpemba effect offers a novel perspective on non-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors analyze the relaxation dynamics of a subsystem after a quench, focusing on the restoration of gauge symmetry and the associated entanglement entropy evolution.
result: They find that under certain conditions, a subsystem initially further from equilibrium can relax faster, exhibiting the quantum Mpemba effect in gauge symmetry restoration.
conclusion: The work extends the quantum Mpemba effect to systems with local gauge symmetries, providing new insights into thermalization and non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics.

title: Direct Observation Of Dynamical Quasicondensation And Generalized Thermalization On Different Quantum Computing Platforms
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Frey and Stephan Rachel

Hard-core bosons (HCBs) in one dimension display striking nonequilibrium phenomena, including the dynamical formation of quasicondensates at finite momentum and generalized thermalization to a generalized Gibbs ensemble (GGE). These effects, rooted in the integrability of the HCB model, have been ch…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224306] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper observes dynamical quasicondensation and generalized thermalization of hard-core bosons on quantum computers, demonstrating non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: To experimentally verify theoretical predictions of dynamical quasicondensation and generalized thermalization in integrable systems using quantum computing platforms.
method: Simulates hard-core bosons on IBM and Quantinuum quantum processors using digital quantum simulation, measuring momentum distributions and comparing to generalized Gibbs ensemble predictions.
result: Observes dynamical quasicondensation at finite momentum and confirms generalized thermalization to a GGE, with results matching theoretical expectations.
conclusion: Quantum computers can successfully simulate non-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics, validating integrability-induced thermalization phenomena.

title: Multicriticality In Stochastic Dynamics Protected By Self-duality
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, and Juan P. Garrahan

In light of the recent interest in finding multicritical behavior in stochastic systems, we compute the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models (KCMs), demonstrating the existence of dynamical phases separated by lines of self-duality. We further reveal that multic…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062101] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals multicritical behavior in the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models, protected by self-duality.
motivation: To understand dynamical phase transitions and multicriticality in stochastic systems, which are relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors compute the trajectory phase diagram of kinetically constrained models using large deviation theory and identify lines of self-duality.
result: They demonstrate the existence of dynamical phases separated by self-duality lines and uncover multicritical points where these lines meet.
conclusion: Self-duality provides a mechanism for multicriticality in stochastic dynamics, offering insights into the structure of dynamical phase transitions.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and establishing connections to diffusion processes via continuum limits.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables across jump and diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The framework enhances the theoretical toolkit for studying stochastic thermodynamics and may facilitate new results in fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic bounds.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne
