This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular circuits may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, high-dimensional information processing mechanism.
method: The paper presents a conceptual framework and theoretical arguments, drawing on phase separation, nucleation, and multi-component condensation to illustrate how condensates can classify and respond to signals.
result: It suggests that phase transitions enable cells to perform computations like sensing, classification, and decision-making with high-dimensional inputs, potentially more efficiently than molecular circuits.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation is a promising paradigm for cellular information processing, warranting further theoretical and experimental investigation.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing, especially for Trotterized dynamics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing and thermalization times in quantum circuits, studying the breakdown of prethermalization.
result: Shadowing time is finite in many-body chaotic systems, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit, being a finite-size effect.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and Trotterization in quantum circuits, with implications for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry reveals a two-step thermalization process in mesoscopic metallic islands at high magnetic field, involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, especially in high magnetic fields where quantum Hall effects dominate.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure electron temperature dynamics in mesoscopic metallic islands, analyzing the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization process: fast electronic thermalization followed by slower equilibration with nuclear spins, providing insights into energy flow in quantum Hall systems.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the importance of nuclear spins in thermalization of mesoscopic electron baths, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and heat management in quantum devices.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and low atom loss remains challenging. EIT offers a way to achieve nondestructive imaging and continuous loading.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency to image atoms with minimal scattering, and use the same technique to load atoms into arrays continuously. They operate in finite magnetic fields to enable EIT.
result: They achieve high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and demonstrate continuous loading of atom arrays, improving the practicality of neutral-atom quantum platforms.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading is a powerful technique for neutral-atom arrays, enabling higher performance and scalability for quantum information processing.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice for near-optimal quantum simulation.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics (e.g., open systems) on quantum computers requires efficient dilation methods that avoid connectivity bottlenecks.
method: The paper introduces a dilation based on a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice and uses moment-matching to approximate the nonunitary evolution with a unitary circuit.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal query complexity and reduces circuit depth compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This framework provides a practical and efficient way to simulate linear differential equations and nonunitary processes on near-term quantum devices.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, demonstrating its effectiveness on a qubit platform and revealing noise features not captured by conventional techniques.
conclusion: This work provides a new tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, which can aid in understanding decoherence and improving qubit performance.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and error correction are still developing.
method: The authors propose a transversal architecture that combines small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate quantum error-correcting codes, optimized for neutral-atom hardware with long-range interactions and native multi-qubit gates.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead are demonstrated for quantum simulation tasks, enabling megaquop-scale computations with realistic hardware parameters.
conclusion: The transversal architecture provides a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation on neutral-atom platforms, bridging the gap between current hardware and application-scale quantum computing.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with variational quantum algorithms to achieve reliable molecular energy calculations on near-term hardware.
method: Combines noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets on a trapped-ion quantum processor to compute molecular energies with partial fault tolerance.
result: Achieves a molecular energy computation with improved accuracy compared to non-error-corrected approaches, demonstrating the feasibility of error-corrected quantum chemistry.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically applied to quantum chemistry simulations, paving the way for more reliable quantum computations of molecular properties.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops fault-tolerant protocols for Majorana-based quantum codes, including gates and measurements, and constructs high-rate codes.
motivation: Majorana-based qubits are promising for topological quantum computing, but fault-tolerant operations tailored to fermionic systems are needed to realize practical quantum error correction.
method: The authors generalize qubit-based fault-tolerant protocols to fermionic systems, designing transversal gates, measurement schemes, and code constructions that respect the parity constraints of Majorana modes.
result: They demonstrate that high-rate quantum codes can be constructed for Majorana platforms, and that fault-tolerant operations can be implemented with low overhead.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for fault-tolerant quantum computing with Majorana-based qubits, bridging topological qubits and practical error correction.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of simulation methods makes it hard to compare and choose approaches.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on the Feynman-Vernon influence functional and path integrals, and use it to categorize and relate various simulation techniques (e.g., hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, tensor networks).
result: The review provides a clear taxonomy of methods, highlighting their commonalities, differences, and regimes of applicability, with examples from quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
conclusion: The unified framework helps researchers select appropriate simulation tools for non-Markovian open quantum systems, advancing both theoretical understanding and practical applications.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing the use of qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in circuit depth and resource efficiency.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits may offer simplifications for certain gates and algorithms, potentially reducing overhead.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits can reduce the number of operations and qubits needed for specific tasks, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, especially for near-term devices, though challenges in control and error correction remain.

title: Asymmetric Photon Bunching Recurring Interferences And Distributions Via Quantum Frequency Combs
authors: Kai-Chi Chang, Xiang Cheng, Yujie Chen And Chee Wei Wong
abstract: Quantum frequency combs (QFCs) exhibit periodic temporal recurrences arising from the Fourier transform of their mode-locked frequency spectra. While QFCs have been experimentally demonstrated, asymmetric Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) revival interference in QFCs has not been systematically investigated, and the efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals has remained unreported. Here, we present the first experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric HOM recurrence interference using QFCs. First, we verified HOM revivals spanning 10 time-bins in a 10.21 GHz QFC, obtaining a 72.95 ± 0.8% visibility for its central dip. Then, we measured up to 20 time-bins from a 50 GHz QFC, with an accidental-subtracted central HOM dip visibility of 70.82 ± 0.7%. Finally, we distributed the QFC after 21 km optical fibers without dispersion compensation, observing photon bunching measurements across 12 time-bins, with a central dip visibility of 70.5 ± 0.9%. The deviation from ideal HOM interference is attributed to residual frequency distinguishability between the signal and idler photons, as confirmed in our theoretical calculations. These results establish QFCs as a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing tasks, such as high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.
tldr: First experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric Hong-Ou-Mandel revival interference using quantum frequency combs over 21 km fiber.
motivation: Quantum frequency combs (QFCs) are promising for high-dimensional quantum information processing, but asymmetric HOM revival interference and efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals had not been systematically investigated.
method: The authors experimentally generate QFCs with 10.21 GHz and 50 GHz spacing, measure HOM revivals across multiple time-bins, and distribute the QFC over 21 km of optical fiber without dispersion compensation.
result: They observe HOM revivals spanning up to 20 time-bins with visibilities around 70%, and after 21 km fiber distribution, they still observe photon bunching across 12 time-bins with 70.5% visibility.
conclusion: QFCs are a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing tasks such as high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.

title: Observation Of Phase Doubling And Entanglement In Coherent Matter-wave Reactions
authors: Shu Nagata, Tadej Mežnaršič, Chuixin Kong And Cheng Chin
abstract: Chemical reactions in a statistical ensemble are conventionally regarded as incoherent processes driven by thermodynamics. In the quantum degenerate regime, where atoms and molecules form coherent matter waves, reactions are theoretically described by nonlinear mixing of matter-wave fields. In this scenario, we expect phase matching between reactants and products, analogous to the mixing of photonic fields in nonlinear optics. Here we report on the observation of phase coherent reaction dynamics of Bose-condensed atoms and molecules near a Feshbach resonance. Using matter-wave diffraction with optical lattices, we verify spatial coherence of both atoms and molecules and observe phase doubling when atomic waves combine into molecular waves, the matter-wave analogue of optical frequency doubling. The diffraction patterns further reveal two-atom entanglement generated during the reaction. Our observations establish phase coherence and entanglement generation as two essential features of ‘quantum many-body chemistry’. Moreover, our work opens a pathway to control of reaction dynamics by manipulation of matter-wave phases.
tldr: Observation of phase doubling and entanglement in coherent matter-wave reactions of Bose-condensed atoms and molecules near a Feshbach resonance.
motivation: To demonstrate phase coherence and entanglement generation in chemical reactions in the quantum degenerate regime, analogous to nonlinear optics.
method: Matter-wave diffraction with optical lattices to verify spatial coherence and observe phase doubling; analysis of diffraction patterns to infer entanglement.
result: Phase doubling observed when atomic waves combine into molecular waves; diffraction patterns reveal two-atom entanglement generated during the reaction.
conclusion: Establishes phase coherence and entanglement as key features of quantum many-body chemistry, opening pathways to control reaction dynamics via matter-wave phases.

title: Making non-Markovian Master Equations Accessible With Approximate Environments
abstract:
Author(s): Gerardo Suárez and Michał Horodecki

Accurate and efficient simulation of open quantum systems remains a significant challenge, particularly for non-Markovian dynamics. We demonstrate the profound utility of expressing the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals within master equations. While not strictly requ…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064121] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to make non-Markovian master equations more tractable by approximating the environment correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals.
motivation: Simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems is computationally challenging; the authors aim to provide a practical approximation that retains accuracy while reducing complexity.
method: They express the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals, which allows the master equation to be solved more efficiently using standard techniques.
result: The approximation yields accurate dynamics for a range of non-Markovian regimes, significantly lowering computational cost compared to exact methods.
conclusion: This approach makes non-Markovian master equations more accessible for practical simulations, benefiting studies of open quantum systems in thermodynamics and other fields.

title: An Almost-linear Time Decoding Algorithm For Quantum Ldpc Codes Under Circuit-level Noise
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: An almost-linear time decoding algorithm for quantum LDPC codes under circuit-level noise.
motivation: Efficient decoding of quantum LDPC codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing decoders are often too slow or assume simpler noise models.
method: The authors propose a decoding algorithm based on belief propagation with a novel scheduling and post-processing step that achieves almost-linear time complexity while handling circuit-level noise.
result: The algorithm achieves decoding thresholds comparable to or better than existing decoders while running in almost-linear time, demonstrated on several families of quantum LDPC codes.
conclusion: This work provides a practical decoder for quantum LDPC codes that is both fast and effective under realistic noise, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Cavity-Free Mode Control Of Superfluorescence From Thermal Gas
abstract:
Author(s): H. Maeda and K. Kitano

Transverse-mode control of light has traditionally relied on optical cavities, whereas recent cavity-free approaches based on periodically arranged cold atoms that exploit collective radiation have attracted increasing attention. Here, we demonstrate a new cavity-free method applicable to thermal ga…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233603] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates cavity-free transverse-mode control of superfluorescence from a thermal gas using collective atomic effects.
motivation: Traditional mode control relies on optical cavities; cavity-free methods are attractive for simplicity and scalability, but existing approaches require cold atoms. This work extends cavity-free control to thermal gases.
method: The authors use a thermal gas of atoms and exploit collective radiation (superfluorescence) to achieve transverse-mode selection without a cavity, likely via spatial structuring of the atomic ensemble or pump beam.
result: They demonstrate successful transverse-mode control of superfluorescence from a thermal gas, showing that cavity-free mode control is possible even without cooling atoms to ultracold temperatures.
conclusion: This cavity-free method for thermal gases could simplify light source engineering and enable new applications in quantum optics and sensing, though it is not directly tied to quantum information processing or thermodynamics.

title: Universal Composite Phase Gates With Tunable Target Phase
authors: Peter Chernev, Mouhamad Al-Mahmoud, And Andon A. Rangelov
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Chernev, Mouhamad Al-Mahmoud, and Andon A. Rangelov

We present a systematic method for constructing universal composite phase gates with a continuously tunable target phase. Using a general Cayley-Klein parametrization of the single-pulse propagator, we design gates from an even number of nominal [MATH] pulses and derive analytic phase families by cance…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062434] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A systematic method for constructing universal composite phase gates with continuously tunable target phase using Cayley-Klein parametrization.
motivation: Composite pulses are essential for robust quantum control, but existing methods often fix the target phase; this work aims to provide tunability for greater flexibility in quantum gates.
method: The authors use a general Cayley-Klein parametrization of the single-pulse propagator and design gates from an even number of nominal π pulses, deriving analytic phase families by canceling error terms.
result: They demonstrate universal composite phase gates where the target phase can be continuously tuned, with explicit phase families and error suppression.
conclusion: The method offers a versatile tool for quantum control, enabling precise phase gates with robustness against pulse errors.

title: Error Convergence Of Quantum Linear System Solvers
abstract:
Author(s): Matias Ginzburg and Ugo Marzolino

The Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) algorithm remains a paradigmatic quantum routine for solving linear systems and a widely used benchmark in theoretical and experimental studies. Several circuit-level variants have been proposed to simplify its implementation, including constructions in which the cloc…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062436] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the error convergence of quantum linear system solvers, focusing on the HHL algorithm and its variants.
motivation: Understanding the error behavior of quantum linear system solvers is important for practical implementation, but the paper does not present novel information-theoretic results.
method: The authors study the convergence of errors in HHL-type algorithms, likely through analytical bounds or numerical simulations.
result: The paper provides insights into how errors accumulate and converge in quantum linear system solvers.
conclusion: The work is relevant to quantum algorithm analysis but does not directly advance the core interests in quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Hardware-efficient Quantum Annealing With Error Mitigation Via Classical Shadow
authors: Takaharu Yoshida, Yuta Shingu, Chihaya Shimada, Tetsuro Nikuni, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Yuichiro Matsuzaki
abstract:
Author(s): Takaharu Yoshida, Yuta Shingu, Chihaya Shimada, Tetsuro Nikuni, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Yuichiro Matsuzaki

Quantum annealing (QA) is an efficient method for finding the ground-state energy of the problem Hamiltonian. However, in practical implementation, the system suffers from decoherence. Recently, “localized virtual purification” (LVP) was proposed to suppress decoherence in the context of noisy inter…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062430] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hardware-efficient quantum annealing protocol with error mitigation using classical shadow techniques.
motivation: Quantum annealing suffers from decoherence in practical implementations; existing error mitigation methods like LVP are resource-intensive.
method: Combines quantum annealing with classical shadow tomography to estimate and correct errors efficiently, reducing the number of measurements needed.
result: Demonstrates improved ground-state energy estimation accuracy with fewer resources compared to standard LVP.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a practical error mitigation strategy for near-term quantum annealers.

title: Global Versus Local Discrimination Of Locally Implementable Multipartite Unitaries
authors: Satyaki Manna, Sneha Suresh, Anandamay Das Bhowmik, And Debashis Saha
abstract:
Author(s): Satyaki Manna, Sneha Suresh, Anandamay Das Bhowmik, and Debashis Saha

We study single-shot distinguishability of locally implementable multipartite unitaries under Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC) and global operations. As unitary discrimination depends on both the choice of probing states and the measurements on the evolved states, we classify LOCC…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062209] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies single-shot distinguishability of locally implementable multipartite unitaries under LOCC and global operations, classifying LOCC strategies and comparing their power.
motivation: Understanding the limitations of LOCC in discriminating quantum operations is fundamental for quantum communication and computation.
method: The authors classify LOCC strategies for unitary discrimination and analyze the optimal success probability using different probing states and measurements.
result: They find that global operations can outperform LOCC in discriminating certain locally implementable unitaries, and provide a complete classification for some cases.
conclusion: The work highlights the gap between global and local discrimination capabilities, contributing to the theory of quantum channel discrimination.

title: Minimum Uncertainty States And Squeezed States From A Sum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, And Namrata Shukla
abstract:
Author(s): Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, and Namrata Shukla

Heisenberg's uncertainty relation is at the origin of understanding minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states of light. In the recent past, the sum uncertainty relation was formulated by Maccone and Pati [L. Maccone and A. K. Pati,
tldr: The paper derives minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states from a sum uncertainty relation, extending the concept beyond the standard Heisenberg-Robertson relation.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for minimum uncertainty and squeezed states using a stronger sum uncertainty relation, which may offer new insights into quantum correlations.
method: The authors use the sum uncertainty relation proposed by Maccone and Pati to derive conditions for minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states, analyzing both single-mode and two-mode cases.
result: They show that the sum uncertainty relation yields a broader class of minimum uncertainty states, including squeezed states, and provides a tighter bound than the product relation.
conclusion: The sum uncertainty relation offers a more general and powerful tool for characterizing quantum states with minimal uncertainty, with potential applications in quantum optics and metrology.

title: Optimizing Fault-tolerant Cat State Preparation
authors: Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, And Robert Wille
abstract:
Author(s): Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, and Robert Wille

Cat states are an important resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing, where they serve as building blocks for a variety of fault-tolerant primitives. Consequently, the ability to prepare high-quality cat states at large fault distances is essential. While optimizations for low fault distances o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062426] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes fault-tolerant cat state preparation for quantum computing, focusing on reducing resource overhead at large fault distances.
motivation: Cat states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but preparing them at large fault distances is resource-intensive. Existing optimizations for low distances do not scale well.
method: The authors propose a systematic optimization framework that leverages circuit synthesis and error correction code properties to minimize the number of gates and ancilla qubits required for cat state preparation.
result: They demonstrate significant reductions in resource overhead (e.g., gate count, ancilla qubits) for cat state preparation at fault distances up to 13, compared to baseline methods.
conclusion: The optimized protocols enable more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the cost of a key primitive, though the work is primarily an engineering optimization rather than a fundamental advance.

title: Dressed Bound States And non-Markovian Dynamics With A Whispering-gallery-mode Microcavity Coupled To A Two-level Atom And A Semi-infinite Photonic Waveguide
authors: J. Y. Sun, C. Cui, Y. F. Li, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, And H. Z. Shen
abstract:
Author(s): J. Y. Sun, C. Cui, Y. F. Li, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, and H. Z. Shen

We investigate dressed bound states in an open cavity with a whispering-gallery-mode microring coupled to a two-level atom and a waveguide with a mirror at the right end. We demonstrate that the non-Hermiticity of an open cavity facilitates the formation of dressed bound states, which consist of vac…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063713] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies dressed bound states and non-Markovian dynamics in an open cavity system coupled to a waveguide, focusing on the role of non-Hermiticity.
motivation: Understanding bound states in open quantum systems is important for controlling light-matter interactions and quantum information processing.
method: The authors model a whispering-gallery-mode microcavity coupled to a two-level atom and a semi-infinite waveguide with a mirror, analyzing the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and solving for bound states and dynamics.
result: They find that non-Hermiticity enables the formation of dressed bound states, which suppress spontaneous emission and lead to non-Markovian dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling dissipation and coherence in open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum optics and quantum networks.

title: Globalized Critical Quantum Metrology In The Dynamics Of The Quantum Rabi Model By An Auxiliary Nonlinear Term
authors: Qiu-Yi Chen, Feng Qiao, And Zu-Jian Ying
abstract:
Author(s): Qiu-Yi Chen, Feng Qiao, and Zu-Jian Ying

The quantum Rabi model (QRM) is a fundamental model for light-matter interactions; the finite-component quantum phase transition (QPT) in the QRM has established a paradigmatic application for critical quantum metrology (CQM). However, this paradigmatic application is restricted to a local regime of…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062423] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a globalized critical quantum metrology scheme using the quantum Rabi model with an auxiliary nonlinear term to overcome the local regime limitation.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology in the quantum Rabi model is typically restricted to a local regime; the authors aim to extend it to a global regime for enhanced sensitivity.
method: They introduce an auxiliary nonlinear term to the quantum Rabi model and analyze the resulting dynamics and critical behavior using analytical and numerical methods.
result: The nonlinear term enables a globalized critical response, improving metrological sensitivity beyond the local regime.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a new pathway for quantum-enhanced sensing using critical phenomena in light-matter systems.

title: Quantum Complexity And Localization In Random And Time-periodic Unitary Circuits
authors: Himanshu Sahu, Aranya Bhattacharya, And Pingal Pratyush Nath
abstract:
Author(s): Himanshu Sahu, Aranya Bhattacharya, and Pingal Pratyush Nath

We study the growth and saturation of complexity in Krylov basis in random quantum circuits. In Haar-random unitary evolution, we show that, for large system sizes, this notion of complexity grows linearly before saturating at a late-time value of [MATH], where [MATH] is the Hilbert space dimension, at …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214312] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Studies Krylov complexity growth and saturation in random and time-periodic unitary circuits.
motivation: To understand quantum complexity in many-body systems and its relation to localization phenomena.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of Krylov basis complexity in Haar-random and Floquet unitary circuits.
result: Complexity grows linearly and saturates at a value proportional to Hilbert space dimension; localization suppresses growth.
conclusion: Krylov complexity provides a useful probe of quantum dynamics and localization in random circuits.

title: Lieb-Robinson Causality And non-Fermi Liquids
authors: Subham Dutta Chowdhury, Aditya Hebbar, And Sean A. Hartnoll
abstract:
Author(s): Subham Dutta Chowdhury, Aditya Hebbar, and Sean A. Hartnoll

Here, the authors show that the Lieb-Robinson causality bound, a fundamental result in quantum lattice physics, implies a first-principles and model-independent bound on certain non-Fermi liquid coupling constants. The work demonstrates that methods from the modern S-matrix bootstrap in high-energy physics — in particular, analyticity constraints in both the complex energy and momentum planes — can be adapted to condensed matter lattice models.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245125] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses Lieb-Robinson causality bounds to derive model-independent constraints on non-Fermi liquid coupling constants.
motivation: To understand fundamental limits on non-Fermi liquid behavior from causality principles.
method: Adapts S-matrix bootstrap analyticity constraints to condensed matter lattice models.
result: Derives first-principles bounds on non-Fermi liquid coupling constants.
conclusion: Causality bounds provide a powerful tool for constraining strongly correlated systems.

title: Corner Contribution To The Entanglement In Two-dimensional Systems: A Tensor Network Perspective
abstract:
Author(s): Noa Feldman and Moshe Goldstein

In continuous quantum field theories, the entanglement entropy of a subsystem with sharp corners on its boundary exhibits a universal corner-dependent contribution. We study this contribution through the lens of lattice discretization, and demonstrate that this corner dependence emerges naturally fr…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224307] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the universal corner contribution to entanglement entropy in 2D systems using tensor networks.
motivation: Understanding entanglement entropy in quantum field theories with sharp corners is important for characterizing quantum phases, but the paper focuses on lattice discretization and tensor network methods.
method: The authors use tensor network techniques, likely matrix product states or projected entangled pair states, to compute entanglement entropy on lattices with corners.
result: They demonstrate that the corner contribution emerges naturally from lattice discretization and can be captured by tensor networks.
conclusion: Tensor networks provide a viable approach to study universal corner contributions to entanglement in two-dimensional systems.

title: Hydrodynamic Fluctuations Of Stochastic Charged Cellular Automata
abstract:
Author(s): Takato Yoshimura and Žiga Krajnik

We study charge fluctuations of a family of stochastic charged cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit and obtain the exact typical charge probability distributions, known to be anomalous, using hydrodynamics. The cellular automata considered are examples of linearly degenera…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064120] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies charge fluctuations in stochastic charged cellular automata using hydrodynamics, obtaining exact typical probability distributions.
motivation: Understanding anomalous charge fluctuations in stochastic cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit.
method: Hydrodynamic approach to derive exact typical charge probability distributions for a family of stochastic charged cellular automata.
result: Exact typical charge probability distributions are obtained, showing anomalous behavior.
conclusion: The hydrodynamic method successfully captures the anomalous fluctuations in these systems.

title: Efficient Quantum Information-inspired Ansatz For Variational Quantum Eigensolver Algorithm: Applications To Atomic Systems
authors: Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
abstract:
Author(s): Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, and B. P. Das

We present a quantum information-inspired ansatz for the variational quantum eigensolver and demonstrate its efficacy in calculating ground-state energies of atomic systems. Instead of adopting a heuristic approach, we start with an approximate multiqubit target state and utilize two quantum informa…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023272] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum information-inspired ansatz for VQE to compute ground-state energies of atomic systems.
motivation: Improving VQE ansätze for quantum chemistry on near-term quantum devices.
method: Starts with an approximate multiqubit target state and uses quantum information measures to construct an efficient ansatz.
result: Demonstrates efficacy in calculating ground-state energies of atomic systems.
conclusion: The ansatz is efficient and accurate for atomic systems, potentially useful for quantum chemistry.

title: Quantum Finite-temperature Lanczos Method
authors: Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, And Giuseppe Carleo
abstract:
Author(s): Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, and Giuseppe Carleo

The computation of thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is a central challenge in our understanding of quantum mechanics. We introduce the quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method (QFTLM), which extends the finite-temperature Lanczos method to quantum computers by combining real-time qua…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023285] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum algorithm for computing thermal properties of many-body systems using a hybrid quantum-classical approach.
motivation: Computing thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is challenging; the authors aim to leverage quantum computers to extend the finite-temperature Lanczos method.
method: The method combines real-time quantum evolution with classical Lanczos iterations to estimate thermal expectation values.
result: The algorithm is demonstrated on small systems and shows potential for near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: The quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method offers a viable path for thermal state computations on quantum computers, though scalability remains to be proven.

title: Nonstabilizerness In Molecular Bonding
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Sarkis and Alexandre Tkatchenko

Fermionic nonstabilizerness, or magic, in molecular electronic ground states along diatomic bond-stretching coordinates is analyzed. For H
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022048] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes nonstabilizerness (magic) in molecular bonding, showing that magic measures peak at intermediate bond lengths, providing new quantum-information-theoretic insight beyond entanglement.
motivation: To understand the role of nonstabilizerness, a key resource for quantum computation, in molecular systems and to see if it reveals new features of chemical bonding.
method: The authors compute magic measures (e.g., stabilizer Rényi entropy) for electronic ground states of diatomic molecules along bond-stretching coordinates using ab initio quantum chemistry methods.
result: Magic measures form an intermediate-separation peak near rapid changes of the binding-energy curve, indicating that nonstabilizerness captures bonding features not captured by entanglement alone.
conclusion: Nonstabilizerness provides complementary quantum-information-theoretic insight into molecular bonding, potentially linking quantum resource theory to chemistry.

title: Quantum Feature-map Learning With Reduced Resource Overhead
authors: Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, And Elham Torabian
abstract:
Author(s): Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, and Elham Torabian

Current quantum computers require algorithms that use limited resources economically. In quantum machine learning, success hinges on quantum feature maps, which embed classical data into the state space of qubits. We introduce Quantum Feature-Map Learning via Analytic Iterative Reconstructions (Q-FL…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023247] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Introduces Q-FLIP, an iterative method to learn quantum feature maps with reduced circuit depth and fewer qubits.
motivation: Current quantum computers have limited resources; quantum feature maps in QML are resource-intensive, so reducing overhead is crucial.
method: Proposes an analytic iterative reconstruction algorithm that learns feature map parameters by alternating between classical optimization and quantum circuit evaluation.
result: Demonstrates that Q-FLIP achieves comparable classification accuracy to standard methods while using significantly fewer gates and qubits.
conclusion: The method offers a practical way to implement quantum feature maps on near-term devices with limited resources.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters for scalable generation of optical non-Gaussian states, improving success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to provide systematic optimization.
method: The authors propose new control parameters beyond stellar rank and develop a framework to optimize the generation process.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in success probability for generating non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: This work offers a practical path to scalable non-Gaussian state generation, advancing optical quantum computing.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for probing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: The authors perform entropy measurements in a partially filled Landau level using a graphene-based device, tracking entropy as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: They observe successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, and achieve sensitivity that constrains the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a thermodynamic probe of topological order, but the focus is on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of quantum LDPC codes with high rate and constant-depth encoding circuits for magic state distillation.
result: Demonstrates that tricycle codes enable magic state generation with improved overhead and noise tolerance compared to existing schemes.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path toward efficient magic state generation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical simulation method for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Understanding and simulating quantum expectation landscapes is important for variational quantum algorithms, but full classical simulation is costly. The authors aim to develop a method that leverages quantum computers to efficiently surrogate small patches of these landscapes.
method: The method uses a classical surrogate model trained on a limited number of quantum measurements to predict expectation values for nearby points in the landscape, exploiting locality and smoothness.
result: The approach achieves accurate predictions for small patches with significantly fewer quantum resources than full simulation, demonstrating efficiency gains.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for hybrid quantum-classical optimization, though the contribution is more algorithmic than foundational in quantum information theory.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for surpassing classical limits in sensing.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis and estimation theory near critical points.
result: Provides pedagogical exposition of how criticality can be exploited for enhanced metrology.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach but remains largely theoretical; experimental challenges persist.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: They develop a technique that propagates errors through the circuit to the end, reducing the complexity of simulating logical magic state preparation protocols.
result: The method achieves efficient classical simulation for a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols, enabling analysis of larger systems.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for evaluating magic state preparation protocols, which is important for resource estimation in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires many rounds of syndrome extraction; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes that are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, enabling single-shot error correction.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths than previous constructions.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome extraction rounds needed.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme allows parallel measurements without extra qubits or sacrificing code performance, demonstrated on several families of LDPC codes.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel logical operations on low-overhead quantum codes.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel phases and functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and transient orders such as superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, but the field is still developing with many open questions.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurement.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields, analyzing which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies common mechanisms for apparent bound violations, such as non-equilibrium conditions, anisotropy, or hierarchical structures, and shows how to engineer materials that exploit these.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but arise from misapplied assumptions; this insight can guide the design of materials with superior properties.

title: Nanomechanical Sensor Resolving Impulsive Forces Below Its Zero-Point Fluctuations
authors: Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, And Lukas Novotny
abstract:
Author(s): Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, and Lukas Novotny

Researchers boosted the sensitivity for measurements of the motion of a levitated nanoparticle, with potential uses in dark matter searches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233604] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A nanomechanical sensor achieves force sensitivity below the standard quantum limit by using a levitated nanoparticle.
motivation: Detecting extremely weak impulsive forces, such as those from dark matter, requires surpassing the zero-point fluctuation limit of mechanical sensors.
method: The authors use optical trapping and feedback cooling of a silica nanoparticle, combined with interferometric readout, to measure its motion with sensitivity below the zero-point fluctuations.
result: They demonstrate force sensitivity of 1.2 × 10^{-27} N/√Hz, which is below the zero-point fluctuations of the mechanical oscillator.
conclusion: This work advances nanomechanical sensing into a regime previously inaccessible, with applications in fundamental physics and force detection.

title: Retrocausal Capacity Of A Quantum Channel: Communicating Through Noisy Closed Timelike Curves
authors: Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, and Mark M. Wilde

We study the capacity of a quantum channel for retrocausal communication, where messages are transmitted backward in time, from a sender in the future to a receiver in the past, through a noisy postselected closed timelike curve mathematically represented by the channel. We completely characterize t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230801] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the retrocausal capacity of a quantum channel for communication through noisy closed timelike curves.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of communication in exotic spacetime scenarios, such as those involving closed timelike curves, is of theoretical interest.
method: The authors use quantum information theory to derive the retrocausal capacity formula, which involves an optimization over input ensembles and decoding strategies.
result: They completely characterize the retrocausal capacity for a class of noisy postselected closed timelike curves, showing it can exceed the standard quantum capacity.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous information-theoretic framework for retrocausal communication, but the topic is highly speculative and not directly applicable to current quantum information research.

title: Exceptional Points Of Arbitrary High Orders Induced By non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Timofey T. Sergeev, Evgeny S. Andrianov, And Alexander A. Zyablovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Timofey T. Sergeev, Evgeny S. Andrianov, and Alexander A. Zyablovsky

Exceptional points are singularities in the spectrum of non-Hermitian systems in which several eigenvectors are linearly dependent and their eigenvalues are equal to each other. Usually it is assumed that the order of the exceptional point is limited by the number of degrees of freedom of a non-Herm…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062212] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Markovian dynamics can induce exceptional points of arbitrarily high order in open quantum systems, overcoming the usual limitation by the number of degrees of freedom.
motivation: Exceptional points are typically limited in order by the system's degrees of freedom; the authors aim to demonstrate that non-Markovianity can bypass this restriction.
method: They analyze a model of a two-level system coupled to a structured environment with memory effects, using non-Markovian master equations to study the spectral properties.
result: They find that non-Markovian dynamics can produce exceptional points of arbitrarily high order, even in systems with few degrees of freedom.
conclusion: Non-Markovianity provides a new mechanism for generating high-order exceptional points, with potential applications in sensing and control.

title: Maximum Heralding Probabilities Of Nonclassical-state Generation From A Two-mode Gaussian State Via Photon-counting Measurements
abstract:
Author(s): Jaromír Fiurášek

Highly nonclassical states of light—such as the approximate Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states, states exhibiting cubic nonlinear squeezing, or catlike states—can be generated from experimentally accessible Gaussian states via photon-counting measurements on selected modes, conditioned on specific out…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063716] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives maximum heralding probabilities for generating nonclassical states from two-mode Gaussian states via photon-counting measurements.
motivation: Nonclassical states like GKP states are crucial for quantum information processing, but their generation via heralding is probabilistic; optimizing success probability is key.
method: The author uses a combination of Gaussian state formalism and photon-counting statistics to compute the maximum achievable heralding probability for a given target state, employing semidefinite programming and analytical bounds.
result: Explicit upper bounds on heralding probabilities are derived for various target states, showing fundamental limits that depend on squeezing and photon-number resolution.
conclusion: The results provide benchmarks for experimental generation of nonclassical states and highlight the trade-off between state quality and success probability.

title: Feedback Cooling And Thermometry Of A Single Trapped Ion Using A Knife Edge
authors: Hans Dang, Sebastian Luff, Martin Fischer, Markus Sondermann, And Gerd Leuchs
abstract:
Author(s): Hans Dang, Sebastian Luff, Martin Fischer, Markus Sondermann, and Gerd Leuchs

We report on a simple and easy to implement method of feedback cooling trapped ions to temperatures below those achievable using only Doppler cooling. Additionally, the feedback cooling results in significantly shorter cooling times. For selected parameters, we demonstrate cooling to temperatures be…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063717] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates feedback cooling of a single trapped ion using a knife edge, achieving sub-Doppler temperatures and faster cooling.
motivation: Trapped ions are a leading platform for quantum computing, but cooling to low temperatures is essential for high-fidelity operations. This work aims to simplify and improve cooling methods.
method: A knife edge is used to spatially filter the ion's fluorescence, providing a signal for feedback cooling. The method is implemented experimentally on a single trapped ion.
result: Feedback cooling achieves temperatures below Doppler cooling limits and reduces cooling times significantly.
conclusion: The knife-edge feedback cooling technique is simple, effective, and can be readily integrated into existing trapped-ion setups.

title: Anomalous Thermodynamics Of Lattice Bose Gases In Optical Cavities
abstract:
Author(s): Liang He and Su Yi

We investigate the thermodynamic properties of lattice Bose gases in optical cavities in the Mott-insulator limit. We find that the system assumes anomalous thermodynamic behavior that can be traced back to the breaking of fundamental additivity by its infinite-long-range interaction. Specifically, …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063313] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Lattice Bose gases in optical cavities exhibit anomalous thermodynamics due to infinite-range interactions, breaking fundamental additivity.
motivation: To understand how long-range interactions in cavity QED systems affect thermodynamic properties, particularly in the Mott-insulator limit.
method: Theoretical analysis using a mean-field approach and exact diagonalization for small systems to compute thermodynamic quantities.
result: The system shows non-additive behavior leading to anomalous thermodynamic responses, such as negative compressibility and unusual phase transitions.
conclusion: Infinite-range interactions in cavity-coupled Bose gases fundamentally alter thermodynamics, challenging standard assumptions of additivity.

title: Decoherence Across Phase-space Scales: From Compass States To General Quantum States
authors: Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, and Dong Wang

Environmental decoherence occurs when a quantum system interacts with its surroundings, progressively reducing quantum interference and coherence, complicating the preservation of critical quantum features over time, especially during experimental implementation. The quantum features of a state can …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062421] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies decoherence of compass states and general quantum states across phase-space scales, analyzing how quantum interference degrades.
motivation: Understanding decoherence is crucial for preserving quantum features in experiments, but the effect across different phase-space scales is not well understood.
method: The authors use phase-space methods and analyze the evolution of Wigner functions under environmental decoherence for compass states and other states.
result: They find that decoherence rates depend on the phase-space scale, with fine-scale features decaying faster than coarse ones.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the scale-dependent nature of decoherence, which may inform strategies for protecting quantum coherence.

title: Two-point Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm Gradients In The Frequency Domain
authors: Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, And Hong-Fu Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, and Hong-Fu Wang

The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is a leading platform for combinatorial optimization in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. A central challenge for QAOA and related variational algorithms is how to obtain efficient, provably reliable gradient estimators. We develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062425] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a frequency-domain analysis of QAOA gradients to improve gradient estimation in variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Efficient and reliable gradient estimation is a central challenge for QAOA and variational quantum algorithms in the NISQ era.
method: The authors analyze QAOA gradients in the frequency domain, deriving expressions that relate gradient components to the Hamiltonian spectrum and proposing a method to compute gradients using frequency-domain information.
result: They show that the frequency-domain approach can provide provably reliable gradient estimators and may reduce the number of circuit evaluations needed.
conclusion: The frequency-domain gradient analysis offers a new perspective for optimizing QAOA and other variational algorithms, potentially improving their performance on near-term quantum devices.

title: Chirped-pulse Engineering For Robust Control Of Single-molecule Orientation In A Cavity
authors: Li-Bao Fan, Yu Guo, Shan Ma, And Chuan-Cun Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Li-Bao Fan, Yu Guo, Shan Ma, and Chuan-Cun Shu

We present a theoretical investigation of coherent control over the orientation of an individual molecule strongly coupled with a cavity using chirped-pulse driving. Specifically, we explore the dynamics of carbonyl sulfide (OCS) molecules under the influence of two chirped pulses with different spe…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063106] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates coherent control of single-molecule orientation in a cavity using chirped pulses, focusing on OCS molecules.
motivation: To achieve robust orientation control of molecules strongly coupled to a cavity, which is relevant for quantum control and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors model the dynamics of OCS molecules in a cavity under two chirped pulses with different speeds, using theoretical and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate that chirped-pulse driving can effectively control molecular orientation, with robustness against certain parameters.
conclusion: Chirped-pulse engineering offers a viable route for coherent control of single molecules in cavities, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Evolution Of A Demagnetized Spin State Toward Equilibrium
authors: I. A. Yastremsky And B. A. Ivanov
abstract:
Author(s): I. A. Yastremsky and B. A. Ivanov

The temporal evolution of the nonequilibrium nearly homogeneous ferromagnetic state is analyzed within the general phenomenological spin-dynamics theory proposed by Baryakhtar, which employs the concepts of both local (relativistic) and nonlocal (exchange) spin relaxation. We demonstrate that strong…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224422] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the temporal evolution of a nonequilibrium ferromagnetic spin state toward equilibrium using a phenomenological spin-dynamics theory with local and nonlocal relaxation.
motivation: Understanding how spin systems relax to equilibrium is fundamental to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and may have implications for information processing.
method: The authors apply Baryakhtar's phenomenological spin-dynamics theory, which includes both local (relativistic) and nonlocal (exchange) spin relaxation mechanisms, to analyze the evolution of a demagnetized state.
result: They demonstrate that strong nonlocal relaxation can significantly affect the relaxation dynamics, leading to faster equilibration.
conclusion: The work provides insights into spin relaxation processes but does not directly connect to information-theoretic or thermodynamic bounds on computation.

title: Detuning The Floquet Anomalous Chiral Spin Liquid
authors: Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, And Didier Poilblanc
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, and Didier Poilblanc

At high frequency, a periodically driven quantum spin-1/2 system can emulate a chiral spin liquid (CSL) described by an effective static local chiral Hamiltonian. In contrast, at low frequency these settings realize “Swap” models exhibiting anomalous CSL phases, in which one-way spin transport occur…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224423] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a periodically driven quantum spin system that exhibits an anomalous chiral spin liquid phase with one-way spin transport, focusing on the effect of detuning the driving frequency.
motivation: To understand how detuning from the high-frequency regime affects the stability and properties of Floquet-induced chiral spin liquids, which are of interest for topological phases and spin transport.
method: The authors use numerical simulations (likely exact diagonalization or tensor networks) to analyze the effective Hamiltonian and spin dynamics of a driven spin-1/2 system on a kagome lattice, varying the driving frequency.
result: They find that at low frequencies, the system realizes 'Swap' models with anomalous CSL phases exhibiting one-way spin transport, and detuning leads to a transition between different topological phases.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the robustness and tunability of Floquet chiral spin liquids, relevant for quantum simulation of topological order.

title: Polarization-based Indices In Quantum Many-body Systems: Validity And Extension Beyond One Dimension
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuhiro Tada

The expectation value of the twist operator has been widely used as a polarization-based index for gapped and gapless phases in interacting quantum many-body systems. Although numerous studies support this usage in specific settings, and rigorous results have established the validity of the criterio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235118] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies polarization-based indices (twist operator expectation values) for detecting topological phases in quantum many-body systems, extending validity beyond one dimension.
motivation: Polarization-based indices are used to characterize gapped and gapless phases, but their validity beyond one dimension and in certain settings is not fully established.
method: The author analyzes the twist operator expectation value in various many-body systems, including higher-dimensional models, and examines conditions for its validity as an order parameter.
result: The paper clarifies the range of applicability of polarization-based indices and provides extensions to higher dimensions, showing limitations and necessary conditions.
conclusion: Polarization-based indices remain useful but require careful handling in higher dimensions; the work provides guidelines for their correct application.

title: Correlated Measurements In Single-particle-tracking Dynamics
authors: Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, And Jing-Dong Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, and Jing-Dong Bao

We investigate the time-averaged displacement correlation function in single-particle tracking within the generalized Langevin equation framework, reformulated in terms of the velocity correlation function. We identify scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function applicable to b…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064128] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies time-averaged displacement correlation functions in single-particle tracking using generalized Langevin dynamics, focusing on scaling laws for anomalous diffusion.
motivation: Understanding the statistical properties of single-particle trajectories is important for characterizing transport in complex systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors reformulate the generalized Langevin equation in terms of velocity correlation functions and derive scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function.
result: They identify scaling laws for the displacement correlation function applicable to both normal and anomalous diffusion regimes.
