conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for analyzing correlated measurements in single-particle tracking, but it is purely classical and does not address quantum or thermodynamic aspects.

title: Resetting Of Underdamped Brownian Motion
authors: Hanna Franke And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Franke and Igor M. Sokolov

We study underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting, where we apply two different full resetting procedures. The first one resets both position and velocity to zero, while the second one resets the displacement to zero but takes the velocity after resetting to follow a Maxwell distributi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064125] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting with two different resetting protocols, analyzing the resulting non-equilibrium steady states.
motivation: To understand the effect of resetting on underdamped systems, which are more realistic than overdamped approximations, and to explore how different resetting procedures influence the steady-state properties.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation for underdamped Brownian motion with Poissonian resetting, considering two protocols: full resetting of position and velocity to zero, and resetting position to zero while randomizing velocity according to a Maxwell distribution.
result: They derive exact expressions for the stationary probability distributions in position and velocity, and show that the two resetting protocols lead to qualitatively different steady states, with the second protocol yielding a Maxwellian velocity distribution.
conclusion: The work provides a complete analytical treatment of resetting in underdamped systems, highlighting the importance of the resetting protocol on the resulting non-equilibrium behavior.

title: Boundary-induced Drift And Negative Mobility In Constrained Stochastic Systems
abstract:
Author(s): Meitar Goldfarb and Stanislav Burov

We study overdamped stochastic dynamics confined by hard reflecting boundaries and show that the combination of boundary geometry and an anisotropic diffusion tensor generically generates directed motion. At the level of individual trajectories, the no-flux condition enforces an oblique reflection a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064119] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Boundary geometry and anisotropic diffusion in overdamped stochastic systems can generate directed motion and negative mobility.
motivation: To understand how hard reflecting boundaries and anisotropic diffusion can induce directed motion without external bias, and to explore the phenomenon of negative mobility.
method: The authors study overdamped Langevin dynamics with hard reflecting boundaries and an anisotropic diffusion tensor, deriving the no-flux condition and analyzing trajectory behavior.
result: They show that boundary geometry combined with anisotropic diffusion generically produces directed motion, and in certain cases leads to negative mobility (motion opposite to an applied force).
conclusion: Boundary-induced drift is a generic effect in constrained stochastic systems, with potential implications for transport in confined geometries.

title: Cellular Automata In $d$ Dimensions And Ground States Of Spin Models In $(d+1)$ Dimensions
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, and Juan P. Garrahan

We show how the trajectories of [MATH]-dimensional cellular automata (CA) can be used to systematically construct the ground states of [MATH]-dimensional classical spin models, and we characterize their quantum phase transition, when in the presence of a transverse magnetic field. For each of the 256 …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064112] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models from d-dimensional cellular automata trajectories and studies their quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To establish a systematic connection between cellular automata and classical spin models, enabling the study of quantum phase transitions in the resulting systems.
method: The authors use trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata to define ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models, then add a transverse field to study quantum phase transitions.
result: They characterize the quantum phase transitions for all 256 elementary cellular automata rules, showing that the critical behavior is determined by the CA rule.
conclusion: Cellular automata provide a useful tool for constructing classical spin models with tunable quantum phase transitions, linking computation and statistical mechanics.

title: Polarization Symmetry As A Signature Of Bell States In Compton Scattering
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Caradonna and Kenji Shimazoe

We analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry at energies where polarization must be inferred from Compton scattering. Polarization symmetry, defined as equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles, holds if and only if the initial t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023288] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that polarization symmetry in Compton scattering can serve as a signature of Bell states, enabling entanglement certification without direct polarization measurements.
motivation: To certify entanglement in high-energy photon pairs where standard polarization measurements are impractical, using Compton scattering as a proxy.
method: The authors analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry, deriving conditions under which polarization symmetry (equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses) holds if and only if the initial two-photon state is a Bell state.
result: Polarization symmetry is a necessary and sufficient condition for the state to be a Bell state, providing a practical entanglement witness for high-energy photons.
conclusion: This work offers a new method for entanglement certification in Compton scattering experiments, relevant for quantum information applications at high energies.

title: Liouvillian Topology And Nonreciprocal Dynamics In Open Floquet Chains
authors: Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, and Jan Carl Budich

Open quantum systems far from thermal equilibrium can exhibit remarkable physical phenomena including topological properties without a direct equilibrium counterpart. Along these lines, in periodically driven-dissipative systems within the effective non-Hermitian (NH) Hamiltonian approximation spect…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023270] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological properties and nonreciprocal dynamics in open Floquet chains using a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian approach.
motivation: To explore topological phenomena in open quantum systems far from equilibrium, specifically in periodically driven-dissipative systems.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional driven-dissipative chain using the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approximation and compute topological invariants.
result: They identify nontrivial Liouvillian topology and nonreciprocal transport effects in the open Floquet system.
conclusion: The work reveals that open Floquet systems can host topological phases without equilibrium counterparts, extending the concept of topology to non-equilibrium settings.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents symmetry-accelerated classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits using optimal stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Efficient classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verifying quantum computers, especially when circuits are dominated by Clifford gates.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetry reductions to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries, enabling faster classical simulation.
result: They demonstrate that symmetry reductions significantly improve the scalability of stabilizer-based simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for simulating near-Clifford circuits, which is relevant for quantum advantage experiments but does not directly advance core quantum information theory.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based computation to cancel T gates.
result: The proposed relation enables significant reduction in T-count compared to standard methods.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for T-count optimization, contributing to more efficient fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to accelerate simulations.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables in frequency space, capturing temporal correlations.
result: The method accurately predicts Floquet Hamiltonians, observable dynamics, and operator growth beyond the training time window.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and extrapolatable surrogate model for time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, likely using numerical simulations or analytical models.
result: They provide a framework to evaluate how interactions affect the topological protection and spatial extent of Majorana modes.
conclusion: The work offers tools to identify truly robust Majorana bound states, guiding experimental efforts toward non-Abelian braiding.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities in spectral analysis.
motivation: Efficient spectral analysis of large matrices is important for quantum many-body physics and quantum computing, but worst-case complexity is high.
method: The algorithm uses quantum filtering techniques to detect clusters of eigenvalues and estimate their multiplicities with reduced query complexity.
result: The algorithm achieves efficiency beyond worst-case complexity for certain spectral properties.
conclusion: The work provides a quantum algorithm for spectral analysis, but its connection to core quantum information topics like entanglement or cryptography is indirect.

title: Simulating Quantum Circuits With Arbitrary Local Noise Using Pauli Propagation
authors: Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, and Zoë Holmes

Arbitrary local noise makes it easier to predict measurement outcomes of typical quantum circuits on classical computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: Shows that arbitrary local noise makes quantum circuits classically simulable via Pauli propagation.
motivation: Understanding when quantum circuits become classically simulable is crucial for identifying the boundary of quantum advantage.
method: Uses Pauli propagation to simulate noisy quantum circuits, analyzing the effect of arbitrary local noise on measurement outcomes.
result: Arbitrary local noise enables efficient classical simulation of typical quantum circuits.
conclusion: Noise can be a resource for classical simulability, which has implications for quantum advantage claims.

title: Variational Processing Of Multimode Squeezed Light
authors: Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, And Shanhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, and Shanhui Fan

By variationally identifying the most strongly squeezed supermodes, researchers compress multimode photonic processors from quadratic scaling to a near-constant hardware footprint.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020311] Published Mon Apr 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational method to compress multimode photonic processors by identifying the most squeezed supermodes, reducing hardware scaling from quadratic to near-constant.
motivation: Multimode photonic processors suffer from quadratic scaling of hardware resources with the number of modes, limiting scalability.
method: The authors propose a variational approach to find the most strongly squeezed supermodes in a multimode squeezed light source, enabling compression of the processor.
result: The method achieves near-constant hardware footprint regardless of the number of modes, significantly reducing resource requirements.
conclusion: Variational identification of squeezed supermodes offers a practical path to scalable multimode photonic quantum information processing.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are diverse and fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: They show how these methods provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions, fluctuations, and large deviations.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Symmetry-induced Logarithmic Relaxation In The Quantum Kicked Rotor
authors: Julien Hébraud, Floriane Arrouas, Bruno Peaudecerf, Juliette Billy, David Guéry-Odelin, Olivier Giraud, Bertrand Georgeot, Gabriel Lemarié And Christian Miniatura
abstract: We study the effect of discrete symmetries on coherent multiple scattering in the quantum kicked rotor. When the initial momentum is set to zero—as in recent Bose–Einstein condensate experiments—the effective pseudo-disorder becomes even under momentum inversion. The resulting discrete mirror symmetry of the dynamics profoundly alters spectral correlations: it generates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets localised at opposite momenta, whose exponentially small splittings produce a hierarchy of exponentially large dynamical timescales. The coherent backscattering and forward-scattering peaks then exhibit a striking non-monotonic evolution and strongly asymmetric contrasts, followed by an exceptionally slow logarithmic relaxation toward a common asymptotic value—a hallmark of glassy dynamics, here emerging in a fully coherent quantum system. That such archetypal glass-like behaviour arises from a single discrete symmetry constraint reveals an unexpected and deep connection between quantum coherence and slow relaxation phenomena.
tldr: Discrete mirror symmetry in the quantum kicked rotor leads to exponentially long timescales and logarithmic relaxation, resembling glassy dynamics.
motivation: To understand how discrete symmetries affect coherent multiple scattering and spectral correlations in a paradigmatic quantum chaotic system.
method: Analytical and numerical study of the quantum kicked rotor with a mirror symmetry, analyzing Floquet quasienergies, eigenstates, and dynamical observables like coherent backscattering.
result: Mirror symmetry creates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets with exponentially small splittings, producing a hierarchy of timescales and a logarithmic relaxation of coherent peaks.
conclusion: A single discrete symmetry can induce glassy relaxation in a fully coherent quantum system, revealing a deep link between symmetry and slow dynamics.

title: Nonequilibrium Dimension-raising Phase Transitions
abstract: We propose a periodically driven system whose dimensionality is an emergent property that can be tunable, thus enables us to realize not only many-body phases with arbitrary dimensions, but also phase transitions, instead of crossovers, between phases with various dimensions. We study an interacting rotor model whose instantaneous Hamiltonian keeps the one-dimensional feature at any given time. Despite this, an emergent two-dimensional (2D) phase appears when the driving frequency exceeds a critical value, at which a dimension-raising phase transition takes place. We find that the nonequilibrium feature of the system could qualitatively change the finite temperature critical behavior of the emergent 2D phase and make it different from its equilibrium counterpart. A four-dimensional generalization and experimental realizations of the proposed model based on a programmable reconfiguration technique in optical tweezers setups have also been discussed.
tldr: A periodically driven system exhibits dimension-raising phase transitions where the effective dimensionality emerges from driving frequency, with nonequilibrium effects altering critical behavior.
motivation: To explore phase transitions between phases of different dimensionality in driven systems, which are typically crossovers rather than sharp transitions.
method: The authors study an interacting rotor model with a time-dependent Hamiltonian that is one-dimensional at any instant, but under periodic driving an emergent 2D phase appears above a critical frequency. They analyze the finite-temperature critical behavior and generalize to 4D.
result: A dimension-raising phase transition occurs at a critical driving frequency, and the nonequilibrium nature qualitatively changes the finite-temperature critical behavior compared to equilibrium 2D phases.
conclusion: Periodic driving can induce sharp phase transitions between phases of different dimensionality, offering a new route to realize and study higher-dimensional phases in lower-dimensional setups.

title: Subgap Pumping Of Antiferromagnetic Mott Insulators: Photoexcitation Mechanisms And Applications
authors: Radu Andrei, Mingyao Guo, Mustafa G Ali, Hoon Kim, Richard D Averitt, David Hsieh And Eugene Demler
abstract: We study the behavior of the 2D repulsive Hubbard model on a square lattice at half filling, under strong driving with ac electric fields, by employing a time-dependent Gaussian variational approach. Within the same theoretical framework, we analytically obtain the conventional Keldysh crossover between multiphoton and tunneling photoexcitation mechanisms, as well as two new regimes beyond the Keldysh paradigm. We discuss how dynamical renormalization of the Mott–Hubbard gap feeds back into the photoexcitation process, modulating the carrier generation rate in real time. The momentum distribution of quasiparticle excitations immediately after the drive is calculated, and shown to contain valuable information about the generation mechanism. Finally, we discuss experimental probing of the pump-induced nonequilibrium electronic state.
tldr: This paper studies photoexcitation mechanisms in antiferromagnetic Mott insulators under strong ac driving, revealing new regimes beyond the Keldysh crossover.
motivation: Understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems is important for both fundamental physics and potential applications in ultrafast control of materials.
method: The authors use a time-dependent Gaussian variational approach to analyze the 2D repulsive Hubbard model at half filling under strong ac electric fields.
result: They analytically derive the conventional Keldysh crossover and identify two new photoexcitation regimes, showing that dynamical renormalization of the Mott gap modulates carrier generation in real time.
conclusion: The momentum distribution of quasiparticle excitations contains information about the generation mechanism, and the pump-induced non-equilibrium state can be probed experimentally.

title: Quantum Entanglement, Stratified Spaces, And Topological Matter: Towards Entanglement-sensitive Langlands Data
abstract: Using the spinless Haldane model, we study the witness-filtered Berry curvature, quantum geometric tensor, and quantum Fisher information on the gapped strata of the parameter space and evaluate them through the Fukui–Hatsugai–Suzuki discretization. The filtered quantities isolate the part of the geometric response carried by sublattice coherence: they suppress contributions from regions where the occupied Bloch state is locally A/B-separable and emphasize regions where curvature and coherence coexist. We derive exact lattice identities, reconstruction formulas for the curvature-weighted coherence, and bounds relating the filtered quantum geometric tensor and quantum Fisher information to single-particle mode entanglement. Across the gap-closing stratum, the quantized response changes admit a natural description in terms of Hecke modifications. We elicit a corresponding Langlands viewpoint—not as a full correspondence, but as an organizational principle and as the mathematical shadow of these physical geometric constructions.
tldr: The paper uses geometric quantities from the Haldane model to study entanglement and connects them to Langlands theory, but the connection to quantum information is indirect and the focus is on topological matter.
motivation: To understand how quantum entanglement manifests in topological phases and to explore a potential link between physical geometric constructions and Langlands duality.
method: The authors compute witness-filtered Berry curvature, quantum geometric tensor, and quantum Fisher information on gapped strata of the parameter space using the Fukui–Hatsugai–Suzuki discretization.
result: They derive exact lattice identities and bounds relating filtered geometric quantities to single-particle mode entanglement, and observe that quantized response changes across gap-closing strata admit a description in terms of Hecke modifications.
conclusion: The work suggests a Langlands viewpoint as an organizational principle for these geometric constructions, but does not establish a full correspondence or provide direct quantum information applications.

motivation: To understand how geometry-induced quantum phase separation affects the validity of the thermodynamic limit in quantum spin and dimer models.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific domain shapes and analyze the ground state properties using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that the shape of the domain can fundamentally change the macroscopic ground state, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin and dimer models due to geometry-induced phase separation.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a pedagogical overview of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The paper reviews the concept of space-time duality in lattice systems, treating space and time on equal footing, and its connection to brickwork quantum circuits.
result: It presents a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems, highlighting exactly solvable models and the analogy with quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuit theory.

title: Optimizing Qubo On A Quantum Computer By Mimicking Imaginary Time Evolution
authors: Yahui Chai And Alice Di Tucci
abstract: We propose a hybrid quantum–classical algorithm for solving quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems using an imaginary time evolution-mimicking circuit (ITEMC). The circuit parameters are optimized to mimic short-time ITE, using only single- and two-qubit expectation values. This significantly reduces the measurement overhead by avoiding full energy evaluation. By updating the initial state based on results from last step iteratively, the algorithm quickly converges to the low-energy solutions. With a pre-sorting step that optimizes quantum gate ordering based on QUBO coefficients, the convergence is further improved. Our classical simulations achieve approximation ratios above up to 150 qubits. Furthermore, the linear scaling of entanglement entropy with system size suggests that the circuit is challenging to simulate classically using tensor networks. We also demonstrate hardware runs on IBM’s device for 40, 60, and 80 qubits, and obtain solutions compatible with that from simulated annealing.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for solving QUBO problems using a circuit that mimics imaginary time evolution.
motivation: QUBO problems are important for combinatorial optimization, but current quantum algorithms face measurement overhead and convergence issues.
method: The algorithm optimizes circuit parameters to mimic short-time imaginary time evolution using only single- and two-qubit expectation values, and iteratively updates the initial state with a pre-sorting step for gate ordering.
result: Classical simulations achieve high approximation ratios up to 150 qubits, and hardware runs on IBM devices for up to 80 qubits yield solutions comparable to simulated annealing.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm reduces measurement overhead and converges quickly, but its primary contribution is to optimization rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Percolation With Coupled Lasers: Effect Of Non-linearities On The Phase Transition
authors: Simon Mahler, Nikita Stroev, Mahmoud Abu Rmilah, Asher Friesem And Nir Davidson
abstract: Controlled experimental studies of percolation are challenging due to difficulties in tuning site connectivity, isolating local interactions, and mitigating finite-size effects. In this work, we experimentally investigate percolation with a platform of coupled lasers, where connectivity, interaction strength, and system size can be controlled. Using a square array of lasers with astronomical number of possible cluster configurations, we show that the emergence of a percolating cluster corresponds to the onset of phase locking among the lasers. We also show that the percolation probability undergoes a second-order alike transition as a function of the site-occupation probability, with a threshold consistent with classical theoretical predictions. Surprisingly, we find that at low pump level, amplified mode competition (nonlinear regime) alters the effective behavior of the lasing sites and modify the nature of the percolation transition. The experimental results are interpreted by the means of a theoretical toy model with connectivity rules to the classical percolation.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies percolation using a coupled laser array, showing that the percolation transition corresponds to phase locking and that nonlinearities alter the transition.
motivation: Controlled experimental studies of percolation are difficult; coupled lasers offer tunable connectivity and system size to investigate percolation phenomena.
method: A square array of coupled lasers with controllable site-occupation probability and pump levels is used to observe percolation and phase locking, with a toy model to interpret results.
result: Percolation probability undergoes a second-order-like transition consistent with classical percolation, but nonlinearities at low pump levels modify the transition.
conclusion: Coupled lasers provide a versatile platform for studying percolation, and nonlinear effects can alter the phase transition behavior.

title: Hybrid Monte Carlo For Fractional Quantum Hall States
authors: Ting-Tung Wang, Ha Quang Trung, Qianhui Xu, Min Long, Bo Yang And Zi Yang Meng
abstract: We develop a hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) method to efficiently compute the physical observables from the samplings of the Laughlin and the Moore–Read (MR) wave functions of fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems. With the advancements in methodology, including global updates and double stereographic projection on spherical geometry, our HMC simulation is significantly faster than the widely used Metropolis Monte Carlo scheme. As a result, we can readily simulate systems with electron numbers on both disk and sphere geometries. We apply this method to investigate the topological shift obtained from the edge dipole moment, computed from the wave function density on the disk. We also numerically computed the non-Abelian braiding matrices for different braiding schemes of the MR quasiholes on the sphere. Results with much better quality compared with previous works have been achieved. With the thermodynamic limit results obtained at ease, we also discuss the future usage of our method to clarify the questions on the instability of FQH states in an ideal Chern band setting or under quantum decoherence.
tldr: Develops a hybrid Monte Carlo method for simulating fractional quantum Hall wave functions, focusing on computational efficiency and topological properties.
motivation: Efficiently compute observables from Laughlin and Moore-Read wave functions for large systems, overcoming limitations of standard Metropolis Monte Carlo.
method: Uses hybrid Monte Carlo with global updates and double stereographic projection on spherical geometry to sample FQH wave functions.
result: Achieves significantly faster simulations, enabling computation of topological shift and non-Abelian braiding matrices with improved quality.
conclusion: The method facilitates thermodynamic limit studies and can address questions about FQH state stability in Chern bands or under decoherence.

title: Spinon Mediation Of Witness Spin Dynamics In Herbertsmithite
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 10 June 2026;
tldr: This paper uses impurity spins to probe the spin liquid phase in herbertsmithite, focusing on spinon-mediated dynamics.
motivation: To find definitive experimental evidence for a quantum spin liquid ground state in herbertsmithite, which has been elusive.
method: Impurity spins are introduced as local probes, and their dynamics are measured to infer properties of the spin liquid, likely via spinon interactions.
result: The study provides evidence of spinon-mediated spin dynamics, supporting the existence of a spin liquid phase.
conclusion: Impurity spins can serve as effective probes of quantum spin liquids, offering a new experimental approach.

title: Crossover Of Quasi-localized Dynamics And Diffusion In Supercooled Liquids
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the crossover between quasi-localized dynamics and diffusion in supercooled liquids using time-domain interferometry.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic dynamics of glass-forming liquids is crucial for explaining the glass transition and the nature of supercooled states.
method: Time-domain interferometry experiments were performed on a typical glass former to probe both fast localized motions and slower diffusive dynamics.
result: The two dynamical processes are found to be coupled, showing a crossover from quasi-localized to diffusive behavior.
conclusion: The coupling between fast and slow dynamics provides new insight into the relaxation mechanisms in supercooled liquids.

title: Bilayer Excitons In The Laughlin Fractional Quantum Hall State
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the observation of excitons formed between fractionally charged quasiparticles in a bilayer graphene fractional quantum Hall state.
motivation: To study interlayer correlations and excitonic bound states in fractional quantum Hall systems, which are fundamental to understanding strongly correlated topological phases.
method: The authors use a bilayer graphene device and perform transport measurements to detect signatures of excitons formed between Laughlin quasiparticles.
result: They observe evidence for bilayer excitons in the Laughlin fractional quantum Hall state, demonstrating interlayer pairing of fractionally charged quasiparticles.
conclusion: The work reveals a new type of excitonic state in fractional quantum Hall systems, expanding the understanding of composite particles in topological phases.

title: Superconductivity On Two Surfaces
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: Superconductivity observed in rhombohedral multilayer graphene with electrons and holes on opposite surfaces.
motivation: To explore unconventional superconductivity in a two-surface system within graphene.
method: Experimental study of rhombohedral multilayer graphene, measuring transport properties.
result: Superconductivity emerges from a normal state with electrons and holes on opposite surfaces.
conclusion: The two-surface geometry provides a new platform for studying superconductivity.

title: Attosecond Tuning Of Coherent Electron Dynamics In Doped Semiconductors
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 12 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates attosecond-scale control of coherent electron dynamics in doped germanium for petahertz electronics.
motivation: To achieve ultrafast light-field control in semiconductors for future petahertz information processing.
method: Experimental demonstration of sub-cycle manipulation of electron dynamics in doped germanium using attosecond light pulses.
result: Establishes doping as a viable route towards petahertz electronics and lightwave information processing.
conclusion: Doping enables attosecond tuning of coherent dynamics, advancing ultrafast optoelectronics.

title: Watching Ionization In A New Light
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: MeV electron pulses induce strong modulation in optical transmission of semiconductors, enabling room-temperature detection of ionizing radiation with sub-10-ps timing precision.
motivation: To develop a new method for detecting ionizing radiation with high temporal resolution at room temperature, potentially improving medical imaging and radiation diagnostics.
method: Experimental study using MeV electron pulses to irradiate common semiconductors and measuring the resulting modulation in optical transmission.
result: Observation of surprisingly strong modulation in optical transmission, enabling sub-10-ps timing precision for radiation detection at room temperature.
conclusion: The findings could lead to next-generation medical imaging and radiation diagnostics.

title: Is Ball Lightning A Relativistic Soliton?
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes that ball lightning may be explained by relativistic solitons, supported by high-power laser experiments producing millimeter-scale solitons.
motivation: Ball lightning is a poorly understood natural phenomenon; the paper aims to test whether relativistic solitons could be responsible.
method: High-power laser experiments are used to generate and study relativistic solitons, comparing their properties to ball lightning observations.
result: Millimeter-scale relativistic solitons were produced, suggesting they could explain ball lightning.
conclusion: Relativistic solitons are a plausible explanation for ball lightning, warranting further investigation.

title: Chaotic Photonics In Microresonators
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 May 2026;
tldr: A review of chaotic dynamics in microresonator photonics, covering various materials and architectures.
motivation: To survey how chaos in photonic microcavities can be harnessed for technological and scientific applications.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical work on chaotic microcavities, including ray and wave chaos, mode coupling, and nonlinear effects.
result: Chaotic photonics enables novel functionalities such as broadband light generation, sensing, and random lasing.
conclusion: Chaos is a valuable resource in photonics, offering new opportunities for device design and fundamental studies.

title: Generation Of Ultra-broadband Frequency Comb In Strongly Bistable Nonlinear Magnonic Resonator
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates an ultra-broadband magnonic frequency comb generated by driving a nonlinear YIG resonator far off-resonance, producing over 350 comb lines across 450 MHz with tunable spacing.
motivation: To achieve broadband frequency combs in the magnonic domain for potential applications in signal processing and metrology.
method: A strongly bistable nonlinear magnonic resonator (YIG) is driven far off-resonance, exploiting nonlinear dynamics to generate a dense frequency comb.
result: Over 350 comb lines spanning 450 MHz with continuously tunable line spacing are observed.
conclusion: The approach offers a new route to ultra-broadband magnonic frequency combs, which may be useful for microwave photonics and magnon-based information processing.

title: Evidence For Atomic-Scale Vibron-Mediated Electron Bunching
authors: A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, And F. Massee

motivation: To understand electron transport at the atomic scale and the role of vibrational excitations.
method: Atomic-scale measurements using scanning tunneling microscopy or similar techniques.
result: Observation of electron bunching mediated by vibrational excitations.
conclusion: Vibrational excitations can induce correlated electron motion at the atomic scale.

The phase of spins in the quasi-two-dimensional (q2D) XY model has emerged as a topic of significant interest across multiple subfields of physics. Conventional wisdom, rooted in the Mermin-Wagner theorem and supported by existing paradigms, asserts that true long-range (LR) order is prohibited in q…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237101] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies long-range order in a quasi-2D XY model with short-range interactions, challenging the Mermin-Wagner theorem.
motivation: To understand whether true long-range order can exist in quasi-2D systems despite the Mermin-Wagner theorem prohibiting it in strictly 2D.
method: Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analysis of the quasi-2D XY model.
result: They find evidence of long-range order at finite temperature, which is unexpected for a strictly short-range quasi-2D system.
conclusion: Critical fluctuations can stabilize long-range order in quasi-2D XY models, revising conventional understanding.

authors: Duilio de Santis, Alex Gómez-Salvador, Nataliia Bazhan, Sebastian Erne, Maximilian Prüfer, Claudio Guarcello, Davide Valenti, Jörg Schmiedmayer, And Eugene Demler

Emergent collective excitations constitute a hallmark of interacting quantum many-body systems, yet in solid-state platforms their study has been largely limited by the constraints of linear-response probes and by finite momentum resolution. We propose to overcome these limitations by combining the …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233401] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes momentum-resolved two-dimensional spectroscopy to probe nonlinear quantum field dynamics in ultracold atomic gases.
motivation: Linear-response probes and finite momentum resolution limit the study of emergent collective excitations in quantum many-body systems.
method: Combines two-dimensional spectroscopy with momentum resolution, using a series of Bragg pulses to excite and probe nonlinear responses.
result: The method enables extraction of nonlinear response functions and reveals signatures of quantum field dynamics beyond linear response.
conclusion: Momentum-resolved 2D spectroscopy is a powerful tool for exploring nonlinear quantum many-body phenomena.

title: Efimov Effect In Ultracold Microwave-Shielded Polar Molecules
authors: Shayamal Singh And Chris H. Greene
abstract:
Author(s): Shayamal Singh and Chris H. Greene

A quantum-mechanical description is presented for the three-body physics of shielded dipolar molecules, including a prediction of observable Efimov physics. Despite the anisotropic and long-range nature of the interaction, shielding enables a regime in which universality emerges already at the two-b…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233402] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts Efimov physics in ultracold microwave-shielded polar molecules, focusing on three-body bound states.
motivation: Understanding three-body physics in dipolar systems is important for ultracold chemistry and quantum simulation, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Quantum-mechanical calculations of three-body bound states using a model potential for shielded dipolar interactions.
result: Prediction of observable Efimov resonances in microwave-shielded polar molecules.
conclusion: Efimov physics can be realized in ultracold polar molecules with microwave shielding, enabling studies of universal three-body phenomena.

title: Proper Theory Of Magnon Orbital Angular Momentum At Equilibrium
abstract:
Author(s): Junyu Tang and Ran Cheng

The orbital motion of chargeless bosons, unlike that of electrons, does not generate a magnetic moment and thus cannot directly interact with magnetic fields. To formulate the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of magnons, we first identify its proper conjugate variable by considering the Aharonov-Cashe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236702] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for magnon orbital angular momentum at equilibrium, identifying its conjugate variable and deriving a continuity equation.
motivation: Magnons are chargeless bosons whose orbital angular momentum does not couple to magnetic fields, making its formulation non-trivial. The authors aim to provide a proper theoretical description.
method: The authors consider the Aharonov-Casher effect to identify the conjugate variable of magnon OAM and derive a continuity equation for OAM density.
result: They establish a consistent theory of magnon OAM at equilibrium, showing that it is a well-defined quantity with a corresponding conservation law.
conclusion: The work clarifies the nature of magnon OAM and provides a foundation for future studies of orbital dynamics in magnetic systems.

title: Topological Transition And Emergence Of Elasticity Of Dislocation In Skyrmion Lattice: Beyond Kittel’s Magnetic-Polar Analogy
authors: Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, And Takahiro Shimada
abstract:
Author(s): Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, and Takahiro Shimada

Skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures possessing large skyrmion deformation and topological phase transitions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236703] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological transitions and elasticity of dislocations in skyrmion lattices, extending beyond Kittel's magnetic-polar analogy.
motivation: Understanding the mechanical properties and topological transitions of skyrmion dislocations is important for spintronic applications, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze the core structure and elastic properties of skyrmion dislocations, revealing a topological phase transition.
result: They find that skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures with large deformation and undergo a topological phase transition, leading to emergent elasticity.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into skyrmion lattice mechanics but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Lorentz Violation In Emergent Gravity And Its Cosmological Consequences
abstract:
Author(s): Raymond Isichei and João Magueijo

We show that general relativity and other geometrical theories can be viewed as a degenerate Otto cycle with only heat-exchange legs in emergent gravity. Including work-producing legs yields controlled violations of local Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation, which produce late-time c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231501] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper interprets general relativity as a degenerate Otto cycle in emergent gravity, leading to Lorentz violation and late-time cosmological acceleration.
motivation: To explore the connection between emergent gravity and thermodynamics, and to derive observable consequences of Lorentz violation.
method: The authors model gravity as an emergent phenomenon using a thermodynamic cycle analogy, specifically an Otto cycle, and introduce work-producing legs to break Lorentz invariance.
result: They find that controlled violations of local Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation emerge, producing late-time cosmic acceleration without dark energy.
conclusion: The framework provides a novel thermodynamic perspective on gravity and offers a potential explanation for dark energy through Lorentz violation.

title: Nanoscale Coherent Phonons With Broadband Frequency Tunability
authors: Zhengpu Zhao (赵正朴), Da Wu (吴达), Chuwei Zhang (张楚惟), Duanyun Cao (曹端云), Haotian Zheng (郑浩天), Yuqing Huang (黄玉清), Qin Wang (王钦), En-Ge Wang (王恩哥), Chaoyu Guo (郭钞宇), And Ying Jiang

motivation: To enable nanoscale investigation of optical, electronic, thermodynamic, and mechanical properties of functional materials using tunable coherent phonons.
method: The authors develop coherent phonon tips that can be tuned over a broad frequency range and use them to probe materials at the nanoscale.
result: They achieve broadband frequency tunability of coherent phonons at the nanoscale, enabling versatile probing of material properties.
conclusion: The technique provides a new tool for nanoscale characterization of functional materials.

title: Chiral Spin Liquid Instability Of The Kitaev Honeycomb Model With Crystallographic Defects
authors: Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, And Itamar Kimchi
abstract:

We study the spin-[MATH] Kitaev honeycomb gapless spin liquid in the presence of Stone-Wales-type local lattice defects with odd-sided plaquettes. While the clean Kitaev model has no finite-temperature phase transitions, we find that introducing a finite defect density [MATH] p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236704] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of Stone-Wales defects on the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid, finding a finite-temperature chiral spin liquid phase induced by defects.
motivation: The Kitaev model is a paradigmatic exactly solvable spin liquid, but real materials have defects; understanding their effect is crucial for experimental realization.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical arguments and numerical simulations (likely exact diagonalization or tensor networks) to study the Kitaev model with Stone-Wales defects.
result: A finite density of defects drives a finite-temperature phase transition into a chiral spin liquid phase, which is absent in the clean model.
conclusion: Defects can stabilize chiral spin liquids at finite temperature, offering a route to realize these exotic phases in candidate materials.

title: Enhanced Optical Bistability In Conjugate Topological Photonic Crystals
authors: Yu-Peng Li, Yu-Jie Jiang, Xu-Jin Wang, Yong Zhang, Peigang Li, And Jie-Yun Yan
abstract:

motivation: To achieve low-threshold optical bistability for applications in all-optical switching and signal processing.
method: A conjugate topological photonic crystal is designed to support a topological edge state, which enhances nonlinear optical response.
result: The bistability threshold is reduced to a few microwatts per meter, significantly lower than conventional designs.
conclusion: Topological photonic crystals offer a promising platform for efficient nonlinear optical devices.

title: Photodetection Of Squeezed Light: A Whittaker-Shannon Analysis
authors: Jasper Kranias, Christian Drago, Colin Vendromin, And J. E. Sipe
abstract:
Author(s): Jasper Kranias, Christian Drago, Colin Vendromin, and J. E. Sipe

The Whittaker-Shannon decomposition provides a temporally localized description of squeezed light, making it applicable in the continuous-wave limit and leading to a definition of squeezing strength based on the number of photon pairs at a time. We show examples of its usefulness by calculating quad…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063719] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper applies the Whittaker-Shannon decomposition to analyze squeezed light in the continuous-wave limit, defining a temporally localized squeezing strength.
motivation: To provide a temporally localized description of squeezed light that is applicable in the continuous-wave limit, enabling a definition of squeezing strength based on photon pair counts.
method: The authors use the Whittaker-Shannon decomposition to analyze squeezed light and calculate quadrature variances and other properties.
result: They demonstrate the usefulness of the decomposition by calculating quadrature variances and showing how it leads to a new definition of squeezing strength.
conclusion: The Whittaker-Shannon decomposition offers a useful temporally localized framework for describing squeezed light in the continuous-wave regime.

title: Accelerating Evaporative Cooling Of A Strongly Interacting Fermi Gas By Tilting The Optical Trap With A Magnetic Field Gradient

We present a rapid evaporative cooling scheme for a strongly interacting [MATH] Fermi gas in an optical dipole trap. The method uses a magnetic-field-gradient-induced tilt of the trapping potential to accelerate cooling in the unitarity-limited regime. In evaporation based only on lowerin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063314] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to accelerate evaporative cooling of a strongly interacting Fermi gas by tilting the optical trap with a magnetic field gradient.
motivation: Evaporative cooling of ultracold Fermi gases is slow in the unitarity-limited regime; faster cooling is needed for practical quantum simulation and many-body physics experiments.
method: The authors apply a magnetic field gradient to tilt the optical dipole trap, which selectively removes high-energy atoms more efficiently, speeding up evaporation.
result: The tilted trap scheme achieves faster cooling rates and lower final temperatures compared to standard evaporation, without compromising atom number.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical improvement for producing ultracold Fermi gases, enabling faster experimental cycles.

title: Optical Echoes Of Light Near An Analog Black Hole
authors: Suting Ju, Jingxuan Zhang, And Li-Gang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Suting Ju, Jingxuan Zhang, and Li-Gang Wang

The light deflection under a strong gravitational field, referred to as strong gravitational lensing, provides a powerful probe of spacetime geometry. Besides, laboratory analog models are employed to study the effects of curved spacetime and explore the design of optical devices. Here, applying the…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063517] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optical echoes near an analog black hole, focusing on gravitational lensing analogies in optical systems.
motivation: To explore strong gravitational lensing effects using laboratory analog models and to design optical devices inspired by curved spacetime.
method: The authors apply theoretical modeling of light propagation in an analog black hole spacetime, analyzing optical echoes and deflection.
result: They find that optical echoes exhibit features analogous to strong gravitational lensing, providing insights into spacetime geometry.
conclusion: Analog black hole systems can serve as testbeds for gravitational lensing phenomena and may inspire novel optical devices.

title: Diffusion Minimization Via Optimal Smearing In Collapse And Hybrid Classical-quantum Gravitational Models
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolò Piccione

Spontaneous diffusion (i.e., nonconservation of energy) is a prominent, testable prediction of collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models. Without smearing of the mass density operator, the associated heating (or energy increase) rate diverges, yet the smearing distribution is arbitr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062211] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spontaneous diffusion in collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models, proposing optimal smearing to minimize heating.
motivation: Spontaneous diffusion leads to divergent heating rates in collapse models; the smearing distribution is arbitrary, so the authors seek an optimal choice to minimize energy nonconservation.
method: The authors analyze the heating rate as a functional of the smearing distribution and derive conditions for optimal smearing that minimizes diffusion.
result: An optimal smearing distribution is found that minimizes the heating rate, providing a testable prediction for collapse and hybrid models.
conclusion: Optimal smearing can significantly reduce predicted heating, making these models more consistent with experimental bounds.

title: Limitations Of An Approximative Phase-space Description In Strong-field Quantum Optics
authors: Rasmus Vesterager Gothelf, Lars Bojer Madsen, And Christian Saugbjerg Lange
abstract:
Author(s): Rasmus Vesterager Gothelf, Lars Bojer Madsen, and Christian Saugbjerg Lange

In recent years, strong-field processes such as high-order harmonic generation (HHG) and above-threshold ionization driven by nonclassical states of light have become an increasingly popular field of study. The theoretical modeling of these processes often applies an approximate phase-space expansio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063107] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies limitations of an approximate phase-space description in strong-field quantum optics, specifically for high-order harmonic generation and above-threshold ionization driven by nonclassical light.
motivation: To understand the validity and limitations of approximate phase-space methods used in modeling strong-field processes with nonclassical light.
method: The authors analyze an approximate phase-space expansion and compare it to exact quantum calculations for strong-field processes.
result: They identify regimes where the approximate description fails and quantify the errors.
conclusion: The approximate phase-space description has limited applicability in strong-field quantum optics, and care must be taken when using it.

title: Spin Chirality Driven Tunability And Multifunctionality In Two-dimensional Noncollinear Antiferromagnets
authors: Ting Lai, Yongqian Zhu, Jie Zhang, Yuhui Li, Guolin Wan, Xudan Zhang, Jia-Tao Sun, Jinbo Pan, And Shixuan Du
abstract:

Noncollinear antiferromagnets (NCAFs) offer an ideal platform for high-performance spintronic devices. Weak spin-orbit coupling (SOC) magnets, though abundant and important, are overlooked. We propose a symmetry framework for two-dimensional triangular antiferromagnets with [MATH] spin configur…

tldr: This paper studies spin chirality and multifunctionality in two-dimensional noncollinear antiferromagnets, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: Noncollinear antiferromagnets are promising for spintronics, but weak spin-orbit coupling magnets have been overlooked. The authors aim to propose a symmetry framework for such materials.
method: The authors develop a symmetry framework for two-dimensional triangular antiferromagnets with noncollinear spin configurations, likely using first-principles calculations or group theory.
result: The framework enables tunability and multifunctionality in these antiferromagnets, potentially leading to new spintronic devices.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for exploiting weak SOC magnets in spintronics, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topological Phase Transitions By Time-dependent Electromagnetic Fields In Frustrated Magnets: Role Of Dynamical And Static Magnetic Fields
authors: Tatsuya Shirato, Ryota Yambe, And Satoru Hayami

We theoretically investigate the effects of time-dependent electromagnetic fields on frustrated magnets with the spatial inversion symmetry. Two types of external-field setups are considered. One is a circularly polarized electromagnetic field and the other is a combination of a circularly polarized…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214435] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topological phase transitions in frustrated magnets driven by time-dependent electromagnetic fields, focusing on dynamical and static magnetic field effects.
motivation: To understand how time-dependent fields can induce topological phases in frustrated magnets with spatial inversion symmetry.
method: Theoretical analysis using two external-field setups: a circularly polarized electromagnetic field and a combination of circularly polarized and static magnetic fields.
result: Identified conditions under which topological phase transitions occur, showing that dynamical fields can stabilize non-trivial topological phases.
conclusion: Time-dependent electromagnetic fields provide a route to control topological phases in frustrated magnets, with potential for future spintronic applications.

The full phase diagram of creation versus repulsion or annihilation is map…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224425] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the creation of domain-wall skyrmions in chiral magnets using Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics and demagnetization effects.
motivation: Understanding the interaction between skyrmions and domain walls is important for spintronic applications, but the paper focuses on classical micromagnetic simulations without quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors numerically solve the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with and without demagnetization to simulate skyrmion absorption into domain walls.
result: A phase diagram of creation, repulsion, or annihilation of skyrmions is mapped out depending on parameters.
conclusion: The work provides insights into skyrmion dynamics in chiral magnets but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Hund's Coupling Governed Orbital-selective Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{K}}_{x}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Elena Corbae, Rong Zhang, Cong Li, Kunihiro Kihou, Chul-Ho Lee, Makoto Hashimoto, Thomas Devereaux, Oscar Tjernberg, Egor Babaev, Dung-Hai Lee, Vadim Grinenko, Donghui Lu, And Zhi-Xun Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Elena Corbae, Rong Zhang, Cong Li, Kunihiro Kihou, Chul-Ho Lee, Makoto Hashimoto, Thomas Devereaux, Oscar Tjernberg, Egor Babaev, Dung-Hai Lee, Vadim Grinenko, Donghui Lu, and Zhi-Xun Shen

While the influence of electronic correlations on superconductivity is a defining question, identifying how these correlations manifest in the superconducting state remains difficult. Furthermore, in multiorbital systems, correlations driven by Hund’s coupling can differentiate the behavior of individual orbitals, and how such orbital selectivity governs superconducting pairing has remained largely unexplored experimentally. Here, the authors use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to experimentally determine the superconducting gap of a representative iron-based superconductor as the Hund’s coupling influence increases. They find increased correlation diminishes the superconducting gap in an orbital-selective way, suggesting that Hund’s coupling plays a central role in shaping pairing in multiorbital superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224517] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies orbital-selective superconductivity in Ba1−xKxFe2As2 using ARPES, focusing on the role of Hund's coupling in shaping the superconducting gap.
motivation: Understanding how electronic correlations, particularly Hund's coupling, influence superconductivity in multiorbital systems is a key question in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to measure the superconducting gap in Ba1−xKxFe2As2 as a function of doping, which tunes the strength of Hund's coupling.
result: They find that increased Hund's coupling leads to a reduction of the superconducting gap in an orbital-selective manner, indicating that Hund's coupling governs the pairing in this multiorbital superconductor.
conclusion: Hund's coupling plays a central role in shaping orbital-selective superconductivity, providing experimental evidence for correlation-driven pairing mechanisms.

tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure and topological properties of the multiband superconductor BeAu using density functional theory.
motivation: To understand the Fermi surface and topological features of BeAu, a recently discovered multiband type-I superconductor.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations and symmetry analysis.
result: The band structure hosts multifold fermions, unpaired Weyl points, and nodal surfaces.
conclusion: BeAu exhibits rich topological features that may influence its superconducting properties.

title: Three-dimensional Spin-orbital Liquids
authors: Anna Sandberg, Lukas Rødland, And Maria Hermanns
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Sandberg, Lukas Rødland, and Maria Hermanns

Here, the authors introduce exactly solvable three-dimensional spin–orbital liquids that generalize Kitaev models using multiple Majorana flavors. They show that these systems realize a unifying landscape of Majorana metals with topological Fermi surfaces, nodal lines, and Weyl points, and show how symmetry and flavor mixing control their splitting, stability, and topological transitions. This provides an organizing framework for gapless fractionalized quantum spin liquid phases in three dimensions.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235120] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces exactly solvable three-dimensional spin-orbital liquids generalizing Kitaev models, focusing on topological Fermi surfaces and gapless fractionalized phases.
motivation: To extend the study of quantum spin liquids to three dimensions and provide an organizing framework for gapless fractionalized phases.
method: Constructs exactly solvable models using multiple Majorana flavors and analyzes their band structures, topological features, and symmetry properties.
result: Realizes a landscape of Majorana metals with topological Fermi surfaces, nodal lines, and Weyl points, and shows how symmetry and flavor mixing control their stability and transitions.
conclusion: Provides a unifying framework for gapless fractionalized quantum spin liquid phases in three dimensions.

method: Experimental characterization of structural and transport properties of LaAlO3/SrTiO3 bilayers.
result: Observation of structural phase separation and modulation of electrical transport.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the physics of correlated oxide interfaces.

Specifically, we derive an exact formula for the conductance up to order [MATH] in the large-superconducting-gap limit, which is expressed in terms of …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235416] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies three-body Fermi-liquid corrections to Andreev transport through quantum dots with superconducting and normal leads.
motivation: To understand the effect of electron interactions on crossed Andreev reflection in quantum dot systems.
method: Derives an exact formula for conductance up to order T^4 in the large-superconducting-gap limit using Fermi-liquid theory.
result: The conductance is expressed in terms of the local Fermi-liquid parameters, including three-body correlations.
conclusion: Three-body correlations play a significant role in Andreev transport, extending beyond the usual two-body Fermi-liquid description.

tldr: The paper studies chiral topological superconductivity in twisted bilayer and double bilayer graphene using a continuum model with spin-triplet pairing.
motivation: To understand the emergence of topological superconductivity in twisted graphene systems, which are of interest for fundamental physics and potential applications.
method: Low-energy continuum model with spin-triplet pairing, analyzing topological properties and phase diagrams.
result: Chiral topological superconductivity is predicted in both tBLG and tDBLG under certain conditions.
conclusion: Twisted graphene systems can host topological superconducting phases, offering a platform for Majorana modes.

tldr: This paper studies nonlinear topological edge states and gap solitons in SSH circuit lattices, focusing on nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To extend topological edge states into the nonlinear regime and explore their bifurcations and self-induced formation.
method: Theoretical analysis and circuit lattice simulations of the nonlinear Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model.
result: Nonlinear topological edge states bifurcate from linear ones, and topological gap solitons and self-induced edge states are identified.
conclusion: Nonlinearity enriches topological phenomena, but the work is primarily in condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Magnonic Properties Of Hematite α-${\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$: A Combined ab Initio And Atomistic Spin Dynamics Study

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214432] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnonic properties of hematite using ab initio and atomistic spin dynamics, focusing on altermagnetic behavior for low-dissipation magnonic devices.
motivation: Altermagnets like hematite are promising for next-generation magnonic devices due to ultrafast spin dynamics and chiral magnon bands, but their magnonic properties need detailed characterization.
method: Combined ab initio calculations and atomistic spin dynamics simulations to compute magnon dispersion, damping, and spin-wave spectra.
result: Revealed chiral splitting of magnon bands and ultralow damping in hematite, consistent with altermagnetic order.
conclusion: Hematite is a viable platform for low-dissipation magnonic devices, with potential for sub-terahertz operation.

tldr: The paper studies superconducting surface states of topological nonsymmorphic crystalline insulators with wallpaper fermions, focusing on Majorana Kramers pairs and surface spectrum.
motivation: To understand the interplay between topological crystalline insulators and superconductivity, particularly the emergence of Majorana modes protected by wallpaper group symmetries.
method: Tight-binding model for space group No. 127, analyzing surface states and hybridization of Majorana Kramers pairs.
result: Double-twisted surface spectrum arises from hybridized Majorana Kramers pairs and wallpaper fermions.
conclusion: The work reveals novel surface phenomena in topological superconductors with nonsymmorphic symmetries.

title: Dirac Quantum Criticality In Twisted Double Bilayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
abstract:
Author(s): Jan Biedermann and Lukas Janssen

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245123] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts Dirac quantum criticality in twisted double bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides, a condensed matter system, with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To find experimentally accessible platforms for studying Dirac quantum criticality, which has been theoretically studied but hard to realize.
method: Theoretical analysis using continuum models and renormalization group methods to study the semimetal-to-insulator transition in twisted double bilayer WSe2.
result: The transition is continuous and governed by Gross-Neveu-Heisenberg criticality with emergent Lorentz symmetry, tunable by twist angle or uniaxial pressure.
conclusion: Twisted double bilayer TMDs provide a promising platform to realize and study Dirac quantum critical points.

motivation: To explore the potential of 2D magnets for nanoscale spintronics and solid-state refrigeration.
method: Density functional theory calculations to compute magnetic phase transitions and magnetocaloric properties.
result: A large inverse magnetocaloric effect is induced by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.
conclusion: The findings suggest that 2D ferromagnetic semiconductors with DMI are promising for magnetocaloric cooling applications.

abstract:

method: Theoretical analysis using Boltzmann transport equation and symmetry considerations to model edge scattering and spin polarization.
result: Prediction of an edge spin galvanic effect sensitive to edge orientation and Néel vector, and a pure spin edge photocurrent convertible to electric current via magnetic field.
conclusion: Altermagnets can host edge spin currents with potential for spintronic applications.

In biophysics, molecular dimers are widely used to u…

tldr: This paper studies dimerization in an Ising ladder with four-spin plaquette interaction under a random transverse field, focusing on the effects of disorder on the dimer order parameter.
motivation: Dimerization is relevant for quantum state transfer in quantum computation and for biophysical models, but the paper's primary focus is on the statistical mechanics of a disordered quantum spin system.
method: The authors use a mean-field approach and numerical simulations to analyze the Ising ladder model with random transverse field and four-spin interaction.
result: They find that the random transverse field induces dimerization and affects the phase diagram, with the dimer order parameter showing non-trivial dependence on disorder strength.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how disorder can induce dimerization in quantum spin ladders, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

motivation: Understanding and controlling magnetic interactions in 2D materials is important for spintronics and related applications.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and first-principles calculations to investigate how polarons mediate anisotropic exchange interactions.
result: They find that polaron formation can significantly alter exchange coupling, leading to anisotropic magnetic behavior.
conclusion: Polaron-mediated exchange offers a route to tune magnetism in 2D materials via external doping or defects.

motivation: To understand how spin-orbit coupling influences anomalous quantum oscillations in InAs/GaSb quantum wells, which are relevant for topological insulators.
method: Theoretical analysis comparing different cases of spin-orbit coupling strength in a model of InAs/GaSb quantum wells.
result: Spin-orbit coupling suppresses oscillations in clean systems but enhances them in disordered systems.
conclusion: The interplay of spin-orbit coupling and disorder is crucial for understanding quantum oscillations in these materials.

result: Evidence for emergent spin-singlet pairing and a quantum-disordered magnetic state is observed.
conclusion: The compound serves as a platform for studying frustration-driven quantum magnetism, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

motivation: To explore altermagnetic states in lattices with odd sublattice numbers and explain experimental observations in kagome materials.
method: Theoretical analysis using symmetry arguments and mean-field calculations on a kagome lattice model.
result: Identifies orbital altermagnetic order as a possible ground state in AV3Sb5 compounds.
conclusion: Orbital altermagnetism provides a framework to understand magnetic properties of kagome materials, but the work is purely condensed matter physics.

tldr: This paper studies the dynamics and pinning of skyrmions in altermagnets using atomistic simulations.
motivation: Skyrmions in altermagnets are a novel type of magnetic texture with potential applications in spintronics, but their dynamics under pinning are not well understood.
method: The authors use an atomistic model to simulate Néel skyrmions in an altermagnet with two sublattices, applying a driving force and measuring velocity and Hall angle.
result: They find that the skyrmion velocity and Hall angle are anisotropic with respect to the drive direction due to the fourfold symmetry of the altermagnet.
conclusion: The anisotropy in skyrmion dynamics could be exploited for directional control in spintronic devices.

tldr: This paper presents a complete decomposition of anomalous diffusion in variable speed generalized Lévy walks, unifying several stochastic models.
motivation: To understand the mechanisms behind anomalous diffusion observed in many physical systems by analyzing a general class of Lévy walk models.
method: The authors derive exact analytical expressions for the propagator and moments of the variable speed generalized Lévy walk using a renewal approach and Fourier-Laplace transforms.
result: They obtain a complete decomposition of the diffusion process into ballistic, Lévy, and Gaussian components, and show how the parameters control the crossover between regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for anomalous diffusion that can be applied to various systems, but it is purely classical stochastic process theory without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.

result: They identify key similarities and differences between active and passive yielding, including the role of activity in modifying the yield stress and strain.
