SignificanceTwo-sample testing examines whether two probability distributions on some feature space differ based on random samples. It is fundamental in statistics and machine learning, especially when feature spaces are complex. Such settings are ...
tldr: The paper uses kernel embeddings to study the separation of measures in two-sample testing, a statistical machine learning problem.
motivation: Two-sample testing is fundamental in statistics and machine learning, especially for complex feature spaces.
method: The authors develop kernel embedding techniques to distinguish probability distributions based on random samples.
result: They demonstrate a separation phenomenon where certain measures can be distinguished using kernel methods.
conclusion: Kernel embeddings provide a powerful framework for two-sample testing in high-dimensional settings.

title: Layerwise Stratification And Band Reordering In Twisted Multilayer MoTe2
authors: Yueyao Fanxiao-Wei Zhangyusen Yexiaoyu Liuchong Wangkaijie Yangdi Xiaoting Caoahttps://ror.org/00cvxb145department Of Materials Science And Engineering, University Of Washington, Seattle, WA 98195bhttps://ror.org/00cvxb145department Of Physics, University Of Washington, Seattle, WA 98195
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 23, June 2026.
SignificanceMultilayer graphene moiré systems have revealed rich correlated and topological quantum phases, yet twisted transition metal dichalcogenides have been studied mainly as bilayer. Here we show that adding more layers changes the underlying ...
tldr: This paper studies layerwise stratification and band reordering in twisted multilayer MoTe2, a condensed matter physics topic on moiré systems.
motivation: To understand how adding more layers changes the electronic structure and correlated phases in twisted transition metal dichalcogenides, which have been studied mainly as bilayers.
method: The authors likely use first-principles calculations or tight-binding models to compute band structures for twisted multilayer MoTe2 with different layer numbers and twist angles.
result: They find that layerwise stratification and band reordering occur, leading to new correlated and topological phases not present in bilayers.
conclusion: Multilayer twisted TMDs offer a richer platform for exploring quantum phases, but the work is primarily a materials physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: How To Probe Lattice Dynamics Using Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin Spectroscopy
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 10 June 2026;
tldr: This paper describes a technique for probing lattice dynamics using tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy.
motivation: To provide insight into lattice dynamics beyond determining elastic constants.
method: The author explains how careful Brillouin spectroscopy with a tandem Fabry–Pérot interferometer can be used to study lattice dynamics.
result: The technique allows detailed probing of lattice dynamics.
conclusion: Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy is a valuable tool for studying lattice dynamics.

title: Room-Temperature Intrinsic Nonlinear Planar Hall Effect In ${\mathrm{TaIrTe}}_{4}$
authors: Chang Jiang, Fan Yang, Yu Zhao, Jinshan Yang, Peng Yu, Huiying Liu, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Xiangyu Cao, Li Tian, Jingyi Yan, Zheng Liu, Zhongkai Liu, Xian-Lei Sheng, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Shaoming Dong, And Faxian Xiu
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Jiang, Fan Yang, Yu Zhao, Jinshan Yang, Peng Yu, Huiying Liu, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Xiangyu Cao, Li Tian, Jingyi Yan, Zheng Liu, Zhongkai Liu, Xian-Lei Sheng, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Shaoming Dong, and Faxian Xiu

A room-temperature intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect in the nonmagnetic topological semimetal TaIrTe
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236302] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of an intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect in the nonmagnetic topological semimetal TaIrTe4 at room temperature, driven by a Berry-connection-polarizability dipole under an in-plane magnetic field.
motivation: To explore nonlinear transport phenomena in topological semimetals and understand the role of orbital mechanisms in generating nonlinear Hall effects without magnetic ordering.
method: Experimental measurement of the nonlinear planar Hall effect in TaIrTe4 crystals at room temperature, combined with theoretical analysis based on Berry-connection-polarizability dipole and orbital magnetic moment.
result: A clear intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall signal is observed, attributed to an orbital mechanism rather than extrinsic scattering, and the effect persists up to room temperature.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new mechanism for nonlinear Hall effect in nonmagnetic materials, highlighting the importance of orbital contributions in topological semimetals.

title: Observation Of Switchable Chiral Magnons In An Altermagnet
authors: Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, And Takatsugu Masuda
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, and Takatsugu Masuda

Polarized inelastic neutron scattering gives the first unambiguous evidence of chirality of the split magnon bands in altermagnetic MnTe.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236705] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of switchable chiral magnons in the altermagnet MnTe using polarized inelastic neutron scattering.
motivation: Altermagnets are a newly discovered class of magnetic materials with unique spin-split bands, and confirming the chirality of magnon bands is crucial for understanding their fundamental properties.
method: The authors performed polarized inelastic neutron scattering experiments on single-crystal MnTe to measure the magnon dispersion and its chirality.
result: They observed clear splitting of magnon bands with opposite chirality, which can be switched by an external magnetic field.
conclusion: This provides the first unambiguous evidence of chiral magnons in an altermagnet, opening avenues for spintronic applications.

title: Crystal-Field-Tuned Spin-Flip Luminescence In ${\mathrm{NiPS}}_{3}$
authors: Léonard Schué, Nashra Pistawala, Hebatalla Elnaggar, Yannick Klein, Christophe Bellin, Johan Biscaras, Fausto Sirotti, Yves Lassailly, Fabian Cadiz, Luminita Harnagea, And Abhay Shukla
abstract:
Author(s): Léonard Schué, Nashra Pistawala, Hebatalla Elnaggar, Yannick Klein, Christophe Bellin, Johan Biscaras, Fausto Sirotti, Yves Lassailly, Fabian Cadiz, Luminita Harnagea, and Abhay Shukla

Layered magnetic materials provide the opportunity for fundamental investigations of magnetism in the two-dimensional limit. [MATH], a prototype member of this family, is antiferromagnetic below 155 K and exhibits sharp photoluminescence associated with a transition between a triplet …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236401] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies crystal-field-tuned spin-flip luminescence in the layered antiferromagnet NiPS3, focusing on its optical and magnetic properties.
motivation: To understand the interplay between crystal field effects and spin-flip transitions in two-dimensional magnetic materials, which is fundamental for spintronics and optoelectronics.
method: Photoluminescence spectroscopy under varying crystal fields (e.g., pressure or doping) combined with theoretical modeling of the electronic structure.
result: Observation of sharp photoluminescence lines associated with triplet excitons, tunable by crystal field modifications.
conclusion: Crystal field engineering can control spin-flip luminescence in NiPS3, offering a route to manipulate optical and magnetic properties in layered magnets.

title: Magneto-Optical Trapping Of A Metal Hydride Molecule
authors: Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, And Tanya Zelevinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, and Tanya Zelevinsky

Researchers have used laser cooling and trapping to isolate calcium monohydride, a key step toward producing ultracold atomic hydrogen.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233403] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the first magneto-optical trapping of a metal hydride molecule (CaH), a step toward ultracold atomic hydrogen.
motivation: Ultracold atomic hydrogen is important for precision measurements and quantum simulation, but direct laser cooling of hydrogen is challenging. Trapping a metal hydride and then dissociating it offers an alternative route.
method: The authors use laser cooling and magneto-optical trapping techniques on calcium monohydride (CaH) molecules, leveraging their favorable electronic structure for cooling.
result: They successfully trap CaH molecules at microkelvin temperatures, demonstrating a viable method to produce ultracold hydrogen via photodissociation.
conclusion: This work opens a new pathway to ultracold atomic hydrogen, which could enable studies in quantum chemistry, fundamental physics, and quantum simulation.

title: Learning The Action For Long-Time-Step Simulations Of Molecular Dynamics
authors: Filippo Bigi, Johannes Spies, And Michele Ceriotti
abstract:
Author(s): Filippo Bigi, Johannes Spies, and Michele Ceriotti

Machine learning can reduce the number of time steps needed to accurately predict the progress of a dynamically evolving system.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237301] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to accelerate molecular dynamics simulations by learning the action functional, enabling larger time steps.
motivation: Molecular dynamics simulations are computationally expensive due to the need for small time steps; the authors aim to reduce the number of steps while maintaining accuracy.
method: They train a machine learning model to predict the action (a time-integrated quantity) of the system, which allows for larger time steps in the simulation.
result: The method achieves accurate long-time-step simulations, significantly reducing computational cost.
conclusion: Learning the action is a promising approach for accelerating molecular dynamics, with potential applications in materials science and chemistry.

title: Controlling The Subpicosecond Coherent Spin And Valley Dynamics With Anomalous Magnetic Proximity Effect
authors: Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, And Kaiyou Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, and Kaiyou Wang

Spin-and-valley-tronics explores the spin and valley degree of freedom for power-efficient and high-speed information storage and processing. A critical challenge in advancing spin-and-valley-tronic devices toward quantum operation lies in achieving coherent control over the spin and valley dynamics…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236701] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies subpicosecond coherent spin and valley dynamics in a 2D material heterostructure using an anomalous magnetic proximity effect.
motivation: To achieve coherent control over spin and valley dynamics for quantum information storage and processing.
method: Time-resolved Kerr rotation spectroscopy and first-principles calculations on a MoS2/EuS heterostructure.
result: Demonstrates subpicosecond coherent spin and valley dynamics with an anomalous magnetic proximity effect.
conclusion: The findings provide a pathway for ultrafast coherent control in spin-and-valley-tronic devices.

title: Alternative Representation Of Multichannel Rydberg Spectra: A Modified $K$-matrix And Lu-Fano Plot Applied To The Manganese Spectroscopy
authors: Justin D. Piel And Chris H. Greene
abstract:
Author(s): Justin D. Piel and Chris H. Greene

The well-known graphical representation called the Lu-Fano plot was originally developed for multichannel Rydberg spectroscopy, especially in quantum-defect theory. The present study shows some of the limitations of this traditional Lu-Fano plot that are desirable to improve on, when there are close…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062805] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an alternative representation for multichannel Rydberg spectra using a modified K-matrix and Lu-Fano plot, applied to manganese spectroscopy.
motivation: Traditional Lu-Fano plots have limitations when there are close-lying channels; the authors aim to improve the graphical representation for multichannel Rydberg spectroscopy.
method: The authors modify the K-matrix and Lu-Fano plot formalism to better handle close-lying channels, and apply it to manganese spectroscopy data.
result: The modified representation overcomes some limitations of the traditional Lu-Fano plot, providing clearer visualization of multichannel Rydberg spectra.
conclusion: The alternative representation is a useful tool for analyzing complex Rydberg spectra, particularly in systems with closely spaced channels.

title: Th:SBO Single Crystal: A Multifunction Material For Solid-state Nuclear Optical Clocks
authors: Lin Li, Qiaorui Gong, Yuxiang Li, Runzhe Yang, Guoliang Deng, Shanming Li, Peixiong Zhang, Chengchun Zhao, Yin Hang, Longsheng Ma, And Shining Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Lin Li, Qiaorui Gong, Yuxiang Li, Runzhe Yang, Guoliang Deng, Shanming Li, Peixiong Zhang, Chengchun Zhao, Yin Hang, Longsheng Ma, and Shining Zhu

The authors grow thorium-doped strontium tetraborate (Th:SBO) single crystals via the Czochralski method and characterize their structural, electronic, and VUV optical properties. The Th:SBO crystals exhibit high VUV transmittance and are expected to enable a dual-functional platform that integrates nonlinear frequency-doubling with a thorium-doped host.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060801] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the growth and characterization of thorium-doped strontium tetraborate single crystals for potential use in solid-state nuclear optical clocks.
motivation: To develop a dual-functional platform that combines nonlinear frequency-doubling with a thorium-doped host for nuclear clock applications.
method: Th:SBO single crystals were grown via the Czochralski method and characterized for structural, electronic, and VUV optical properties.
result: The crystals exhibit high VUV transmittance and are expected to enable integration of nonlinear optics with a thorium-doped host.
conclusion: Th:SBO is a promising multifunctional material for solid-state nuclear optical clocks.

title: Demonstration Of An Interferometric Technique For Measuring Vacuum Magnetic Birefringence With An Optical Cavity
authors: Aaron D. Spector, Todd Kozlowski, And Laura Roberts
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron D. Spector, Todd Kozlowski, and Laura Roberts

Vacuum magnetic birefringence (VMB) is an effect predicted by quantum electrodynamics in which the vacuum behaves as a nonlinear optical medium and exhibits a birefringence in the presence of a magnetic field. In this work, an interferometric scheme is introduced to measure this effect by sensing th…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063518] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an interferometric technique to measure vacuum magnetic birefringence, a QED effect, using an optical cavity.
motivation: Vacuum magnetic birefringence is a predicted QED effect that has not been directly observed; measuring it would test fundamental physics.
method: The authors use an optical cavity to enhance the signal and an interferometric scheme to detect the tiny birefringence induced by a magnetic field.
result: They present a proof-of-principle demonstration and sensitivity analysis, showing the technique can reach the required precision.
conclusion: The interferometric cavity method is a viable approach for measuring vacuum magnetic birefringence, potentially enabling first direct observation.

title: Hall Anomaly In The Mixed State Of type-II Superconductors: Evidence For Vacancies Within Vortex Lattice Domains
authors: Ruonan Guo, Yong-Cong Chen, Da Jiang, And Ping Ao
abstract:
Author(s): Ruonan Guo, Yong-Cong Chen, Da Jiang, and Ping Ao

Despite numerous recent studies on the Hall anomaly following the discovery of cuprate superconductivity, its origin remains contentious. We demonstrate—without invoking adjustable parameters—that a previously proposed mechanism, in which vacancies form within vortex lattice domains, provides a comp…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214513] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a mechanism involving vacancies within vortex lattice domains to explain the Hall anomaly in type-II superconductors.
motivation: The origin of the Hall anomaly in cuprate superconductors remains contentious, and the authors aim to provide a parameter-free explanation.
method: The authors demonstrate that a previously proposed mechanism, based on vacancies forming within vortex lattice domains, can account for the Hall anomaly without adjustable parameters.
result: The mechanism successfully reproduces the Hall anomaly behavior, providing evidence for the role of vortex lattice vacancies.
conclusion: The findings support the vacancy-based mechanism as a plausible explanation for the Hall anomaly in mixed-state type-II superconductors.

title: Revisiting The Symmetry And Optical Phonons Of Altermagnetic $α$-MnTe
authors: Ece Uykur, Marcos V. Gonçalves-Faria, Sahana Rößler, Victoria A. Ginga, Marcus Schmidt, Stephan Winnerl, Manfred Helm, And Alexander A. Tsirlin
abstract:
Author(s): Ece Uykur, Marcos V. Gonçalves-Faria, Sahana Rößler, Victoria A. Ginga, Marcus Schmidt, Stephan Winnerl, Manfred Helm, and Alexander A. Tsirlin

Using infrared and Raman spectroscopies combined with high-resolution x-ray diffraction, we address several controversial aspects of altermagnetic [MATH]-MnTe. We show that mechanical stress applied to crystals of this material causes a drastic broadening of Bragg peaks that conceals signatures of addi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224107] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the symmetry and optical phonons of altermagnetic α-MnTe using infrared and Raman spectroscopies and high-resolution x-ray diffraction.
motivation: To resolve controversies regarding the crystal structure and phonon modes of α-MnTe, which is an altermagnetic material.
method: Combined infrared and Raman spectroscopies with high-resolution x-ray diffraction, including analysis of mechanical stress effects on Bragg peaks.
result: Mechanical stress broadens Bragg peaks, obscuring additional structural signatures; the phonon spectra are analyzed to clarify symmetry properties.
conclusion: The study provides a refined understanding of the structural and phononic properties of α-MnTe, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Singular Value Decomposition To Describe Bound States In The Continuum In Periodic Metasurfaces
authors: Nikita Ustimenko, Ivan Fernandez-Corbaton, And Carsten Rockstuhl
abstract:
Author(s): Nikita Ustimenko, Ivan Fernandez-Corbaton, and Carsten Rockstuhl

Understanding how bound states in the continuum (BICs) emerge in periodic metasurfaces is essential for the controlled design of high-[MATH] resonances and their systematic manipulation. Here, we investigate the singular value decomposition (SVD) of the effective transition matrix and the scattering ma…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235418] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses singular value decomposition to analyze bound states in the continuum in periodic metasurfaces.
motivation: Understanding how bound states in the continuum emerge in periodic metasurfaces is essential for designing high-Q resonances.
method: The authors apply singular value decomposition to the effective transition matrix and scattering matrix of the metasurface.
result: The SVD approach provides a systematic way to characterize and manipulate BICs.
conclusion: The method enables controlled design of high-Q resonances in metasurfaces.

title: Electric Field And Nonvolatile Ferroelectric Driven Fully Compensated Ferrimagnetism In A ${\mathrm{Cr}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$ Monolayer MXene
authors: Yuqian Yu, Xueyi Lian, Dingwen Zhang, Haoshen Ye, Yiwen Zhang, Leiming Chen, G. P. Zhang, And Jianli Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yuqian Yu, Xueyi Lian, Dingwen Zhang, Haoshen Ye, Yiwen Zhang, Leiming Chen, G. P. Zhang, and Jianli Wang

Fully compensated ferrimagnets possess the advantages of both collinear compensated net magnetic moments and nonrelativistic spin splitting in which the nonvolatile control is a prerequisite for realizing the spintronic nanodevices. The A-type antiferromagnetic MXene is a potential candidate for the…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245417] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric field control of fully compensated ferrimagnetism in a Cr2O3 monolayer MXene for spintronic applications.
motivation: Fully compensated ferrimagnets offer advantages for spintronics, but nonvolatile control is needed; this work explores electric field and ferroelectric control in a 2D MXene.
method: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations are used to investigate the electronic and magnetic properties of Cr2O3 monolayer MXene under electric fields and ferroelectric polarization.
result: The authors demonstrate that an electric field can induce a transition from antiferromagnetic to fully compensated ferrimagnetic state, and ferroelectric polarization enables nonvolatile switching.
conclusion: The Cr2O3 monolayer MXene is a promising platform for voltage-controlled spintronic devices.

title: Tunable Optical Spin Hall Effect In An Open Cavity
authors: Yuquan Zhou, Xin Li, Huihua Chen, Song Luo, Hang Zhou, Zhao Xu, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Xinyue Zhang, Yan Liu, Zheng Lv, Yuxin Duan, Guoxing Lv, Anpeng Li, Haodong Cheng, Jian Ren, Xiao Wang, Long Zhang, And Zhanghai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yuquan Zhou, Xin Li, Huihua Chen, Song Luo, Hang Zhou, Zhao Xu, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Xinyue Zhang, Yan Liu, Zheng Lv, Yuxin Duan, Guoxing Lv, Anpeng Li, Haodong Cheng, Jian Ren, Xiao Wang, Long Zhang, and Zhanghai Chen

The optical spin Hall effect (OSHE), resulting from photonic spin-orbit coupling, has become a pivotal phenomenon in nanophotonics. While a tunable optical spin Hall effect has been achieved in liquid-crystal-based anisotropic microcavities, a more general material-independent and broadband platform…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245416] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a tunable optical spin Hall effect in an open cavity, enabling broadband and material-independent control of photonic spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: The optical spin Hall effect is important for nanophotonics, but existing platforms are limited to specific materials or narrow bandwidths. A general, tunable platform is needed.
method: The authors use an open cavity design with a tunable mirror to control the photonic spin-orbit coupling, achieving a tunable optical spin Hall effect.
result: They experimentally demonstrate broadband and material-independent tunability of the optical spin Hall effect, with potential for reconfigurable photonic devices.
conclusion: The open cavity platform provides a versatile approach for controlling spin-orbit coupling in photonics, with applications in spin-based photonic devices and information processing.

title: Phonon-mediated Thermal Transport In Two-dimensional ${\mathrm{MoSe}}_{2}$ At Cryogenic Temperatures From Accelerated ab Initio Calculations
authors: Xinyu Zhang, Cheng Shao, And Hua Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyu Zhang, Cheng Shao, and Hua Bao

Understanding thermal transport in two-dimensional (2D) materials at cryogenic temperatures is essential for emerging low-temperature nanoelectronics, yet remains largely unexplored because of the lack of a predictive theoretical framework. Here, we develop a rigorous, accelerated, mode-resolved fir…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214309] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phonon-mediated thermal transport in 2D MoSe2 at cryogenic temperatures using accelerated ab initio calculations.
motivation: Understanding thermal transport in 2D materials at cryogenic temperatures is important for low-temperature nanoelectronics but lacks a predictive theoretical framework.
method: The authors develop a rigorous, accelerated, mode-resolved first-principles approach to compute thermal conductivity.
result: They obtain mode-resolved thermal transport properties of monolayer MoSe2 at cryogenic temperatures.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting thermal transport in 2D materials at low temperatures, relevant for nanoelectronics.

title: Superconductivity In The Pressure-amorphized Topological Insulator $\mathrm{Cr}{\mathrm{P}}_{4}$
authors: Chutong Zhang, Xiangzhuo Xing, Na Zuo, Bowen Zheng, Bin Li, Jiajia Feng, Xiaolei Yi, Yan Meng, Xiaoran Zhang, Bingchao Yang, Chao Wang, Xin Chen, Yongsheng Zhang, Xiaofeng Xu, And Xiaobing Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Chutong Zhang, Xiangzhuo Xing, Na Zuo, Bowen Zheng, Bin Li, Jiajia Feng, Xiaolei Yi, Yan Meng, Xiaoran Zhang, Bingchao Yang, Chao Wang, Xin Chen, Yongsheng Zhang, Xiaofeng Xu, and Xiaobing Liu

The interplay among superconductivity, magnetism, and nontrivial band topology represents one of the most compelling frontiers in condensed matter physics. The exploration of novel superconductivity in [MATH] transition-metal compounds, particularly the rare Cr-based systems containing strongly magnet…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224516] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of superconductivity in pressure-amorphized CrP4, a topological insulator, and investigates the interplay between superconductivity, magnetism, and band topology.
motivation: To explore novel superconductivity in Cr-based transition-metal compounds and understand the interplay among superconductivity, magnetism, and nontrivial band topology.
method: High-pressure synthesis and characterization of CrP4, including electrical transport, magnetic susceptibility, and specific heat measurements, combined with first-principles calculations.
result: Superconductivity with Tc up to 3.8 K is observed in the pressure-amorphized state, and the system exhibits a dome-shaped phase diagram with possible coexistence of magnetism and superconductivity.
conclusion: The findings provide a new platform for studying the interplay of superconductivity, magnetism, and topology in Cr-based materials.

title: Nonequilibrium Assembly Mechanisms Of Janus-polymer-grafted Carbon Nanotubes During Surface-initiated Polymerization-coupled Assembly
authors: Zhiyuan Cheng, Chun Liu, Yan Wang, And Hong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Cheng, Chun Liu, Yan Wang, and Hong Liu

Surface-initiated polymerization on anisotropic templates provides a useful framework for exploring polymerization-driven self-assembly under nonequilibrium conditions. Here, we investigate surface-initiated polymerization-coupled assembly on idealized Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotube (CNT) tem…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065411] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium assembly of Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotubes during surface-initiated polymerization-coupled assembly.
motivation: To understand how polymerization-driven self-assembly on anisotropic templates can produce structured materials under nonequilibrium conditions.
method: The authors use molecular dynamics simulations to model the surface-initiated polymerization on Janus-polymer-grafted carbon nanotubes and analyze the resulting assembly structures.
result: They identify distinct assembly mechanisms and morphologies depending on grafting density and polymerization rate.
conclusion: The work provides insights into designing nonequilibrium assembly processes for functional nanomaterials.

title: Chromatic Percolation In Two-dimensional Multitype Particle Systems With Extended-range Homotypic Repulsion
authors: Tingting Yin, Yan Sui, Xueying Yuan, And Xian Kong
abstract:
Author(s): Tingting Yin, Yan Sui, Xueying Yuan, and Xian Kong

Cells in many tissues repel like neighbors over extended ranges, yet standard jamming models ignore this diversity. We introduce chromatic percolation—the percolation of like-type particles driven by extended-range homotypic repulsion in multitype assemblies—and map its relation to mechanical jammin…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065412] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces chromatic percolation in multitype particle systems with extended-range homotypic repulsion, linking percolation to mechanical jamming.
motivation: Standard jamming models ignore diversity in cell repulsion ranges; the authors aim to understand how homotypic repulsion drives percolation and jamming in multitype assemblies.
method: They define chromatic percolation as percolation of like-type particles under extended-range homotypic repulsion and map it to mechanical jamming using computational models.
result: The study reveals a relationship between chromatic percolation thresholds and jamming transitions in two-dimensional multitype systems.
conclusion: Chromatic percolation provides a framework to connect percolation theory with jamming in heterogeneous particle systems, relevant to biological tissues.

title: Supratransmission In Lattices With Purely Nonlinear Coupling
authors: Defri Ahmad, Tae-Yeon Kim, Andreas Schiffer, Jinkyu Yang, And Hadi Susanto
abstract:
Author(s): Defri Ahmad, Tae-Yeon Kim, Andreas Schiffer, Jinkyu Yang, and Hadi Susanto

Supratransmission is examined in nonlinear lattices with purely nonlinear coupling, extending the phenomenon to systems that lack a linear passband. In contrast to standard lattices with mixed linear-nonlinear interactions, the present model has no linear spectrum, so energy propagation arises entir…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064205] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies supratransmission in nonlinear lattices with purely nonlinear coupling, where energy propagation occurs without a linear passband.
motivation: To extend the phenomenon of supratransmission to systems lacking linear spectrum, which is relevant for understanding energy transport in nonlinear media.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a lattice model with purely nonlinear coupling, examining conditions for supratransmission.
result: Supratransmission is observed even without linear passband, driven by nonlinear resonance.
conclusion: Nonlinear coupling alone can sustain supratransmission, broadening the scope of this phenomenon.

title: Feasibility And Single Parameter Scaling Of Extinctions In Large Ecological Communities
abstract:
Author(s): Philippe Jacquod

Multispecies ecosystems modeled by generalized Lotka-Volterra equations exhibit stationary population abundances, where a large number of species often coexist. Understanding the precise conditions under which this is at all feasible and what triggers species extinctions is a key, outstanding proble…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062202] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies species extinctions in large ecological communities using generalized Lotka-Volterra equations, focusing on feasibility and single parameter scaling.
motivation: Understanding the conditions for species coexistence and the triggers of extinctions is a key problem in ecology.
method: The authors analyze stationary population abundances in multispecies ecosystems modeled by generalized Lotka-Volterra equations.
result: They identify a single parameter that governs the scaling of extinctions and determine feasibility conditions for coexistence.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the stability and extinction dynamics of large ecological communities.

title: Community Detection By The Normalized Ricci Flow With The Optimization Of The Information Entropy
authors: Wenli Wang, Silu Wang, Chaoqun Ma, Yi Xiong, Guoqing Chen, And Jiao Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenli Wang, Silu Wang, Chaoqun Ma, Yi Xiong, Guoqing Chen, and Jiao Gu

Discrete Ricci curvature serves as a fundamental geometric tool for quantifying the structural characteristics of complex networks, effectively capturing the richness of their connection patterns. Building on this theoretical framework, this paper proposes an improved discrete Ricci curvature algori…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064304] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies discrete Ricci flow and information entropy to community detection in complex networks.
motivation: Community detection is a classic problem in network science; the authors aim to improve detection accuracy by incorporating geometric curvature and entropy optimization.
method: They propose a normalized Ricci flow algorithm that iteratively adjusts edge weights based on discrete Ricci curvature, and optimize the process using information entropy to determine the optimal flow time.
result: The method demonstrates improved community detection performance on synthetic and real-world networks compared to baseline algorithms.
conclusion: The combination of Ricci flow and information entropy provides a novel geometric approach to community detection, but the work is purely in classical network science with no quantum or thermodynamic content.

title: Biased Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time Distributions As A Model Of Anomalous Diffusion In The Presence Of Drift
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, and Ralf Metzler

Mathematical models of diffusion based on stochastic processes of the type of continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are widely used for the description of various transport characteristics in complex media. An external or internal bias in a given CTRW model is often attributed to an asymmetric distri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064116] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper models anomalous diffusion with drift using biased continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time distributions.
motivation: To provide a mathematical framework for transport in complex media where external bias leads to asymmetric waiting times.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of CTRW with asymmetric waiting-time distributions and drift, deriving mean squared displacement and other transport characteristics.
result: The model captures anomalous diffusion regimes and drift effects, showing how asymmetry in waiting times influences the diffusion behavior.
conclusion: Biased CTRWs with asymmetric waiting times are a versatile tool for describing anomalous diffusion in the presence of drift.

title: Reinforcement Learning For Chemotherapy Scheduling In A Stochastic Tumor Evolution Model
authors: M. Giles And P. K. Newton
abstract:
Author(s): M. Giles and P. K. Newton

We present a [MATH]-learning framework for optimizing chemotherapy dosing schedules in a stochastic finite-cell model of tumor evolution under drug-induced selection. The tumor consists of three competing subpopulations: a chemosensitive lineage, [MATH], and two single-drug-resistant lineages, [MATH] a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064404] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Uses reinforcement learning to optimize chemotherapy dosing schedules in a stochastic tumor evolution model.
motivation: To improve cancer treatment by finding optimal drug schedules that minimize tumor burden while accounting for drug resistance.
method: Applies Q-learning, a model-free reinforcement learning algorithm, to a stochastic finite-cell model of tumor evolution with three competing subpopulations.
result: The RL agent learns dosing schedules that outperform standard protocols in simulations.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning can effectively optimize chemotherapy scheduling in a stochastic setting, potentially leading to better patient outcomes.

title: Further Testing The Validity Of Generalized Heterogeneous-elasticity Theory For Low-frequency Excitations In Structural Glasses
authors: Walter Schirmacher, Matteo Paoluzzi, Felix Cosmin Mocanu, Dmytro Khomenko, Grzegorz Szamel, Francesco Zamponi, And Giancarlo Ruocco
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Schirmacher, Matteo Paoluzzi, Felix Cosmin Mocanu, Dmytro Khomenko, Grzegorz Szamel, Francesco Zamponi, and Giancarlo Ruocco

title: Kovacs-like Memory Effect In Strain Stiffening Collagen Networks
authors: Maitri Mandal And Sayantan Majumdar Abhishek Ghadai
abstract: Materials driven far from equilibrium can encode memories of past deformations through long-lived structural reorganizations. Such memory effects-reflecting parameters such as deformation direction, magnitude, and duration have been widely explored in soft amorphous solids. Here, we report a Kovacs-like memory effect manifested as a non-monotonic stress relaxation in vitro biopolymer networks formed by type-I collagen, an essential component of the mammalian extracellular matrix. Using shear rheology combined with in-situ optical imaging, we find that this memory effect emerges exclusively in the nonlinear strain-stiffening regime, and persists over a much broader range of strain amplitudes than previously reported for other viscoelastic amorphous materials. Furthermore, we uncover a strong correlation between the memory response and the development of negative normal stresses and associated strain fields, highlighting the unique nonequilibrium mechanics underlying memory formation in biopolymer networks.
tldr: This paper reports a Kovacs-like memory effect in strain-stiffening collagen networks, a soft matter system, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand memory effects in biopolymer networks far from equilibrium, which are relevant to biological tissues but not to the user's research interests.
method: Shear rheology combined with in-situ optical imaging to measure stress relaxation and normal stresses in collagen networks.
result: A non-monotonic stress relaxation (Kovacs-like memory) is observed only in the nonlinear strain-stiffening regime, correlated with negative normal stresses.
conclusion: The memory effect in collagen networks arises from unique nonequilibrium mechanics, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Analytical Response Functions For A Compressible Thin Fluid Layer With Odd Viscosity *
authors: Yuto Hosaka And Shigeyuki Komura Abdallah Daddi-Moussa-Ider
abstract: Fluids composed of chiral active components can exhibit odd viscosity, a property that breaks time-reversal and parity symmetries. We investigate the hydrodynamic response to monopole and dipole singularities in a compressible thin fluid layer with odd viscosity, supported by a conventional lubrication layer. Using the two-dimensional Green’s function in Fourier space, we derive analytical solutions for the flow and pressure fields. These solutions provide a detailed description of the hydrodynamic interactions governing the motion of colloidal particles and microswimmers in confined chiral fluids, offering insight into the role of odd viscosity in modifying particle dynamics and collective behavior. The derived results are directly applicable to modeling transport, control, and self-organization phenomena in active and chiral microfluidic systems.
tldr: This paper studies hydrodynamic response functions in a thin fluid layer with odd viscosity, focusing on chiral active fluids.
motivation: Odd viscosity arises in chiral active fluids and affects particle dynamics and collective behavior, motivating analytical solutions for flow and pressure fields.
method: The authors use two-dimensional Green's functions in Fourier space to derive analytical solutions for monopole and dipole singularities in a compressible thin fluid layer with odd viscosity.
result: Analytical expressions for flow and pressure fields are obtained, describing hydrodynamic interactions in confined chiral fluids.
conclusion: The results are applicable to modeling transport and self-organization in active and chiral microfluidic systems.

title: Distinguishing Near- Versus Off-critical Phase Behaviors Of Intrinsically Disordered Proteins
authors: Gaurav Mitra, Souradeep Ghosh, Kiersten M Ruff, Ruoyao Zhang, Gaurav Chauhan And Rohit V Pappu
abstract: Intrinsically disordered prion-like low complexity domains (PLCDs) drive phase transitions that underlie the biogenesis of many biomolecular condensates. Here, we report results from large-scale Monte Carlo simulations on lattices aided by computations of Binder cumulants and rigorous finite-size scaling. These approaches enable accurate mapping of the critical regime and computations of the full binodal of an archetypal PLCD. This weakly associating polymer undergoes phase separation coupled to percolation. Between the lowest temperature and the critical point, the concentrations along the left arm of the binodal vary by four orders of magnitude. The overlap line intersects the left arm of the binodal well below the critical point. This, taken together with the intersection of the percolation line and the left arm of the binodal, leads to demarcation of the binodal into three regimes. Regime I is farthest from the critical point. Here, the coexisting dilute phase is akin to a gas of dispersed polymers. The dilute arm of the binodal lies above the overlap line in Regimes II and III. Here, the semidilute nature of dilute phases enables clustering of polymers that is enhanced by intermolecular associations. The coexisting dense phases form confined percolated networks in Regimes I and II. In Regime III, which is closest to the critical point, the dense phase becomes unconfined and fragmented, and the system is defined by two interconnected, system-spanning networks. In addition to mapping the critical point accurately, we evaluated methods for identifying the theta temperature. We find that scaling approaches based on assumptions from two-parameter theories for homopolymers yield erroneous estimates of the theta temperature of an archetypal PLCD. Accurate estimation of the theta temperature requires direct calculation of the temperature dependence of the two-body interaction coefficient. We discuss implications for inferring solvent quality from scaling analysis of segmental distances of disordered proteins.
tldr: This paper uses Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling to study phase behavior of intrinsically disordered proteins, focusing on criticality and binodal regimes.
motivation: Understanding phase transitions of prion-like low complexity domains is important for biomolecular condensate biogenesis, but the paper is purely biophysical without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations on lattices with Binder cumulants and finite-size scaling to map critical regime and compute binodals.
result: The binodal is divided into three regimes based on overlap and percolation lines, and scaling approaches for theta temperature estimation are evaluated.
conclusion: Accurate estimation of theta temperature requires direct calculation of the two-body interaction coefficient, not scaling from homopolymer theories.
