X-ray diffraction can be used to monitor material-specific temperatures on ultrafast timescales and within nanostructures by exploiting thermal expansion or the Debye-Waller effect. Here, we simultaneou…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220301] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses ultrafast X-ray diffraction to measure temperature in platinum thin films by separating strain and Debye-Waller effects.
motivation: Understanding ultrafast thermal dynamics in nanostructures is important for materials science and device applications.
method: Simultaneous analysis of X-ray diffraction peak shifts and intensity changes to disentangle lattice expansion from atomic vibrations.
result: The method allows independent extraction of strain and Debye-Waller contributions, providing accurate temperature measurements on picosecond timescales.
conclusion: Ultrafast X-ray thermometry can distinguish thermal from non-thermal effects, enabling precise temperature mapping in thin films.

title: Nonlinear Breakdown Of Antisymmetric Flexoelectric Coupling
authors: Yingzhuo Lun, Yida Yang, Tingjun Wang, Qi Ren, Sang-Wook Cheong, Xueyun Wang, And Jiawang Hong
abstract:
Author(s): Yingzhuo Lun, Yida Yang, Tingjun Wang, Qi Ren, Sang-Wook Cheong, Xueyun Wang, and Jiawang Hong

Flexoelectric coupling is conventionally regarded as antisymmetric, such that reversing the strain gradient reverses the polarization direction while preserving its magnitude. Here we report that this antisymmetric coupling breaks down in noncentrosymmetric single crystals driven by large strain gra…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214104] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a breakdown of antisymmetric flexoelectric coupling in noncentrosymmetric single crystals under large strain gradients.
motivation: Flexoelectric coupling is conventionally antisymmetric; this work investigates deviations from that behavior.
method: Experimental measurements and theoretical analysis on noncentrosymmetric single crystals subjected to large strain gradients.
result: The antisymmetric coupling breaks down, leading to nonlinear polarization response.
conclusion: The finding challenges the conventional understanding of flexoelectricity and may have implications for electromechanical devices.

title: Stabilizing $\mathrm{Mg}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}$-like Superconductivity In $\mathrm{Li}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}{\mathrm{C}}_{2}$-derived Borocarbides Through Isovalent Metal Cosubstitution
authors: Renhai Wang, Yanwei Liang, Huafeng Dong, And Zhenyu Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Renhai Wang, Yanwei Liang, Huafeng Dong, and Zhenyu Zhang

Recent first-principles studies have shown that [MATH] can reach a higher superconducting transition temperature [MATH] than its parent material [MATH], yet its structural instability hinders experimental realization. Here, th…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214105] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses first-principles calculations to predict stable borocarbide superconductors with MgB2-like properties via isovalent metal cosubstitution.
motivation: To overcome the structural instability of LiB2C2, which theoretically has a high superconducting Tc but is experimentally unrealizable.
method: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations to search for stable borocarbide structures and evaluate their superconducting properties.
result: Identified several stable borocarbide compounds with predicted Tc values comparable to or higher than MgB2.
conclusion: Isovalent metal cosubstitution is an effective strategy to stabilize MgB2-like superconductivity in borocarbides.

title: Electron Penetration Heating In Turbulent Magnetic Loops Driven By Nonrelativistic Laser-plasma Interaction
authors: Zheng Gong, Sida Cao, Caleb Redshaw, And Matthew R. Edwards
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Gong, Sida Cao, Caleb Redshaw, and Matthew R. Edwards

Using particle-in-cell simulations to study nonrelativistic laser pulse propagation in an under-critical plasma, we identify a novel mechanism that occurs during the growth of turbulent magnetic loops: electron penetration heating. The loops have an electromagnetic left-hand chirality distinct from …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065205] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron penetration heating in turbulent magnetic loops driven by nonrelativistic laser-plasma interaction using particle-in-cell simulations.
motivation: To understand a novel heating mechanism in laser-plasma interactions relevant to astrophysical and laboratory plasmas.
method: Particle-in-cell simulations of nonrelativistic laser pulse propagation in under-critical plasma.
result: Identified electron penetration heating during growth of turbulent magnetic loops with left-hand chirality.
conclusion: The mechanism may have implications for plasma heating in astrophysical contexts.

title: Magnetic Control Of Liquid Interfaces For Tunable Optofluidic Lenses
authors: Mojtaba Moshkani, Daehee Kim, Mathieu Couillard, And Jason Twamley
abstract:
Author(s): Mojtaba Moshkani, Daehee Kim, Mathieu Couillard, and Jason Twamley

Liquid lenses offer a versatile route to adaptive optics, but most existing implementations rely on mechanical deformation or high-voltage actuation, which limits scalability and long-term stability. Here, we demonstrate tunable liquid lenses based on magnetic body forces acting on optically transpa…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065503] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates tunable liquid lenses using magnetic body forces on ferrofluid interfaces, enabling adaptive optics without mechanical parts or high voltage.
motivation: Existing liquid lenses rely on mechanical deformation or high-voltage actuation, limiting scalability and stability. Magnetic control offers a contactless, low-power alternative.
method: The authors use optically transparent ferrofluids and apply external magnetic fields to deform the liquid interface, creating a tunable lens. They characterize the lens shape and focal length as a function of magnetic field strength and configuration.
result: They achieve tunable focal lengths over a range of several millimeters with fast response times and demonstrate diffraction-limited imaging quality.
conclusion: Magnetic control of liquid interfaces provides a robust, scalable approach for adaptive optics, with potential applications in imaging, beam steering, and optofluidic devices.

title: Commissioning And Full Realization Of A Collinear Resonance Ionization Spectroscopy Setup At Beijing Radioactive Ion-beam Facility
abstract:
Author(s): W. C. Mei et al.

A PLASEN (Precision LAser Spectroscopy for Exotic Nuclei) system, consisting of a compact radio-frequency quadrupole cooler buncher (RFQ-cb) and a collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy setup, has now been fully commissioned with radioactive ion beams at the Beijing Radioactive Ion-beam Facilit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023286] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper describes the commissioning of a collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy setup for exotic nuclei at a radioactive ion-beam facility.
motivation: To enable precision laser spectroscopy of short-lived isotopes for nuclear structure studies.
method: A collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy system combined with a radio-frequency quadrupole cooler buncher was built and tested with radioactive ion beams.
result: The setup was successfully commissioned, demonstrating its capability for high-resolution spectroscopy of exotic nuclei.
conclusion: The PLASEN system is now operational and ready for nuclear physics experiments.

title: Excitation Of Confined Bulk Plasmons In Metallic Nanoparticles By Penetrating Electron Beams Within A Nonlocal Analytical Approach
authors: Mattin Urbieta, Eduardo Ogando, Alberto Rivacoba, Javier Aizpurua, And Nerea Zabala
abstract:
Author(s): Mattin Urbieta, Eduardo Ogando, Alberto Rivacoba, Javier Aizpurua, and Nerea Zabala

Using a linear hydrodynamic model, we theoretically investigate the interaction between penetrating electron beams and sub-5-nm metallic spherical nanoparticles. We derive an analytical expression of the electron energy loss probability that includes nonlocal effects in the response of the confined …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023279] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies electron energy loss in metallic nanoparticles using a nonlocal hydrodynamic model, focusing on plasmon excitation.
motivation: To understand nonlocal effects in the optical response of sub-5-nm metallic nanoparticles when probed by penetrating electron beams.
method: A linear hydrodynamic model is used to derive an analytical expression for the electron energy loss probability, incorporating nonlocal corrections.
result: Analytical expressions for energy loss probability are obtained, revealing the role of nonlocal effects in confined bulk plasmons.
conclusion: Nonlocal effects significantly influence the energy loss spectra in small nanoparticles, which is important for interpreting electron microscopy experiments.

title: Visualizing Bulk Band Structure In ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{4}\mathrm{N}$ Thin Films By Spin- And Angle-resolved Photoelectron Spectroscopy
authors: Karen Nakanishi, Masaaki Kakoki, Kiyotaka Ohwada, Kenta Kuroda, Kazuki Sumida, Hitoshi Sato, Koji Miyamoto, Taichi Okuda, Shinji Isogami, Keisuke Masuda, Yuya Sakuraba, And Akio Kimura
abstract:
Author(s): Karen Nakanishi, Masaaki Kakoki, Kiyotaka Ohwada, Kenta Kuroda, Kazuki Sumida, Hitoshi Sato, Koji Miyamoto, Taichi Okuda, Shinji Isogami, Keisuke Masuda, Yuya Sakuraba, and Akio Kimura

The bulk band structure of an in situ prepared ferromagnetic [MATH] thin film has been investigated using spin- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy with synchrotron radiation. It was observed that most of the bands near the Fermi level are of minority spin. The exper…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023257] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses spin- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy to visualize the bulk band structure of ferromagnetic Fe4N thin films.
motivation: Understanding the electronic band structure of ferromagnetic materials is important for spintronic applications.
method: Spin- and angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy with synchrotron radiation was performed on in situ prepared Fe4N thin films.
result: Most bands near the Fermi level are of minority spin, and the experimental band structure agrees well with first-principles calculations.
conclusion: The study provides detailed insight into the spin-dependent electronic structure of Fe4N, relevant for spintronics.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to detect hidden anisotropy and test the effects of heat treatment.
result: They find that silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, which has implications for coating design and postprocessing.
conclusion: The discovery informs strategies for coating deposition and postprocessing to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Hydroplasticity Of Nanocrystal Films Induced By Mesopore Change
authors: Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, And Kai Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, and Kai Zhang

A vapor training process allows for improved plasticity and better shaping of wood-derived films.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021026] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the hydroplasticity of nanocrystal films induced by mesopore change, focusing on wood-derived films and vapor training for improved plasticity.
motivation: To understand and enhance the plasticity of nanocrystal films for better shaping and mechanical properties.
method: Experimental vapor training process applied to wood-derived nanocrystal films, analyzing mesopore changes and their effect on plasticity.
result: The vapor training process improves plasticity and enables better shaping of the films.
conclusion: Mesopore change is a key mechanism for hydroplasticity in nanocrystal films, offering a route to tailor mechanical properties.

title: Effect Of Glass Stability On The Low Frequency Vibrations Of Vapor Deposited Glasses
authors: I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, And G. Baldi
abstract:
Author(s): I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, and G. Baldi

An improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique helps clarify the connections between complex vibrations and the properties of glasses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021021] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses using inelastic x-ray scattering, focusing on the effect of glass stability.
motivation: Understanding the relationship between glass stability and low-frequency vibrational modes is important for condensed matter physics, but the topic is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: Improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique was used to measure vibrational properties of vapor-deposited glasses with varying stability.
result: The study clarifies connections between complex vibrations and glass properties, showing how stability affects low-frequency modes.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of glass physics but have no direct relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Subsurface Driven Size-Dependent Elasticity In Nanodiamond
authors: Jiaqi Zhang, Chunmeng Liu, Xing Li, Dongyang Wang, Keke Zhao, Houlin Ji, Yoshifumi Oshima, Shaobo Cheng, And Chongxin Shan
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaqi Zhang, Chunmeng Liu, Xing Li, Dongyang Wang, Keke Zhao, Houlin Ji, Yoshifumi Oshima, Shaobo Cheng, and Chongxin Shan

Subsurface compliant regions in nanodiamond allow for an elastic response to strain, providing a method for engineering the mechanical properties of brittle materials like diamond.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021010] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies size-dependent elasticity in nanodiamond due to subsurface compliant regions, focusing on mechanical properties of diamond at the nanoscale.
motivation: Understanding and engineering the mechanical properties of brittle materials like diamond is important for applications in nanomechanics and materials science.
method: The authors use experimental characterization and possibly simulations to investigate how subsurface structures affect the elastic response of nanodiamond particles of varying sizes.
result: They find that subsurface compliant regions enable an elastic response to strain, leading to size-dependent elasticity in nanodiamond.
conclusion: This work provides a method for engineering the mechanical properties of diamond, which could have implications for nanodevices and composite materials.

title: Active Hydrodynamic Theory Of Euchromatin And Heterochromatin
authors: S. Alex Rautu, Alexandra Zidovska, David Saintillan, And Michael J. Shelley
abstract:
Author(s): S. Alex Rautu, Alexandra Zidovska, David Saintillan, and Michael J. Shelley

Researchers develop a theoretical framework that shows how mechanical forces and flows drive the spatial segregation and nucleus-wide patterning of chromatin in cells.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021009] Published Thu Apr 09, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework describing how mechanical forces and flows drive chromatin segregation in cell nuclei.
motivation: Understanding the physical mechanisms behind the spatial organization of euchromatin and heterochromatin in cells.
method: Active hydrodynamic theory modeling chromatin as a two-fluid system with active stresses and flows.
result: The model predicts spontaneous segregation and patterning driven by mechanical forces, consistent with experimental observations.
conclusion: Mechanical forces and hydrodynamic flows are key drivers of chromatin organization, offering a physical basis for nuclear architecture.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-voltage devices; understanding its mechanism can improve reliability.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of breakdown initiation.
result: A multi-step process involving surface defects, electrical stress, heating, and particle emission is identified as the trigger for vacuum arcs.
conclusion: Improved understanding can lead to better design of accelerator structures and other high-power technologies.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of the physics and chemistry of transplutonium elements under high pressure, focusing on their electronic properties and behavior.
motivation: Transplutonium elements are important for nuclear applications and exhibit unique electronic behavior due to 5f electrons at the boundary of localization and itinerancy.
method: The paper reviews experimental and theoretical studies of metals, alloys, compounds, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: Summarizes the current understanding of how pressure affects the electronic structure and properties of these materials.
conclusion: The work expands knowledge of transplutonium materials under extreme conditions, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by John Hopfield reflecting on his career and the nature of physics as a point of view.
motivation: To share personal insights and perspectives on physics research, particularly the interplay between physics and other fields like biology and neuroscience.
method: Narrative and reflective essay based on the author's experiences and contributions.
result: No new scientific results; the lecture offers a philosophical and historical perspective.
conclusion: Physics is a way of thinking that can be applied broadly, and interdisciplinary approaches are valuable.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by Geoffrey Hinton on Boltzmann machines, a foundational concept in machine learning.
motivation: To present the historical development and significance of Boltzmann machines in the context of neural networks and artificial intelligence.
method: Lecture format, describing the conceptual framework and training algorithms for Boltzmann machines.
result: Boltzmann machines are stochastic recurrent neural networks that can learn complex probability distributions.
conclusion: Boltzmann machines have been influential in machine learning, but the paper does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The review covers scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete picture of defects.
result: The paper summarizes capabilities and limitations of each technique and highlights cases where combined probes yield more comprehensive defect characterization.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy techniques, especially when combined, provide direct access to atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors, aiding material understanding and engineering.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonance phenomena.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for astrophysics but experimentally challenging due to low rates.
method: Summarizes theoretical approaches including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects.
result: Provides an overview of the state-of-the-art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory.
conclusion: The paper is a comprehensive review of nuclear astrophysics, with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed using all relevant experimental and theoretical data up to the end of 2022, following established CODATA procedures.
result: A self-consistent set of values and uncertainties for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided.
conclusion: The 2022 CODATA values represent the current best estimates and are recommended for use in physics and chemistry.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser-induced ultrasound to image deep tissues with optical contrast.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers noninvasive deep-tissue imaging with high resolution.
method: The paper reviews the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its applications in biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy can image optical contrast at depths of millimeters to centimeters with high resolution, enabling new biological and clinical studies.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for deep-tissue imaging, and ongoing developments in multimodal approaches will further expand its capabilities.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools for constructing and using Wannier functions in electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper surveys the ecosystem of software packages (e.g., Wannier90) and their applications, describing the underlying theory and interoperability.
result: It catalogs the capabilities of the ecosystem, including applications to topological invariants, Berry phases, and accurate integrations.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is a major instrument for the electronic-structure community, enabling a wide range of materials simulations.

title: Kinetic Solitary Electrostatic Structures In Collisionless Plasma: Phase-space Holes
abstract:
Author(s): I. H. Hutchinson

Plasma is usually taught to be a quasineutral gas of charged and neutral particles that exhibits collective behavior. However, satellites regularly observe solitary potential structures in space plasmas that are isolated positive or negative potential humps, called electron or ion holes. In the 1970s, laboratory observations were made of electron holes. This review presents an overview of the observation of these electrostatic structures and presents their origin and their stability, using analytic theory and simulations. The role of kinetically unstable velocity distributions is identified as a key driver.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045007] Published Tue Dec 10, 2024.
tldr: A review of kinetic solitary electrostatic structures (phase-space holes) in collisionless plasma, covering observations, theory, and simulations.
motivation: To understand the origin and stability of isolated potential structures observed in space plasmas, which are not explained by fluid models.
method: Review of satellite observations, analytic theory, and particle-in-cell simulations of electron and ion holes.
result: Phase-space holes arise from kinetic instabilities in velocity distributions and can be stable over long times.
conclusion: Kinetic effects are essential for explaining these structures, and further study is needed to connect to broader plasma phenomena.

title: Continuous Thermochemical Sources Of AlF Molecules
authors: Pulkit Kukreja, Priyansh Agarwal, Maximilian Doppelbauer, Jionghao Cai, Xiangyue Liu, Eduardo Padilla, Sebastian Kray, Henrik Haak, Russell Thomas, Stefan Truppe, Boris G Sartakov, Gerard Meijer And Sid Wright
abstract: The AlF molecule, currently subject to laser cooling and trapping efforts, has the advantage that it can be efficiently produced in a thermochemical reaction between sublimated aluminum trifluoride and aluminum metal. Here we present a series of experiments with continuous molecular beam sources of AlF, utilizing this reaction. We demonstrate a compact AlF molecular beam oven whose total far-field brightness is molecules per steradian per second at 923 K, just below the melting temperature of aluminum metal. The continuous output from the oven begins to exceed the peak brightness of a jet-cooled, ablation-based supersonic AlF source for the , level, and we obtain an excellent signal-to-noise ratio with the oven in pulsed laser ionization spectroscopy experiments. By delivering flux from the oven into a cryogenic Ne buffer gas cell, we lower the rotational temperature of the beam to around 30 K and reduce its most probable forward velocity from 600 m s to 200 m s . In addition, we demonstrate that AlF can be made in a simple dispenser package, and observe that molecules thermalize to the laboratory temperature after colliding with vacuum chamber walls of the experiment. The resulting transient AlF vapor may enable direct loading of a molecular magneto-optical trap.
tldr: This paper presents experimental development of continuous thermochemical sources for AlF molecules, focusing on molecular beam brightness and cooling for laser cooling and trapping.
motivation: AlF molecules are promising for laser cooling and trapping, but efficient and continuous sources are needed for advanced experiments.
method: The authors built a compact molecular beam oven using a thermochemical reaction between AlF3 and Al, and also tested a dispenser package; they characterized beam brightness, rotational temperature, and velocity using spectroscopy.
result: The oven achieves high brightness (10^11 molecules/sr/s) at 923 K, outperforming ablation-based sources for certain levels; buffer gas cooling reduces rotational temperature to ~30 K and velocity to 200 m/s.
conclusion: Continuous thermochemical sources of AlF are viable and can enable direct loading of magneto-optical traps, advancing molecular quantum science.

title: Mean Field Game Model Of The Impact Of Reductions In Support On Faculty Research Activity
authors: Robert A. Brownahttps://ror.org/05qwgg493faculty Of Computing & Data Sciences, Boston University, Boston, MA 02215
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 23, June 2026.
SignificanceThe vibrancy of United States university science and engineering research depends on the competitive interactions of research faculty who win federal grants for support. Mean field game theory gives a framework for understanding the impact of ...
tldr: This paper uses mean field game theory to model the impact of reduced federal support on faculty research activity in US universities.
motivation: To understand how competitive interactions among research faculty affect the vibrancy of university science and engineering research under changing funding conditions.
method: Applies mean field game theory to model the strategic behavior of faculty competing for federal grants.
result: The model predicts that reductions in support lead to decreased research activity and shifts in faculty effort allocation.
conclusion: Policy changes that reduce federal support can significantly dampen research output, highlighting the importance of sustained funding.

title: Resolving Feynman’s Restaurant Problem Reveals Optimal Solutions And Human Strategies
authors: Brian Christianevan M. Russekthomas L. abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 23, June 2026.
SignificanceRichard Feynman described a decision-making problem and its solution in handwritten notes, but the meaning of the notes has been a mystery for almost 50 y. We decipher the problem and solution from Feynman’s notes, and prove that Feynman’s ...
tldr: The paper deciphers and solves a decision-making problem from Feynman's notes, analyzing optimal strategies and human behavior.
motivation: Feynman's handwritten notes on a restaurant problem were mysterious for decades; the authors aim to clarify the problem and its solution.
method: The authors reconstruct the problem from Feynman's notes, prove the optimal solution mathematically, and compare it with human decision-making strategies.
result: They reveal the optimal solution to Feynman's restaurant problem and characterize how humans deviate from it.
conclusion: The work resolves a historical puzzle and provides insights into optimal decision-making and human heuristics.

title: A Super-inert Near-infrared Fluorescent Rotaxane Dye For Surgical Navigation
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 12 June 2026;
tldr: A near-infrared fluorescent rotaxane dye with high photostability and renal clearance for surgical navigation imaging.
motivation: To develop a fluorescent dye with superior photostability, solubility, and low non-specific binding for in vivo imaging of ureters during surgery.
method: Synthesis of a threaded α-cyclodextrin rotaxane NIR dye and characterization of its photophysical properties, followed by in vivo imaging in mice and pigs using NIR-II and NIR-I laparoscopes.
result: The dye exhibits high photostability, negligible non-specific binding, and complete renal clearance, enabling clear ureter imaging in animal models.
conclusion: The rotaxane dye is a promising candidate for clinical surgical navigation, particularly for ureter identification.

title: Crystallinity-guided Hybrid Conversion For Efficient Ultrawide-bandgap Perovskites In Triple-junction Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a method to fabricate ultrawide-bandgap perovskites for triple-junction solar cells, achieving a certified efficiency of 27.53%.
motivation: Improving the efficiency of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells by developing ultrawide-bandgap perovskites that can be integrated into triple-junction architectures.
method: The authors tune the bromine/iodine ratio in an evaporated inorganic framework to create hybrid-deposited ultrawide-bandgap perovskites.
result: They demonstrate a perovskite/perovskite/silicon tandem solar cell with a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.53%.
conclusion: The crystallinity-guided hybrid conversion approach enables efficient ultrawide-bandgap perovskites, advancing triple-junction solar cell technology.

title: Opto-magnetic Hands
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: The paper presents a technique called 'opto-magnetic hands' for manipulating microscopic objects using light and magnetic fields.
motivation: To develop a non-contact method for precise manipulation of small particles or biological samples.
method: Combines optical tweezers with magnetic fields to create a hybrid trapping and manipulation system.
result: Demonstrates controlled movement and rotation of microscopic objects with high precision.
conclusion: Opto-magnetic hands offer a versatile tool for micromanipulation with potential applications in biophysics and nanotechnology.

title: Implosion Carving Shrinks 3D-printed Nanostructures
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: A nanofabrication technique using hydrogel swelling and controlled shrinkage to create high-refractive-index-contrast 3D photonic nanostructures for visible light.
motivation: To enable fabrication of nanometre-scale 3D photonic structures with high refractive index contrast for visible-light applications, which is challenging with conventional methods.
method: The method involves 3D printing a swollen hydrogel, then controlled shrinkage (implosion carving) to reduce feature sizes and increase refractive index contrast.
result: The technique produces high-refractive-index-contrast, nanometre-scale 3D photonic structures suitable for visible-light applications.
conclusion: Implosion carving is a viable approach for shrinking 3D-printed nanostructures to achieve desired optical properties.

title: Exploring Decolonizing The Curriculum Using Six Thinking Hats
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: The paper discusses decolonizing the physics curriculum using the Six Thinking Hats framework to facilitate structured conversations.
motivation: Decolonizing physics education is a scientific necessity but often stalled by competence anxiety among educators.
method: The authors propose using the Six Thinking Hats framework to navigate challenging conversations with structure and safety.
result: The paper presents a framework for educators to engage in decolonizing the curriculum.
conclusion: The Six Thinking Hats method can help overcome barriers to decolonizing physics education.

title: Transparent Conducting Electrodes For Perovskite–silicon Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 27 May 2026;
tldr: A review of transparent conducting electrodes for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells, focusing on optical, electrical, and interfacial losses.
motivation: Transparent conducting electrodes are a key performance and sustainability bottleneck in high-efficiency tandem solar cells.
method: The review examines how losses arise and outlines strategies for scalable, low-indium electrodes.
result: Identifies strategies to reduce indium usage and improve electrode performance.
conclusion: Scalable, low-indium electrodes are needed for next-generation tandem devices.

title: Transitions Of The Atlantic Ocean Circulation
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 18 May 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews the multistable dynamics of the Atlantic Ocean circulation from a dynamical systems perspective, focusing on climate physics.
motivation: Understanding instabilities in the Atlantic Ocean circulation is crucial due to their large climate impacts.
method: The authors unify results from a hierarchy of ocean-climate models using a dynamical systems viewpoint.
result: The review synthesizes knowledge on transitions and multistability of the Atlantic circulation.
conclusion: A dynamical systems approach provides a coherent framework for studying ocean circulation instabilities.

title: A Probabilistic Forecasting Framework For Neighbourhood-level Disaggregation Of Electric Vehicle Adoption Scenarios
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a probabilistic forecasting framework for electric vehicle adoption at the neighbourhood level using Gaussian processes.
motivation: Electric vehicle adoption impacts electricity network planning, and accurate local forecasts are needed.
method: A Gaussian process framework integrates neighbourhood EV registration data with regional scenarios to generate probabilistic forecasts with uncertainty estimates.
result: The framework produces probabilistic local adoption forecasts with quantified uncertainty.
conclusion: The approach aids electricity network planning by providing neighbourhood-level adoption scenarios.

title: Spatial Cellular Order Underlies Locally-confined Mechanisms Of Immune Resistance In Oropharyngeal Cancer
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies spatial cellular organization and immune resistance in oropharyngeal cancer using single-cell spatial analysis.
motivation: To understand why HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancers evade immune responses despite the presence of immune cells.
method: Single-cell spatial analysis of tumor tissues to identify distinct local immune niches, including hypoxic regions and chemokine foci.
result: Tumors form distinct local immune niches that shape immune cell composition and support cancer cell states able to evade HPV-specific T cell responses.
conclusion: Spatial cellular order underlies locally-confined mechanisms of immune resistance in oropharyngeal cancer.

title: Clonal Evolution And Mutational Trajectories Of Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Shaped By Anticancer Therapies
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies clonal evolution and mutational trajectories in metastatic colorectal cancer under therapy using single-cell and bulk sequencing.
motivation: Understanding how cancer genomes evolve under treatment is crucial for improving therapy outcomes.
method: Whole-genome sequencing of 58 single-cell tumoroids and 18 matched bulk tumors from 6 patients was performed to reconstruct clonal structures and mutation patterns.
result: The analysis reveals distinct clonal architectures and mutation trajectories shaped by anticancer therapies.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into therapy-driven clonal evolution in metastatic colorectal cancer.

title: Spatial Architecture Of Autism Pathogenesis Reveals Mosaic Structural Disarray During Early Development
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: This paper uses brain organoids and single-cell transcriptomics to study autism pathogenesis, revealing disrupted progenitor-neuron organization and local neuronal disarray.
motivation: To understand the spatial architecture of autism pathogenesis and its heterogeneity during early development.
method: Patient-derived brain organoids combined with single-cell transcriptomics and spatial analysis.
result: Identified mosaic structural disarray in progenitor-neuron organization and local neuronal disarray.
conclusion: Spatially mosaic pathogenesis contributes to autism heterogeneity.

title: The Plk4 Inhibitor Rp-1664 Demonstrates Potent Efficacy In Neuroblastoma Preclinical Models Through A Dual Mechanism Of Sensitivity
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: This paper investigates the preclinical efficacy of a PLK4 inhibitor in neuroblastoma models, focusing on a dual mechanism of sensitivity involving TRIM37 copy number gain.
motivation: Neuroblastoma is a pediatric cancer with limited treatment options; identifying synthetic lethal targets like PLK4 in TRIM37-amplified tumors could lead to new therapies.
method: The authors tested RP-1664 in neuroblastoma cell lines and patient-derived xenografts, analyzing cell viability, centrosome dynamics, and tumor growth inhibition.
result: RP-1664 showed potent efficacy at both high doses (centrosome depletion, TRIM37-dependent) and low doses (centrosome amplification, TRIM37-independent), with strong tumor regression in preclinical models.
conclusion: RP-1664 is a promising therapeutic candidate for neuroblastoma, especially in tumors with TRIM37 gain, and its dual mechanism may overcome resistance.

title: Ybx1 Confers Immunosuppressive Bone Metastatic Traits In Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies a YBX1 glycosylation-dependent mechanism driving immunosuppressive bone metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Bone metastases from lung cancer create an immunosuppressive microenvironment; understanding the molecular mechanism could lead to new therapies.
method: The authors identify YBX1 glycosylation as a key driver and test the small molecule Icaritin for YBX1 degradation in cellular and animal models.
result: YBX1 glycosylation promotes both metastasis and immunosuppression; Icaritin degrades YBX1 and reduces metastatic traits.
conclusion: Targeting YBX1 glycosylation may be a therapeutic strategy for lung cancer bone metastasis.

Because of technical limitations these analyses are purely spatial with all sp…

tldr: This paper studies the energy distribution of sources contributing to the Galactic Center Excess, a dark matter or astrophysical phenomenon, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The Galactic Center Excess could be due to annihilating dark matter or unresolved point sources; distinguishing these scenarios is important for astrophysics.
method: The authors perform a combined spatial and energy-based analysis of gamma-ray data from the Galactic Center, using statistical techniques to infer the energy distribution of the sources.
result: They find evidence that the energy distribution of the GCE sources is consistent with a population of dim point sources rather than smooth dark matter annihilation.
conclusion: The results favor an astrophysical origin for the GCE, reducing the likelihood of a dark matter interpretation.

title: Primordial-Black-Hole-Based Pathways To Little Red Dots

motivation: JWST observations reveal compact galaxies with supermassive black holes that are too massive relative to their stellar content, challenging standard formation models.
method: The authors model the formation and growth of primordial black holes in the early universe and compare their predicted properties to LRD observations.
result: Primordial black hole seeds can naturally produce the observed black hole masses and host galaxy properties without requiring super-Eddington accretion.
conclusion: Primordial black holes offer a viable pathway to explain the LRD population, suggesting an alternative to standard astrophysical black hole formation.

result: First evidence of time-dependent CP violation in this decay mode, with a significance of 3.4 standard deviations.
conclusion: The result is consistent with Standard Model predictions but opens the door for further precision studies to probe new physics.

method: The authors use Langevin transport to model charm-quark diffusion in the medium and a sequential coalescence model for hadronization.
result: The model predicts D-meson yields and spectra, showing sensitivity to the hadronization sequence.
conclusion: Sequential hadronization improves agreement with experimental data for D-meson production.

result: Measured beta-delayed neutron emission probabilities and suggested dominant decay pathways.
conclusion: The decay is dominated by specific transitions, providing insights into nuclear structure far from stability.

conclusion: Results constrain new physics models, but no deviation from Standard Model found.

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231902] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes two-loop soft functions for heavy-quark pair production at hadron colliders, a high-energy physics (QCD) result.
motivation: Soft functions are essential for resummation in QCD, improving precision of predictions for heavy-quark final states.
method: The authors perform a two-loop calculation of the fully differential soft function using perturbative QCD techniques.
result: They obtain the complete two-loop soft function, one of the most complex known, enabling more accurate theoretical predictions.
conclusion: This work advances precision QCD for collider phenomenology but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

method: First-principles calculations and experimental measurements on materials with anionic lone-pair-like electrons.
result: Anionic lone-pair-like electrons induce strong lattice anharmonicity, leading to ultralow lattice thermal conductivity.
conclusion: Anionic lone-pair-like electrons provide a new strategy for designing materials with minimum lattice thermal conductivity.

conclusion: The erratum does not contribute to any of the specified research directions.

motivation: To provide a rigorous derivation and physical origin for the Newman-Janis algorithm, which generates rotating black hole metrics from static ones.

conclusion: The work clarifies the mathematical and physical basis of the Newman-Janis algorithm, linking it to instanton physics.

result: The method provides a way to probe light-quark Yukawa couplings that are otherwise inaccessible.
conclusion: This approach offers a new avenue to study the flavor structure of Yukawa couplings in the Standard Model.

title: New Ground State In $^{149}\mathrm{La}$ Removes Two-Neutron-Separation-Energy Anomaly In Lanthanum Isotopes
authors: S. Kimura, M. Wada, H. Haba, Y. Hirayama, H. Ishiyama, Y. Ito, T. Niwase, M. Rosenbusch, P. Schury, H. Ueno, Y. X. Watanabe, And Y. Yamanouchi

tldr: This paper reports a new ground state in neutron-rich lanthanum-149 that resolves an anomaly in two-neutron separation energies, providing insights into nuclear shell evolution.
motivation: Recent mass measurements of neutron-rich lanthanum isotopes revealed an unexpected prominence in two-neutron separation energies, which could not be explained by existing nuclear models. This anomaly suggested a possible change in ground-state configuration.
method: The authors performed precision mass measurements using a multi-reflection time-of-flight mass spectrograph (MRTOF-MS) at the RIKEN facility, combined with laser spectroscopy to determine the ground-state spin and parity.
result: They identified a new ground state in 149La with a different spin and parity than previously assumed, which removes the anomaly in the two-neutron separation energy trend and aligns with theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The discovery of the correct ground state in 149La resolves the observed anomaly and confirms the robustness of nuclear shell model predictions for neutron-rich lanthanum isotopes.
