authors: Seamus F. Gallagher And Markus Deserno
abstract:
Author(s): Seamus F. Gallagher and Markus Deserno

Fission and fusion of lipid membranes are ubiquitous shape transformations in living cells, necessary for maintaining the shape of organelles and enabling a host of transport processes between them. These topology-changing events involve curvature-elastic free energy changes proportional to the Gaus…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 238201] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a topological method to measure the Gaussian curvature modulus of lipid membranes in simulations.
motivation: Understanding the Gaussian curvature modulus is crucial for modeling membrane fission and fusion, which are essential cellular processes.
method: The authors develop a computational approach based on the Gauss-Bonnet theorem to extract the Gaussian curvature modulus from molecular dynamics simulations of lipid bilayers.
result: They demonstrate the method's accuracy on simulated membrane shapes and provide estimates of the Gaussian curvature modulus for common lipid types.
conclusion: The proposed technique enables reliable measurement of a key elastic parameter, facilitating more accurate modeling of membrane remodeling events.

title: Unified Treatment Of Direct And Resonant Scattering In Low-energy $\text{electron}\text{−}{\mathrm{H}}_{2}$ Vibrational Excitation: Boomerang Oscillations And The $υ=0→1$ Excitation
authors: Liam H. Scarlett, Nathan A. Garland, Gregory J. Boyle, Dale L. Muccignat, Ronald D. White, Mark C. Zammit, Ilkhom B. Abdurakhmanov, Maciej Cytowski, Igor Bray, And Dmitry V. Fursa
abstract:
Author(s): Liam H. Scarlett, Nathan A. Garland, Gregory J. Boyle, Dale L. Muccignat, Ronald D. White, Mark C. Zammit, Ilkhom B. Abdurakhmanov, Maciej Cytowski, Igor Bray, and Dmitry V. Fursa

The vibrational excitation of molecular hydrogen [MATH] by low-energy electrons is one of the most fundamental reactions in atomic and molecular physics, playing a key role in the chemistry of the interstellar medium and studies of fusion plasmas. Crossed-beam experiments and electron …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062803] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-energy electron-H2 vibrational excitation using a unified treatment of direct and resonant scattering, focusing on boomerang oscillations and cross sections.
motivation: Understanding electron-molecule collisions is important for interstellar chemistry and fusion plasma modeling.
method: The authors employ a computational approach combining direct and resonant scattering theories to calculate vibrational excitation cross sections.
result: They reproduce boomerang oscillations and provide accurate cross sections for the v=0→1 excitation.
conclusion: The unified treatment successfully describes the scattering process and yields results consistent with experiments.

title: High-order Harmonic Generation In Argon Driven By Short Laser Pulses: Effects Of Post-pulse Propagation And Windowing
authors: Aaron T. Bondy And Klaus Bartschat
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron T. Bondy and Klaus Bartschat

We present ab initio calculations using the [MATH]-matrix with time dependence method for high-order harmonic generation (HHG) in argon in a short, intense pulse regime. The calculations employ a six-cycle [MATH] pulse at 850 nm with peak intensity $2.3×{10}^{14}{0ex}}\mathrm…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063108] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents ab initio calculations of high-order harmonic generation in argon driven by short laser pulses, focusing on post-pulse propagation and windowing effects.
motivation: To understand the effects of post-pulse propagation and windowing on high-order harmonic generation in argon, which is relevant for attosecond science and strong-field physics.
method: The authors use the R-matrix with time dependence method to simulate HHG in argon under a six-cycle 850 nm pulse at peak intensity 2.3×10^14 W/cm^2.
result: The calculations show how post-pulse propagation and windowing influence the harmonic spectrum, including modifications to the cutoff and efficiency.
conclusion: Post-pulse propagation and windowing are important for accurately modeling HHG in short-pulse regimes, with implications for experimental design.

title: Critical Yet Subtle Role Of Cap Configuration In Single-walled Carbon Nanotube Solid-catalytic Growth
authors: Tianliang Feng, Ziwei Xu, And Feng Ding
abstract:
Author(s): Tianliang Feng, Ziwei Xu, and Feng Ding

We propose a novel and intuitive algorithm that determines the chirality of nascent carbon caps by tracking the relative shifts of six pentagons within a topological coordinate system. Based on this algorithm, we propose three chirality mutation routes for pentagon shifts from armchair (AC) to near-…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235417] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the role of cap configuration in determining chirality during carbon nanotube growth, using a topological algorithm to track pentagon shifts.
motivation: Understanding chirality control in carbon nanotube synthesis is important for applications, but the paper focuses on materials science rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors propose an algorithm to determine chirality of nascent carbon caps by tracking pentagon shifts in a topological coordinate system, and identify chirality mutation routes.
result: Three chirality mutation routes from armchair to near-armchair configurations are identified, highlighting the critical role of cap configuration.
conclusion: The cap configuration plays a subtle but critical role in determining nanotube chirality during solid-catalytic growth.

title: Spinel $\mathrm{Li}{\mathrm{Ga}}_{5}{\mathrm{O}}_{8}$ As A $p$-type Ultrawide Band Gap Semiconductor: A Critical Theoretical Reevaluation
abstract:
Author(s): Yongcheng Zhu and Zewen Xiao

Transparent oxide semiconductors are pivotal for optoelectronic applications, but the development of [MATH]-type ones, especially those with ultrawide band gaps, remains a significant challenge. Recently, spinel [MATH] (band gap approximately 5.3 eV) was reported…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235205] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical reevaluation of spinel LiGa5O8 as a p-type ultrawide band gap semiconductor, focusing on electronic structure and defect properties.
motivation: To address the challenge of developing p-type transparent oxide semiconductors with ultrawide band gaps for optoelectronic applications.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) to compute band structure, formation energies, and defect levels.
result: The paper critically reassesses previous claims and provides revised understanding of the electronic and defect properties of LiGa5O8.
conclusion: LiGa5O8 may not be as promising for p-type conductivity as previously reported, highlighting the need for further theoretical and experimental investigation.

title: Vector Resonant Relaxation And Statistical Closure Theory. Ii. One-loop Closure
abstract:
Author(s): Sofia Flores and Jean-Baptiste Fouvry

The dynamics of stars orbiting a supermassive black hole can be used as a test case for statistical closure schemes that allow the calculation of dynamical correlation functions in the fully nonlinear and nonperturbative regime. The authors develop an iterative scheme based on the Martin–Siggia–Rose formalism, and find that it compares well with numerical simulations.

#AdvancingField #TechnicalAdvancement


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064127] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a statistical closure scheme for stellar dynamics around a supermassive black hole using the Martin–Siggia–Rose formalism.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of stars orbiting a supermassive black hole and test statistical closure schemes in the nonlinear regime.
method: An iterative scheme based on the Martin–Siggia–Rose formalism is developed and compared with numerical simulations.
result: The iterative scheme compares well with numerical simulations.
conclusion: The proposed closure scheme is effective for calculating dynamical correlation functions in this astrophysical context.

title: Threshold And Quasistationary Distribution For The Susceptible-infectious-susceptible Model On Networks
authors: George T. Cantwell And Cristopher Moore
abstract:
Author(s): George T. Cantwell and Cristopher Moore

Giving nodes a memory of their susceptibility transition dynamically expands the state space in the susceptible-infectious-susceptible model. This enhanced pair approximation accurately determines epidemic thresholds and infection fractions across arbitrary networks.

#ClassicalProblem #UniversalBehavior


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064305] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies epidemic thresholds and quasistationary distributions for the SIS model on networks using an enhanced pair approximation.
motivation: Understanding epidemic spread on networks is important for public health, but the paper focuses on classical epidemiological modeling.
method: The authors introduce a memory of susceptibility transition to expand the state space and apply an enhanced pair approximation to analyze the SIS model on arbitrary networks.
result: The enhanced pair approximation accurately determines epidemic thresholds and infection fractions across arbitrary networks.
conclusion: The method provides a more accurate analytical tool for studying epidemic dynamics on networks.

title: Kinetic And Fluid Descriptions Of Jeans Instability In Kappa-distributed Suprathermal Astrophysical Plasmas
authors: Pooja Dalal And Ram Prasad Prajapati
abstract:
Author(s): Pooja Dalal and Ram Prasad Prajapati

The Jeans instability in an unmagnetized, collisionless self-gravitating plasma characterized by a kappa or Lorentzian velocity distribution is investigated in the framework of kinetic and fluid approaches. We have examined the role of suprathermality on the instability threshold wave number and gro…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065208] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Jeans instability in astrophysical plasmas with kappa-distributed suprathermal particles using kinetic and fluid models.
motivation: To understand the effect of suprathermal particle distributions on gravitational instability in astrophysical plasmas.
method: Kinetic theory with Vlasov-Poisson system and fluid equations with kappa-distributed pressure closure.
result: Suprathermality modifies the instability threshold wave number and growth rate compared to Maxwellian plasmas.
conclusion: Kappa distributions significantly affect Jeans instability, important for astrophysical structure formation.

title: Wake-tail Effects In Two-dimensional Wave Refocusing
abstract:
Author(s): Theodoros T. Koutserimpas

In even spatial dimensions, solutions of the wave equation violate Huygens' principle, producing a persistent wake tail inside the light cone rather than a sharply localized propagating front. This intrinsic tail complicates refocusing. Here, we examine how the wake-tail structure of the two-dimensi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065102] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wake-tail effects in two-dimensional wave refocusing, a topic in classical wave physics with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding how the violation of Huygens' principle in even dimensions affects wave refocusing is a fundamental problem in classical wave theory.
method: The author analytically and numerically examines the wake-tail structure of the two-dimensional wave equation and its impact on refocusing.
result: The wake tail causes persistent afterglow that degrades the quality of refocusing compared to three-dimensional waves.
conclusion: The findings highlight intrinsic limitations of wave refocusing in two dimensions due to the wake tail.

title: Resonance Behavior Of A Bubble Near A Spherical Inclusion
authors: Thomas Micol, Alexander A. Doinikov, Cyril Mauger, And Claude Inserra
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Micol, Alexander A. Doinikov, Cyril Mauger, and Claude Inserra

We present an analytical model for the frequency response of a gas microbubble oscillating near a spherical inclusion of arbitrary size and mechanical nature (rigid, fluid, or viscoelastic) immersed in a viscous compressible fluid. The model considers both radial and nonspherical oscillations in the…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065103] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the frequency response of a gas microbubble oscillating near a spherical inclusion in a viscous fluid.
motivation: Understanding bubble dynamics near inclusions is important for applications like ultrasound contrast agents and cavitation.
method: An analytical model is developed for radial and nonspherical oscillations of a bubble near a rigid, fluid, or viscoelastic spherical inclusion in a compressible viscous fluid.
result: The model predicts resonance behavior and frequency shifts depending on the inclusion's size and mechanical properties.
conclusion: The analytical model provides insights into bubble-inclusion interactions, which can guide experimental design in acoustics.

title: Humidity As A Critical Parameter For Predicting Breakdown Voltage In Submicrometer Electrode Gaps In Air
authors: B. Disson, N. Bonifaci, O. Lesaint, C. Poulain, R. Dussart, And S. Iseni
abstract:
Author(s): B. Disson, N. Bonifaci, O. Lesaint, C. Poulain, R. Dussart, and S. Iseni

This experimental work reinvestigates the breakdown voltage in air for electrode gaps ranging from [MATH] to [MATH]. Rarely addressed in the literature of the field, a special focus is placed on varying the gas humidity and its direct impact on the breakdown vo…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065207] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies the effect of humidity on breakdown voltage in submicrometer air gaps.
motivation: Understanding breakdown in small gaps is important for microelectronics and MEMS, but humidity effects are rarely addressed.
method: Experimental measurements of breakdown voltage in air for electrode gaps from 0.5 to 10 μm under controlled humidity conditions.
result: Humidity significantly affects breakdown voltage, with higher humidity reducing the voltage required for breakdown.
conclusion: Humidity must be considered as a critical parameter for predicting breakdown in submicrometer gaps.

title: Linear Rayleigh-Taylor Instability With Foams
authors: A. Bret, A. J. Devault, S. G. Dannhoff, M. Gatu Johnson, C. K. Li, And J. A. Frenje
abstract:
Author(s): A. Bret, A. J. DeVault, S. G. Dannhoff, M. Gatu Johnson, C. K. Li, and J. A. Frenje

We analyze the behavior of the linear phase of the Rayleigh-Taylor instability (RTI) in the presence of a foam. Such a problem may be relevant, for example, to some inertial confinement fusion (ICF) scenarios such as foams within the capsule or lining the inner hohlraum wall. The foam displays three…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065409] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the linear phase of the Rayleigh-Taylor instability in the presence of a foam, relevant to inertial confinement fusion.
motivation: Understanding the effect of foams on the Rayleigh-Taylor instability is important for improving inertial confinement fusion designs.
method: The authors perform a linear stability analysis of the Rayleigh-Taylor instability with a foam modeled as a porous medium, deriving dispersion relations.
result: The foam modifies the growth rate and wavelength of the instability, with potential stabilizing effects depending on foam parameters.
conclusion: Foams can influence the linear Rayleigh-Taylor instability, which may be exploited to mitigate instabilities in ICF capsules.

title: Edwards Thermodynamic Framework Controls Density Segregation In Cyclically Sheared Granular Materials
authors: Haiyang Lu, Houfei Yuan, Shuyang Zhang, Zhikun Zeng, Yi Xing, Jiazhao Xu, Xin Wang, And Yujie Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Haiyang Lu, Houfei Yuan, Shuyang Zhang, Zhikun Zeng, Yi Xing, Jiazhao Xu, Xin Wang, and Yujie Wang

Granular segregation is a widespread phenomenon observed in various industrial applications, geophysical processes, and daily life events. It can be driven by multiple mechanisms, and numerous models have been proposed to elucidate this behavior. However, most of these models are phenomenological an…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065407] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies density segregation in granular materials under cyclic shear using Edwards' thermodynamic framework.
motivation: Granular segregation is common in industry and nature, but existing models are phenomenological and lack a unified thermodynamic basis.
method: The authors apply Edwards' statistical mechanics of granular matter, treating density as a thermodynamic variable, and perform cyclic shear experiments to test predictions.
result: The Edwards framework successfully predicts the observed density segregation patterns, showing that the system evolves towards a state of maximum entropy.
conclusion: Edwards' thermodynamic approach provides a quantitative and predictive model for granular segregation, unifying previous phenomenological descriptions.

title: Higher-order Contagion Processes In 3.99 Dimensions
authors: Sandro Meloni, Andrea Gabrielli, And Pablo Villegas
abstract:
Author(s): Sandro Meloni, Andrea Gabrielli, and Pablo Villegas

Higher-order interactions have recently emerged as a promising framework for describing new dynamical phenomena in heterogeneous contagion processes. However, a fundamental open question is how to understand their contribution from the perspective of the physics of critical phenomena. Based on a mes…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062301] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies higher-order contagion processes from a critical phenomena perspective in 3.99 dimensions.
motivation: Understanding the role of higher-order interactions in contagion dynamics is an open question, especially from the viewpoint of critical phenomena.
method: The authors use a mesoscopic approach and renormalization group techniques to analyze contagion models with higher-order interactions near the upper critical dimension.
result: They derive scaling laws and critical exponents for the contagion process in 3.99 dimensions.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions modify the critical behavior, but the paper remains within the realm of classical statistical physics and network science.

title: Innate Behavioral Mechanisms And Defensive Traits In Ecological Models Of Predator-prey Types
authors: Sangeeta Saha, Swadesh Pal, And Roderick Melnik
abstract:
Author(s): Sangeeta Saha, Swadesh Pal, and Roderick Melnik

Phenotypic plasticity enables prey species to develop inducible defences in response to predation risk, significantly influencing predator-prey interactions. In this study, we propose a nonlinear predator-prey model in which prey exhibit inducible defense mechanisms, while predators experience mutua…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064203] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper models predator-prey dynamics with inducible prey defenses and mutual interference among predators using nonlinear differential equations.
motivation: To understand how phenotypic plasticity in prey and mutual interference among predators affect ecological stability and population dynamics.
method: A nonlinear predator-prey model is proposed and analyzed using dynamical systems theory, including stability analysis and bifurcation analysis.
result: The model exhibits complex dynamics such as limit cycles and bistability, depending on defense strength and interference parameters.
conclusion: Inducible defenses and predator mutual interference can stabilize or destabilize predator-prey systems, with implications for ecological management.

title: Zonal Magnetic Fields Regulate Nonlinear Edge-localized-mode Dynamics Via Self-consistent Force Balance
authors: Nami Li, Xueqiao Xu, Ben Dudson, Rob Falgout, And Giorgis Georgakoudis
abstract:
Author(s): Nami Li, Xueqiao Xu, Ben Dudson, Rob Falgout, and Giorgis Georgakoudis

Edge-localized modes (ELMs) eject intense bursts of heat and particles that threaten plasma-facing components in fusion reactors. Nonlinear full-torus [MATH] simulations show that turbulence-driven zonal magnetic fields (ZMFs) play an essential role in nonlinear ELM evolution by maintaini…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065204] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies zonal magnetic fields in edge-localized modes in fusion plasmas, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Edge-localized modes threaten fusion reactor components, so understanding their nonlinear dynamics is crucial for reactor design.
method: Nonlinear full-torus MHD simulations are used to model the effect of turbulence-driven zonal magnetic fields on ELM evolution.
result: Zonal magnetic fields regulate ELM dynamics through self-consistent force balance, affecting heat and particle bursts.
conclusion: Zonal magnetic fields play an essential role in nonlinear ELM evolution and should be considered in fusion plasma control strategies.

title: Effects Of Hydrodynamic Motion On The Stopping Power And Energy Deposition Of Alpha Particles In An Inertial Confinement Fusion Hotspot
authors: Bao Du, Dongguo Kang, Peilin Yao, Fengjun Ge, Zhensheng Dai, Shiyang Zou, Zongqiang Yuan, Lianqiang Shan, Hongbo Cai, And Shaoping Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Bao Du, Dongguo Kang, Peilin Yao, Fengjun Ge, Zhensheng Dai, Shiyang Zou, Zongqiang Yuan, Lianqiang Shan, Hongbo Cai, and Shaoping Zhu

The outflow velocity of expanding deuterium-tritium (DT) fuel can become significant after the bangtime, approaching local ion thermal velocity when the inertial confinement fusion (ICF) hotspot surpasses the ignition threshold. Under such conditions, the conventional assumption of an isotropic targ…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065206] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of hydrodynamic motion on alpha particle stopping power in inertial confinement fusion hotspots.
motivation: In ICF hotspots, the outflow velocity of DT fuel can become significant, invalidating the usual isotropic target assumption and affecting energy deposition.
method: The authors derive a modified stopping power formula accounting for hydrodynamic motion and perform numerical simulations.
result: Hydrodynamic motion reduces the stopping power and shifts the Bragg peak, altering alpha particle energy deposition profiles.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic effects must be considered for accurate alpha heating modeling in ICF ignition conditions.

title: Micelle Enrichment In Liquid Foams
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo Chiappisi

Using small-angle neutron scattering with contrast matching, combined with optical and electrical probes, this study focuses on the quantitative measurements of surfactant concentration profiles in foam. Enrichment is observed, with broad implications for foam stability, transport phenomena, and applications.

#SoftMatterSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L063401] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies surfactant concentration profiles in liquid foams using neutron scattering, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding surfactant distribution in foams is important for foam stability and applications, but the topic is classical soft matter physics.
method: Small-angle neutron scattering with contrast matching, combined with optical and electrical probes, was used to measure surfactant concentration profiles.
result: Enrichment of surfactant concentration was observed in the foam.
conclusion: The findings have implications for foam stability and transport phenomena, but are unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Collective Dynamics Of Natural Killer Cells Interacting With Cancer And Fibroblast Cells
authors: Yun-Xuan Zhang, Shu-Chen Liu, And Lin I
abstract:
Author(s): Yun-Xuan Zhang, Shu-Chen Liu, and Lin I

The authors tested the response of natural killer cells cocultured with cancer cells and with fibroblasts. They found that natural killer cells targeted the cancer cells, but not fibroblasts. The natural killer cells clustered around cancer cells and promoted apoptosis, whereas they scouted around fibroblasts and did not form large aggregates. Generality of these responses could be established by testing additional normal cell types and tumor lines.

#BiophysicsSpotlight #BroadlyAccessible #Interdisciplinary


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062401] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the collective dynamics of natural killer cells interacting with cancer and fibroblast cells, focusing on immune response and cell clustering.
motivation: Understanding how natural killer cells distinguish between cancer cells and normal cells is important for immunotherapy.
method: The authors cocultured natural killer cells with cancer cells and fibroblasts and observed their behavior using microscopy.
result: Natural killer cells clustered around cancer cells and induced apoptosis, but only scouted around fibroblasts without forming aggregates.
conclusion: The response is specific to cancer cells, suggesting potential for targeted immunotherapy.

title: Controlled Interference Of Laser-induced Shock Waves In Microdroplet Jetting
authors: R. A. Meijer, G. Lajoinie, B. Liu, S. Witte, And O. O. Versolato
abstract:
Author(s): R. A. Meijer, G. Lajoinie, B. Liu, S. Witte, and O. O. Versolato

We report the formation of high-velocity microjets driven by the interference of two laser-induced shock waves in a tin microdroplet. A first 0.4-ns laser pulse launches a shock wave into the droplet (diameter [MATH], 50, and [MATH]). Due to the droplet's s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023287] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies laser-induced shock waves in tin microdroplets to produce high-velocity microjets, with applications in extreme ultraviolet lithography.
motivation: To understand and control the formation of microjets from laser-driven droplets, which is relevant for industrial applications like EUV light sources.
method: Two laser pulses create interfering shock waves in a tin droplet; the dynamics are observed with time-resolved imaging.
result: The interference pattern of shock waves can be tuned to control the jet direction and velocity.
conclusion: Controlled interference of shock waves enables precise microjetting, useful for droplet-based EUV sources.

title: Circular Dichroism In The Photoelectron Angular Distribution Of Achiral Molecules
authors: Christian S. Kern, Xiaosheng Yang, Giovanni Zamborlini, Simone Mearini, Matteo Jugovac, Vitaliy Feyer, Umberto de Giovannini, Angel Rubio, Serguei Soubatch, Michael G. Ramsey, F. Stefan Tautz, And Peter Puschnig
abstract:
Author(s): Christian S. Kern, Xiaosheng Yang, Giovanni Zamborlini, Simone Mearini, Matteo Jugovac, Vitaliy Feyer, Umberto De Giovannini, Angel Rubio, Serguei Soubatch, Michael G. Ramsey, F. Stefan Tautz, and Peter Puschnig

Circular dichroism in the angular distribution (CDAD) is the effect that the angular intensity distribution of photoemitted electrons depends on the handedness of the incident circularly polarized light. The origin of CDAD can be manifold, including intrinsic properties of the system under study, su…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023275] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies circular dichroism in photoelectron angular distributions from achiral molecules, focusing on the role of molecular orientation and final-state scattering.
motivation: Understanding the origin of circular dichroism in photoemission from achiral molecules is important for interpreting experimental data and for potential applications in molecular imaging.
method: The authors combine experimental measurements of photoelectron angular distributions with theoretical simulations using multiple scattering and density functional theory.
result: They show that the observed circular dichroism arises from the interplay between molecular orientation and final-state scattering effects, not from intrinsic chirality.
conclusion: The findings clarify the mechanism of CDAD in achiral systems and provide a framework for analyzing such effects in future experiments.

title: Membrane-associated Self-assembly For Cellular Decision-making
authors: Samuel L. Foley And Margaret E. Johnson
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel L. Foley and Margaret E. Johnson

Cellular decision-making based on information received from the external environment is frequently initiated by transmembrane receptors. These receptors are known to propagate such information by triggering a series of irreversible, energy-consuming reactions. While this active mechanism ensures swi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023280] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies membrane-associated self-assembly for cellular decision-making, a topic in biophysics and systems biology.
motivation: Understanding how cells make decisions based on external signals is crucial for biology and medicine.
method: The authors use computational modeling to simulate self-assembly processes on membranes triggered by receptor activation.
result: They show that self-assembly can act as a switch for cellular decisions, with timescales and thresholds tunable by molecular parameters.
conclusion: Membrane self-assembly provides a robust mechanism for cellular decision-making without requiring active energy consumption.

title: Sea-surface Retention Effect Shapes Ocean Microplastic Fibers
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Mazzino and Giuseppe Suaria

Microfibers contaminate the global ocean, but their impact depends on length-dependent residence at the air-sea interface. In the submillimeter range, the sea surface exhibits a surface-enrichment signature: The long-to-short fiber ratio is higher at the interface than a few meters below (about 5 m)…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023283] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the length-dependent retention of microplastic fibers at the sea surface, finding that longer fibers are enriched at the air-sea interface compared to subsurface waters.
motivation: Microplastic fibers are a major pollutant in the ocean, but their vertical distribution and residence time at the sea surface are poorly understood, which affects estimates of their environmental impact.
method: The authors combine field measurements of fiber length distributions at the sea surface and at 5 m depth with a theoretical model of fiber rise velocity and turbulent mixing to explain the observed surface enrichment.
result: They find that the ratio of long to short fibers is significantly higher at the sea surface than at 5 m depth, and this can be explained by the balance between buoyant rise and turbulent diffusion.
conclusion: The sea surface acts as a selective retention layer for longer microplastic fibers, which has implications for their transport, degradation, and ingestion by marine organisms.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Dephasing Reduction In An Optically Guided Laser-plasma Accelerator
authors: Ronan Lahaye, Igor A. Andriyash, Julien Gautier, Olena Kononenko, Adrien Leblanc, Jean-Philippe Goddet, Amar Tafzi, And Cédric Thaury
abstract:
Author(s): Ronan Lahaye, Igor A. Andriyash, Julien Gautier, Olena Kononenko, Adrien Leblanc, Jean-Philippe Goddet, Amar Tafzi, and Cédric Thaury

Laser-plasma accelerators offer a compact means of producing high-energy electron beams, but their performance is fundamentally limited by dephasing between the accelerated electrons and the plasma wave. To overcome this limitation, we investigate the combination of plasma density tapering and optic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023274] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates dephasing reduction in a laser-plasma accelerator using plasma density tapering and optical guiding.
motivation: Laser-plasma accelerators are limited by dephasing between electrons and the plasma wave; the authors aim to overcome this to improve electron beam energy and quality.
method: They experimentally combine plasma density tapering with optical guiding to maintain resonance over longer distances.
result: The technique reduces dephasing, leading to higher-energy electron beams with improved stability.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical path to enhance performance of laser-plasma accelerators for compact high-energy applications.

title: Generation Of Attosecond Pulses From Relativistic Oscillating Plasma Gratings
authors: Hao-Jie Zhang, Bo-Yuan Li, Xiang-Yan An, Rong Huang, Zheng-Ming Sheng, Feng Liu, And Min Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Jie Zhang, Bo-Yuan Li, Xiang-Yan An, Rong Huang, Zheng-Ming Sheng, Feng Liu, and Min Chen

We propose a scheme to generate two isolated attosecond pulses at controllable angles through the interaction between relativistic laser pulses and a solid target. Two [MATH]-polarized laser pulses with certain frequency chirps are employed to drive oscillating plasma gratings (OPGs) on the target surf…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023261] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to generate attosecond pulses using relativistic oscillating plasma gratings driven by chirped laser pulses.
motivation: Attosecond pulse generation is important for ultrafast science, and the authors aim to produce isolated attosecond pulses at controllable angles.
method: Two chirped laser pulses interact with a solid target to create oscillating plasma gratings, which reflect the pulses to generate attosecond bursts.
result: The scheme yields two isolated attosecond pulses with controllable emission angles and durations.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a new way to generate attosecond pulses with potential applications in ultrafast spectroscopy.

title: Unified Model For Full-stage Shear Thickening Via Surface Chemistry And Friction
authors: Kang Wang, Bing Liu, Quan Liu, Huaxia Deng, And Xinglong Gong
abstract:
Author(s): Kang Wang, Bing Liu, Quan Liu, Huaxia Deng, and Xinglong Gong

Shear thickening fluid exhibits complex properties in a wide range of external conditions, leading to the significance for probing its state-transition property at the molecular level. Here, we propose a constitutive model that unifies the three rheological stages of shear thinning, shear thickening…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023263] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a constitutive model for shear thickening fluids based on surface chemistry and friction, unifying three rheological stages.
motivation: Shear thickening fluids exhibit complex state transitions under varying conditions, and understanding these at the molecular level is important for applications.
method: The authors develop a constitutive model that incorporates surface chemistry and friction effects to describe shear thinning, shear thickening, and the transition between them.
result: The model successfully unifies the three rheological stages and matches experimental data.
conclusion: The model provides a molecular-level understanding of shear thickening behavior, which could aid in designing smart materials.

title: Inhibitory Synaptic Timescales Drive Oscillatory Regime Transitions In Recurrent Excitatory-inhibitory Networks
authors: Siamak Kheiri, Saeed Taghavi, Matjaž Perc, And Alireza Valizadeh
abstract:
Author(s): Siamak Kheiri, Saeed Taghavi, Matjaž Perc, and Alireza Valizadeh

In recurrent cortical networks, inhibitory kinetics are often assumed to tune oscillation frequency continuously. Using a recurrent excitatory-inhibitory (E-I) model with fixed excitatory synaptic dynamics, we systematically vary inhibitory decay time constants and show instead that inhibitory times…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023251] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how inhibitory synaptic timescales drive transitions between oscillatory regimes in a recurrent excitatory-inhibitory network model.
motivation: Understanding how inhibitory kinetics shape network oscillations is important for cortical dynamics, but the paper focuses on neural dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a recurrent E-I network model with fixed excitatory dynamics and systematically vary inhibitory decay time constants to observe regime transitions.
result: Inhibitory timescales can cause abrupt transitions between oscillatory regimes, not just continuous frequency tuning.
conclusion: Inhibitory kinetics play a critical role in determining network oscillation patterns, with implications for neural computation.

title: Multiobjective Tweezers In Scattering Media
authors: Tristan Nerson, Jakob Hüpfl, Clément Ferise, David Globosits, Marlene Hudler, Matthieu Malléjac, Stefan Rotter, And Romain Fleury
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Nerson, Jakob Hüpfl, Clément Ferise, David Globosits, Marlene Hudler, Matthieu Malléjac, Stefan Rotter, and Romain Fleury

Radiation forces and torques enable the manipulation of objects with acoustic and electromagnetic waves. Yet, harnessing them in complex scattering media remains a formidable challenge, especially when multiple objects must be controlled under competing objectives. Here, we demonstrate that sound or…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023254] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates multi-objective manipulation of particles using acoustic tweezers in complex scattering media.
motivation: Controlling multiple objects with radiation forces in scattering environments is challenging due to competing objectives and wave interference.
method: The authors use wavefront shaping and optimization algorithms to simultaneously trap and manipulate multiple particles with acoustic waves in a scattering medium.
result: They achieve independent control of multiple particles despite strong scattering, demonstrating multiobjective tweezing.
conclusion: The approach extends optical/acoustic tweezers to complex media, enabling new applications in biophysics and microfluidics.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and applies it to flow control.
motivation: To overcome the inherent bandwidth limitation of conventional resonance for applications requiring broadband response, such as flow stabilization.
method: The authors theoretically and numerically demonstrate super-resonance in a mechanical/acoustic system, showing how a broadband out-of-phase response can be achieved beyond the typical resonant bandwidth.
result: Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling effective flow control.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new paradigm for resonant systems with potential applications in flow control and other areas requiring broadband dynamic response.

title: Erratum: Opposite Effects Of The Rotational And Translational Energy On The Rates Of Ion-Molecule Reactions Near 0 K: The ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{NH}}_{3}$ And ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{ND}}_{3}$ Reactions [Phys. Rev. X 14, 011034 (2024)]
authors: Raphaël Hahn, David Schlander, Valentina Zhelyazkova, And Frédéric Merkt
abstract:
Author(s): Raphaël Hahn, David Schlander, Valentina Zhelyazkova, and Frédéric Merkt
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 029901] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting a previous paper on low-temperature ion-molecule reaction rates, with no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The original paper studied rotational and translational energy effects on ion-molecule reactions near 0 K; the erratum corrects errors in that work.
method: The erratum likely corrects data or analysis from the original experimental or theoretical study.
result: The erratum provides corrected results for the D2+ + NH3 and D2+ + ND3 reactions.
conclusion: The corrected results refine the understanding of low-temperature ion-molecule reaction dynamics.

title: Stretching Theory Of Hookean Metashells
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Giomi

A continuum theory that describes how mechanical metamaterials deform on surfaces takes the form of the Schrödinger equation and provides a different path for materials design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021035] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: A continuum theory for mechanical metamaterials on surfaces is formulated analogously to the Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework for designing mechanical metamaterials that deform on curved surfaces.
method: The author derives a continuum theory that maps the deformation of Hookean metashells to a Schrödinger-like equation.
result: The theory provides a new mathematical description of metashell mechanics, enabling novel material design.
conclusion: The approach offers a different path for materials design by leveraging quantum mechanical analogies.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, and Hai Lei

A force-response model helps understand fatigue behavior and provides a design strategy for fatigue resistant hydrogels and soft materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021031] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is crucial for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and develop a force-response model to connect single-molecule behavior to bulk fatigue properties.
result: They identify key molecular determinants of fatigue and demonstrate how protein unfolding/refolding cycles govern macroscopic crack growth.
conclusion: The work provides a design strategy for fatigue-resistant hydrogels by engineering protein-based crosslinks with tailored mechanical stability.

title: Tracking Ultrafast Ion Diffusion Dynamics In ${\mathrm{AgCrSe}}_{2}$ Superionic Conductor
authors: Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, And Jiaqing He
abstract:
Author(s): Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, and Jiaqing He

Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion in superionic conductors provides a better link to macroscopic properties and high-performance material design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021024] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast ion diffusion dynamics in a superionic conductor using experimental techniques.
motivation: Understanding ion diffusion in superionic conductors is important for designing high-performance materials.
method: The authors use direct spatial and temporal characterization methods to track ion motion.
result: They provide detailed dynamics of ion diffusion in AgCrSe2.
conclusion: The work links microscopic ion motion to macroscopic properties, aiding material design.

title: Cell Bulging And Extrusion In A Three-Dimensional Bubbly Vertex Model For Curved Epithelial Sheets
authors: Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, And Ulrich S. Schwarz
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, and Ulrich S. Schwarz

Cells at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021023] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cell bulging and extrusion in curved epithelial sheets using a three-dimensional bubbly vertex model.
motivation: Understanding how mechanical forces at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets lead to cell extrusion is important for tissue biology and disease.
method: The authors develop a three-dimensional bubbly vertex model to simulate curved epithelial sheets and analyze cell dynamics at topological defects.
result: They find that cells at topological defects experience mechanical forces that facilitate bulging and extrusion.
conclusion: The model provides insights into the role of geometry and mechanics in cell extrusion, relevant to tissue homeostasis and morphogenesis.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga
authors: Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, And Xiang Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, Van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, and Xiang Cheng

Experimental three-dimensional measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga reveal that microscopic organisms generate unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena, expanding our understanding of microhydrodynamics with profound biological implications for microbial motility and physiology.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021019] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental 3D measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga, revealing unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena.
motivation: Understanding microhydrodynamics of swimming microorganisms is important for biology and fluid dynamics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: Experimental three-dimensional flow measurements around a free-swimming alga.
result: Discovery of unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena.
conclusion: The findings expand understanding of microhydrodynamics with biological implications.

title: Boosting The Thermoelectric Performance Of $α$-MgAgSb Through Phase-Transition-Induced Self-Doping
authors: Kaiwei Guo, Tianyu Wang, Zhen Fan, Lunhua He, Fuhong Chen, Yi Wang, Qi Zhao, Jiawei Yang, Hangtian Zhu, Jun Li, Te-Huan Liu, And Huaizhou Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiwei Guo, Tianyu Wang, Zhen Fan, Lunhua He, Fuhong Chen, Yi Wang, Qi Zhao, Jiawei Yang, Hangtian Zhu, Jun Li, Te-Huan Liu, and Huaizhou Zhao

A doping-free approach is able to boost thermoelectric performance, providing an attractive route for developing waste heat recovery technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021011] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a doping-free approach to enhance thermoelectric performance of α-MgAgSb via phase-transition-induced self-doping.
motivation: Thermoelectric materials can convert waste heat to electricity, but traditional doping methods have limitations. A doping-free route is attractive for developing efficient waste heat recovery technologies.
method: The authors induce a phase transition in α-MgAgSb to create self-doping, and characterize the resulting thermoelectric properties.
result: The phase-transition-induced self-doping significantly boosts the thermoelectric performance of α-MgAgSb.
conclusion: This doping-free approach offers a promising strategy for enhancing thermoelectric materials without conventional doping.

title: Nearly Isotropic Upper Critical Field In Pressurized Trilayer Nickelate ${\mathrm{La}}_{4}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{10−δ}$
abstract:
Author(s): Di Peng et al.

Angle-dependent magnetotransport measurements under extreme pressure reveal an isotropic upper critical field in trilayer nickelates driven by the compensation of distinct electronic orbitals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021008] Published Wed Apr 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nearly isotropic upper critical field in pressurized trilayer nickelate superconductor La4Ni3O10−δ.
motivation: Understanding the superconducting properties of nickelates under pressure, particularly the anisotropy of the upper critical field, is important for elucidating the pairing mechanism.
method: Angle-dependent magnetotransport measurements were performed under extreme pressure to determine the upper critical field anisotropy.
result: The upper critical field is nearly isotropic, attributed to compensation of distinct electronic orbitals.
conclusion: The isotropic behavior suggests a unique superconducting state in trilayer nickelates, distinct from cuprates.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental progress in hadron production from open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Understanding hadron production and searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating QCD and exploring quark confinement and gluon binding.
method: The paper reviews experimental results from BABAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII on e+e- collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs.
result: BESIII has emerged as the leading facility for high-precision measurements in this area, with recent advances highlighted.
conclusion: The study of open-charm meson pairs provides key insights into strong interaction dynamics and hadron spectroscopy.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:
Author(s): Véronique Van Elewyck and Dietrich Belitz

Three Colloquia honor the Arecibo Observatory’s legacy, exploring its revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 010001] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its impact on planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
motivation: To honor the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its contributions to various scientific fields.
method: The editorial compiles three colloquia that review the observatory's achievements.
result: The paper highlights Arecibo's revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has left a lasting legacy in multiple areas of science.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the scientific legacy of planetary radar observations at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: To document the contributions of the Arecibo planetary radar system to planetary science and its role in supporting in situ exploration.
method: The paper presents a historical overview of radar techniques and summarizes key observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo radar provided unique subsurface and surface data that advanced understanding of planetary bodies and asteroid characterization.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system was a uniquely powerful tool for planetary radar, and its loss leaves a gap in observational capabilities.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its scientific impact over five decades.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific results from Arecibo's upgrades and observations.
result: Highlights Arecibo's major contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo was a transformative instrument in radio astronomy, and its loss is significant for the field.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews advances in geospace science made using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: To summarize the scientific contributions of the Arecibo Observatory in upper atmospheric and ionospheric research over its 50-year operation.
method: Review of incoherent scatter radar technique and results from Arecibo's radar, lidar, optical, and satellite instruments.
result: Key advances in plasma physics, space weather, metal atom layers, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling are highlighted.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory provided unique capabilities for geospace research, and its legacy continues to inform current studies.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger connections.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, and their detection could reveal physics of dense matter.
method: The paper surveys detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and discusses simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It outlines the potential for multimessenger observations to inform nuclear astrophysics and condensed matter physics.
conclusion: Multimessenger astronomy with continuous gravitational waves will enhance understanding of neutron star interiors and fundamental physics.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: The rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is poorly understood, and controlled laboratory experiments are needed.
method: The paper synthesizes experiments, theory, and computational models of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce turbulent fluctuations and supersaturation.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can capture key cloud processes and help bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: These chambers offer a promising approach to resolving the long-standing bottleneck in cloud physics.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection in multimessenger astronomy.
motivation: Core collapse supernovae are rare events that provide unique insights into stellar physics and neutron star formation; detecting gravitational waves alongside photons and neutrinos would enable multimessenger studies.
method: The paper summarizes recent progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods and parameter estimation for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: It presents the latest predictions for gravitational wave signatures from neutrino-driven core collapse supernovae and outlines strategies for multimessenger observation.
conclusion: A Galactic supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, and current detectors are poised to extract physical parameters from the gravitational wave signal.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the universe, and their properties provide crucial information about matter under extreme compression.
method: The review summarizes recent measurements from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile observations, comparing them to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: The measurements constrain neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, and are compared to theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of the dense matter equation of state.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a tension between the dipole in the cosmic microwave background and that in large-scale structure, challenging the cosmological principle.
motivation: To test the foundational cosmological principle of isotropy and homogeneity by comparing the dipole in galaxy/quasar catalogs with the CMB dipole.
method: Analysis of large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole in matter distribution and compare it with the CMB dipole, including assessment of biases and systematics.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole, which cannot be explained by the standard ΛCDM model.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require new physics beyond ΛCDM.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their effects on galaxy and large-scale structure formation.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and test self-interacting dark matter scenarios using astrophysical observations.
method: The paper is a review summarizing theoretical models of self-interacting dark matter and comparing them with observational data from galaxies to large-scale structures.
result: It provides an overview of current constraints on dark matter self-interactions from various astrophysical probes.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable candidate, and future observations will further constrain its properties.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond-Standard-Model physics, and the HL-LHC offers new discovery potential.
method: The paper surveys current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and projects discovery potential across multiple search channels.
result: Stringent bounds have been placed on supersymmetric parameter space, narrowing viable models.
conclusion: The HL-LHC may discover or further constrain supersymmetry, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions, plasma physics, and diagnostics like neutrinos and helioseismology.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar properties and testing solar models.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models and experimental data from the last decade on nuclear reaction rates, plasma effects, and solar diagnostics.
result: It summarizes advances in nuclear reaction cross sections, plasma screening, and improved solar neutrino and helioseismic measurements.
conclusion: The updated understanding of hydrogen burning improves solar models and resolves some discrepancies with observations.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This review covers the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, focusing on turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding bubble dynamics is important for natural and industrial two-phase flow systems.
method: The paper reviews recent advances in experimental and theoretical studies of bubble motion, including effects of deformability, surfactants, and rheology.
result: Key advances over the past 20 years are summarized, highlighting the influence of turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes on bubble behavior.
conclusion: The review provides insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in active matter systems, focusing on collective motion and applications in biology and robotics.
motivation: To understand how self-alignment (alignment of orientation with velocity) leads to novel collective behaviors in active matter.
method: Unified mathematical framework and review of existing models of self-alignment in active systems.
result: Self-alignment enables phenomena like orbiting in traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key mechanism for designing smart materials and understanding biological motion.
