title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of gravitational wave signals from the early universe, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: To explore how gravitational waves can probe the first second after the Big Bang, which is opaque to electromagnetic radiation.
method: Review of theoretical models for gravitational wave production from cosmological phase transitions, topological defects, and other early-universe sources, along with detection strategies.
result: Summarizes possible gravitational wave signatures and outlines detection methods for stochastic backgrounds.
conclusion: Gravitational waves offer a unique window into the early universe, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Atomic-scale 3d Insights Into Heteroepitaxial Mechanisms In Hcp/fcc, Bcc/fcc, And Fcc/fcc Core–shell Nanoparticles
authors: Xilong Mu, Yao Zhang, Kang’an Wang, Haoyi Tang, Zhiheng Xie, Zezhou Li, Xuemin Cao, Peng He And Jihan Zhou
abstract: Heteroepitaxy on nanocrystals of diverse crystal structures—hexagonal close-packed (hcp), body-centered cubic (bcc), and face-centered cubic (fcc)—is a powerful approach for engineering atomic arrangements. However, the mechanisms by which interfacial defects and strain relaxation accommodate structural mismatch remain poorly understood at the three-dimensional (3D) atomic scale. Here, we use atomic-resolution electron tomography to determine the 3D atomic structures and reveal heteroepitaxial mechanisms in Pt-based core–shell nanoparticles with diverse crystal structures including hcp/fcc Ru@Pt, bcc/fcc PdCu@Pt, and fcc/fcc Ru@Pt. We have identified distinct heteroepitaxial modes in these model systems, each mitigating the structural mismatch within a single particle: mixed coherent/semi-coherent growth in hcp/fcc Ru@Pt, coherent growth with strain sharing between core and shell in bcc/fcc PdCu@Pt, and oriented growth combined with twin proliferation in decahedral fcc/fcc Ru@Pt. The various semi-coherent growth modes in the hcp/fcc nanoparticle yield a 3D dislocation network at a scale below 10 nm, interconnected by Lomer–Cottrell, Hirth, and Shockley dislocations. The key heteroepitaxial mechanisms in these examined systems are quantitatively validated by interfacial energies derived from molecular statics simulations. We anticipate these insights will inform the targeted design of interfacial structures and enable precise strain engineering in core–shell nanomaterials.
tldr: This paper uses atomic-resolution electron tomography to study heteroepitaxial mechanisms in core-shell nanoparticles with different crystal structures.
motivation: Understanding how interfacial defects and strain relaxation accommodate structural mismatch in heteroepitaxial nanoparticles is crucial for engineering atomic arrangements.
method: Atomic-resolution electron tomography was used to determine 3D atomic structures of Pt-based core-shell nanoparticles (hcp/fcc Ru@Pt, bcc/fcc PdCu@Pt, fcc/fcc Ru@Pt), combined with molecular statics simulations.
result: Distinct heteroepitaxial modes were identified: mixed coherent/semi-coherent growth, coherent growth with strain sharing, and oriented growth with twin proliferation; a 3D dislocation network below 10 nm was observed.
conclusion: The insights into heteroepitaxial mechanisms can inform targeted design of interfacial structures and strain engineering in core-shell nanomaterials.

abstract:

SignificanceMale reproduction can impose substantial costs, but how these costs depend on nutrient context remains unclear. Using male fruit flies on chemically defined diets, we show that removing dietary sterols shortens lifespan in mating males, ...
tldr: This paper studies the lifespan cost of sterol depletion in male fruit flies, focusing on mating-dependent effects.
motivation: To understand how nutrient context, specifically sterol availability, affects the cost of reproduction in males.
method: Using chemically defined diets, the authors manipulated sterol levels and measured lifespan and reproductive activity in male Drosophila melanogaster.
result: Removing dietary sterols shortened lifespan in mating males but not in non-mating males, indicating a mating-dependent cost.
conclusion: Sterol depletion imposes a lifespan cost specifically in mating males, highlighting the importance of nutrient context in reproductive costs.

motivation: GLP-1 receptor agonists cause weight loss but also loss of lean muscle mass, which is undesirable. The authors aim to find a way to preserve muscle mass and strength during such treatment.

conclusion: Targeting 15-pgdh may be a therapeutic strategy to mitigate muscle loss associated with GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy.

tldr: This paper studies the role of the cytoplasmic region of beta-dystroglycan in neuromuscular junction maturation and muscle function in mice.
motivation: Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying neuromuscular junction formation and maintenance is crucial for developing therapies for muscular dystrophies.
method: The authors generated transgenic mice lacking the cytoplasmic domain of beta-dystroglycan and analyzed neuromuscular junction structure and function using histological, electrophysiological, and behavioral assays.

tldr: This paper studies how general anesthetics interact with proteins, revealing functional group-specific biases in binding, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: General anesthetics are promiscuous but structurally specific; understanding their binding biases is important for drug design and safety.
method: The authors performed interactome-wide docking simulations to assess binding affinities of various anesthetics across many proteins.
result: They identified functional group-specific biases that influence anesthetic-protein interactions.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need to account for these biases when using anesthetics as probes in biological studies.

tldr: This paper studies how extended DNA sequence context influences mutation bias in E. coli, a topic in evolutionary biology and genomics.
motivation: Understanding where mutations occur in genomes is crucial for predicting evolution, but most studies only consider short sequence contexts.

method: The authors use bacterial genetics, cell biology assays, and mouse infection models to show that host-derived methylglyoxal triggers the PrfA virulence regulon in Listeria.

conclusion: Host methylglyoxal is a key signal that Listeria exploits to switch to its virulent intracellular lifestyle, highlighting a host-pathogen metabolic interface.
